text:
Author: Oleksandr Rud @sssvetomir New Psychology DREVO considers a person as an integral living system in which the body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, values, relationships and environment are inextricably linked. New Psychology as a Unified Living System Psychology of the future is the science of human harmony. Foundations of the New Psychology Psychology of the Future The Soul from the Point of View of New Psychology The Spirit from the Point of View of New Psychology Psyche Consciousness Psyche and consciousness Subconscious and superconscious Body Seven levels of man Values ​​and meaning Social connections Environment Interaction with nature and the environment From the psychology of survival to the psychology of creation MANIFESTO OF THE NEW PSYCHOLOGY The principle of psychological ecology New Psychology DREVO Definition of a healthy person Practical methods of personal development Practices of New Psychology DREVO What is love? Revealing the Soul The purpose of man Strengthening the spirit Causes of psychological problems Laws of personality development From the psychology of survival to the psychology of creation Preamble Humanity is entering a new era. We're creating artificial intelligence, editing genomes, exploring space, and building a digital civilization. However, the central question remains: Who is a man? Modern psychology has helped us gain a deeper understanding of the brain, emotions, and behavior. But a person is more than just neurons, hormones, and cognitive processes. They are a living, multidimensional system in which the body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, values, relationships, and the surrounding world continuously interact and influence one another. This book offers a new perspective on human nature. New Psychology DREVO Views personality not as a collection of individual functions or a set of psychological problems, but as a holistic system with enormous potential for development. Its goal is not only to help people cope with fear, anxiety, and internal conflicts, but also to show the path to maturity, freedom, creativity, and a meaningful life. This book is based on a simple idea: Man comes into the world not only to survive, but also to grow, love, collaborate, create and leave behind a legacy. The ideas presented here integrate the achievements of modern science, philosophy, psychology, biology, pedagogy, and the centuries-old wisdom of humanity. Where scientific data exists, the book draws on it. Where the subject is soul, spirit, the meaning of life, and inner experience, it offers a philosophical model open to further exploration and development. The symbol of this system is a tree. A tree doesn't become strong overnight. It gradually strengthens its roots, forms a trunk, opens its crown, and bears fruit. A person develops in the same way. Their inner strength is born not from self-conquest, but from the harmonious development of all aspects of their personality. This book is an invitation to explore your own nature. Not to find ready-made answers to all questions, but to learn to ask the right questions, to better understand yourself, to understand other people more deeply, and to consciously participate in the development of life. Human development is the development of society.
The development of society is the development of civilization.
The development of civilization begins with the development of each of us. New psychology asa single living system. In the traditional worldview of the Slavs, man was viewed not as a set of separate organs or psychological processes, but asa single living system, in which body, soul, spirit, race and nature are interconnected. Several principles can be identified. Soul— the source of feelings, conscience, love, creativity, and the inner drive to live. It was perceived as what makes a person truly alive. Spirit— will, purpose, striving upward, the ability to overcome fear and follow the chosen path. If the soul senses, the spirit guides. Body— the instrument through which the soul and spirit act in the world. Caring for the body was not an end in itself, but a condition for a full life. Humanity's relationship with the surrounding world was also of great importance. Forests, rivers, land, and the sun were perceived not simply as resources, but as part of the overall order of life. Hence the respect for nature, seasonal cycles, and labor. Interestingly, many modern branches of psychology are returning to similar ideas, albeit using different language. For example: psychosomatics studies the connection between mental states and the body; Ecopsychology studies the influence of nature on mental state; Positive psychology examines meaning, values, and the inner development of a person. It's important to distinguish between historical facts and modern interpretations. Few direct written sources remain on pre-Christian Slavic beliefs, so many details are reconstructed from folklore, archaeology, linguistics, and comparisons with other Indo-European traditions. Consequently, some modern concepts of "Slavic psychology" are more philosophical reconstructions than proven descriptions of ancient views. If we look at it more broadly, we can formulate the following idea: The psychology of the future may become not only a science of human behavior, but also a science of the harmony of the body, consciousness, personality, relationships, and what various philosophical and religious traditions call the soul. Psychology of the future is the science of human harmony. Psychology of the Futuremay become much broader than modern psychology. If today it mainly studies behavior, emotions, thinking, and brain function, then in the future it may turn intothe science of holistic human development. This concept can be represented as follows. Psychology of the future is the science of human harmony. A person is considered as a single system consisting of several interconnected levels: body - health, movement, nutrition, physiology; psyche - emotions, memory, thinking, character; consciousness - attention, awareness, ability to learn; values ​​and meaning - worldview, motivation, life goals; social connections - family, community, culture; environment - nature, city, technology. In this model, the psychologist's role changes. They become not only a specialist in treating mental health issues but also help people develop their abilities, build lasting relationships, develop their thinking, and find meaning. New directions The psychology of the future may combine the achievements of many sciences: neurobiology; cognitive science; medicine; pedagogy; sociology; artificial intelligence; human ecology. However, any claims about consciousness, the effectiveness of methods, or the impact of practices must be tested by research and not accepted without evidence. The main goal The main goal is not just getting rid of anxiety or depression, but the development of a person in all his or her full potential: physical health; emotional stability; critical thinking; ability to cooperate; creativity; a sense of responsibility to society and nature. Possible wording Future psychology is an interdisciplinary science of human development that integrates knowledge about the brain, mind, body, consciousness, social relationships, and interactions with the environment to improve quality of life and unlock human potential. This approach does not reject modern scientific methods, but rather expands them by integrating data from different fields of knowledge and maintaining the requirement to test ideas through empirical research. Foundations of the New Psychology The new psychology can view humans not as the bearer of symptoms or a set of cognitive processes, but as a holistic, evolving system. It integrates knowledge from the natural, social, and human sciences, maintaining a critical approach to hypotheses and relying on verifiable data where possible. 1. Human integrity
A person is a unity of body, psyche, consciousness, relationships with others, and the environment. Changes in one area can impact others. 2. Development instead of eliminating problems
Psychology helps not only overcome difficulties but also develop strengths: resilience, creativity, the ability to learn, collaborate, and make decisions. 3. Meaning and values
Understanding your own values ​​and life goals impacts well-being, motivation, and ability to cope with challenges. 4. Unity of reason and emotions
Emotions and thinking work together. Emotions convey information, and rational thinking helps us understand and use it. 5. The body and mind are interconnected
Sleep, nutrition, physical activity, illness, and stress all affect psychological well-being, just as mental well-being can affect physical well-being. 6. Man is a part of society and nature
Mental well-being is associated with the quality of relationships, a sense of belonging, a safe environment, and contact with nature. 7. Awareness and responsibility
A person is able to observe their thoughts, emotions and habits, gradually changing their behavior through conscious choice. 8. Scientific verifiability
Any new theory must be testable. Ideas concerning consciousness, spiritual experience, or new methods of assistance can be explored, but they should not be declared established facts without sufficient evidence. 9. Individuality
There is no one-size-fits-all developmental path. Assistance methods must take into account individual characteristics, culture, age, and life experience. 10. Continuous development
Psychological development continues throughout life. The goal is not to achieve an "ideal state," but to be able to learn, adapt, and maintain internal resilience in the face of change. Such a system can be considered as the basis of an interdisciplinary psychology that combines the achievements of modern science with philosophical questions about personality, the meaning of life, and human development, without mixing ideological ideas with established scientific knowledge.

title: Psychology of the Future
excerpt: The psychology of the future is a science not only about the psyche but also about the development of human potential. Its goal is to help people live consciously, maintain inner balance, build healthy relationships, dev
text: The psychology of the future is a science not only about the psyche but also about the development of human potential. Its goal is to help people live consciously, maintain inner balance, build healthy relationships, develop their abilities, and interact with the world around them. It can be built on the following principles. 1. Integrity A person is a single system in which the body, psyche, consciousness, values, social connections and the environment constantly influence each other. 2. Development instead of struggle The main goal is not only to reduce suffering, but also to develop personal strengths: curiosity, resilience, creativity, responsibility and the ability to collaborate. 3. Understanding instead of condemnation All behavior has a cause. Instead of making hasty judgments, psychology seeks to understand the biological, psychological, and social factors that led a person to their choices. 4. Individual approach Each person has a unique combination of abilities, life experiences, temperament, and values. There are no universal solutions. 5. Mindfulness Development begins with the ability to notice your thoughts, emotions, habits and reactions, and then consciously choose a course of action. 6. Scientificity New ideas must be tested by research. Future psychology is open to new hypotheses, but does not accept them as fact without sufficient evidence. 7. Interdisciplinarity It combines knowledge from psychology, neuroscience, medicine, pedagogy, sociology, ecology, computer science, and artificial intelligence to better understand people. 8. The relationship between man and society Personality develops within family, culture, and society. Caring for psychological well-being includes creating healthy communities, education, and conditions for collaboration. 9. Ethics Technology, artificial intelligence and psychological methods must be used with respect for human freedom, dignity and the right to make independent decisions. 10. Continuous development Psychological development doesn't end at a certain age. People are capable of learning, rethinking experiences, and changing their lives throughout their lives. Vision Future psychology is an interdisciplinary science that helps us understand ourselves, develop our abilities, enhance our well-being, and build harmonious relationships with others and the world around us. The Soul from the Point of View of New Psychology New psychology can consider the soul not as an object of faith or only a religious concept, but asworking model of the inner core of personality- that which gives a person a sense of his own uniqueness, integrity and direction in life. In this concept, the soul is not an organ or a region of the brain. It is a concept that describes the deepest level of human experience. The soul manifests itself through: conscience; love and compassion; striving for truth; sense of beauty; creativity; inner meaning of life; ability to make free choices; a sense of authentic self. The psyche answers the question"How does a person think, feel and act?" The soul answers the question"What does a person live for and what does he strive to become?" If the psyche can adapt to the environment, then the soul helps a person not to lose himself even under strong external pressure. Health of the soul The state of the soul can be understood not mystically, but through observable manifestations: internal integrity; consistency between beliefs and actions; the ability to love and trust; presence of meaning; a sense of connection with other people and the world; the ability to create something new. Diseases of the soul In a philosophical sense, one can speak not so much of “diseases of the soul” as of its alienation: loss of meaning; internal schism; living contrary to one's own values; chronic feeling of emptiness; loss of the ability to empathize and experience joy. It is important to distinguish such philosophical descriptions from clinical diagnoses, which belong to the field of psychiatry and psychology. The main task of the new psychology If traditional psychology often answers the question: "How to reduce suffering?" then the psychology of the future can add a second question: "How can we help a person discover their inner core and live their life in harmony with it?" Possible definition The soul is a philosophical concept that denotes the deepest core of personality, which encompasses values, the pursuit of meaning, the capacity for love, creativity, and free choice. The new psychology can explore how this inner core manifests itself in human behavior, relationships, and well-being, using both humanistic approaches and empirical methods where applicable. The Spirit from the Point of View of New Psychology Spirit isinner guiding force of personality, thanks to which a person is able to transcend their instincts, habits, and circumstances. It is the spirit that allows one to choose not what is easiest, but what one considers right or meaningful. If you use this model: Body— answers the question:"What can I do?" Psyche— he answers:"What do I feel and how do I perceive the world?" Soul— he answers:"Who am I? What is truly valuable to me?" Spirit— he answers:"Where am I going? What am I willing to act for?" Manifestations of the Spirit The spirit manifests itself in the ability to: maintain dignity in difficult circumstances; be true to your principles; overcome fear; take responsibility; to sacrifice personal gain for the sake of others or for the sake of an ideal; continue on after defeats. In this model, spirit is not emotion. A person can experience fear, fatigue, or doubt, but still act in accordance with their beliefs. Strong spirit A person with a strong spirit is characterized by: internal stability; discipline; responsibility; courage; keeping one's word; the ability to inspire others. Weakening of the spirit We can talk about a state when a person: loses meaning and direction; stops believing in the possibility of change; renounces his values ​​under pressure of circumstances; avoids responsibility. It is important to distinguish such philosophical descriptions from mental disorders: they are not medical diagnoses. The interaction of body, mind, soul and spirit These four levels can be thought of as interconnected elements: Bodygives the opportunity to act. Psycheperceives, feels and analyzes. Souldefines deep values ​​and a sense of authenticity. Spiritdirects a person towards the chosen goal and helps to remain faithful to it. Psyche Psyche— is the system through which a person perceives the world, processes information, experiences emotions, remembers experiences, makes decisions, and adapts to the environment. Figuratively speaking: Body— action tool. Psyche— perception and control system. Soul— the inner core of personality, values ​​and meaning (within the framework of your philosophical model). Spirit- the power of direction, will and following the chosen path. Basic functions of the psyche The psyche is responsible for: perception; attention; memory; thinking; imagination; emotions; speech; training; decision making; adaptation to changing conditions. It is the psyche that allows a person to learn from experience and change their behavior. The main task of the psyche Its main function isensure survival and effective interaction with the environmentTherefore, the psyche constantly evaluates: safe or dangerous; useful or harmful; familiar or unknown; possible or impossible. Many automatic reactions—anxiety, alertness, habits—can be seen as adaptive mechanisms. Healthy psyche Signs of psychological well-being may include: flexibility of thinking; emotional stability; ability to learn; adequate perception of reality; self-regulation; ability to build relationships. Interaction Within your model: Bodyprovides energy and physical capabilities. Psycheanalyzes the situation and suggests options for action. Soulhelps to determine what corresponds to internal values. Spirithelps to implement the chosen direction, even when it is difficult. Consciousness Consciousness— is a person’s ability to be aware of themselves, the surrounding world, and their own internal processes, as well as to direct attention and make choices. If the psyche continuously processes information, then consciousness allows us to see this work and, to a certain extent, influence it. In this model Body— it works. Psyche— perceives, feels, remembers, analyzes. Consciousness- observes, realizes, chooses. Soul— sets deep values ​​and a sense of authenticity. Spirit- gives direction, meaning and determination to follow the chosen path. Basic functions of consciousness Consciousness allows a person to: to be aware of one's existence; notice your thoughts and emotions; manage attention; make informed choices; predict the consequences of actions; reflect on yourself and the world; learn from your own experience. Levels of consciousness As a philosophical model, several levels can be distinguished: Consciousness of perception- "I see and hear." Self-awareness— “I understand that this is happening to me.” Reflexive consciousness- “I can observe my thoughts and feelings.” Value consciousness— “I realize what I consider right and important.” Creative consciousness- "I am able to create new ideas and transform the world." Development of consciousness The development of consciousness is not just the accumulation of knowledge, but the growth of ability: notice automatic reactions; separate facts from interpretations; maintain clarity of thinking in difficult situations; make decisions in line with your values; understand other people. Possible definition Consciousness is a person's ability to be aware of themselves and the world, to direct their attention, to analyze their own mental processes, and to make informed decisions. It serves as the link between perception, values, and actions.

title: Psyche and consciousness
excerpt: Psyche The psyche is a system of perception, processing and storage of information that ensures a person’s interaction with themselves and the surrounding world. It unites all the processes by which a person senses, feel
text: Psyche The psyche is a system of perception, processing and storage of information that ensures a person’s interaction with themselves and the surrounding world. It unites all the processes by which a person senses, feels, thinks, remembers, learns and acts. The psyche constantly analyzes what is happening, compares new experiences with accumulated ones, predicts consequences and helps the body adapt to changing conditions. The main functions of the psyche: perception of the surrounding world; information processing; formation of emotions; memory; thinking; imagination; speech; training; adaptation; personality formation. The psyche constantly interacts with the body, subconscious, consciousness and social environment. Its main task is to ensure effective interaction between a person and life. The psyche answers the question: "What's happening?" Consciousness Consciousness is a person’s ability to be aware of what is happening, to observe oneself, to understand one’s thoughts, feelings and actions, and to make conscious choices. If the psyche continuously processes information, then consciousness determines,which part of this information to pay attention to And how to answer it. Consciousness allows a person to go beyond automatic reactions and become the author of their own decisions. The main functions of consciousness: self-awareness; attention management; observation of thoughts and emotions; distinguishing between facts and interpretations; decision making; goal setting; introspection; development of self-control; the ability to change habitual patterns of behavior. Consciousness answers the question: "What do I choose?" Interaction of the psyche and consciousness The psyche and consciousness are not opposed to each other. The psyche continuously collects and processes a huge flow of information. Consciousness chooses what will be the subject of attention and what action will be performed. You can imagine it like this: Bodyfeels. Subconsciousreacts automatically. Psycheperceives, analyzes and suggests possible options. Consciousnessobserves, evaluates and chooses. Superconsciousnessopens up new ideas, meanings and directions. Souldetermines internal values. Spirithelps to bring the chosen path to life. Thus, the psyche creates many possible reactions, and consciousness transforms one of them into a conscious action. The psyche is responsible for processing experience. Consciousness is responsible for freedom of choice. It is precisely through the interaction of the psyche and consciousness that a person is able not only to adapt to the world, but also to consciously change himself and the surrounding reality. Subconscious and superconscious In the new psychology, the subconscious and superconscious are considered as two different levels of a person’s inner life. Subconscious The subconscious is the deepest intelligence of the body, which combines personal experience, heredity, innate programs and automatic processes of the body. It is formed not only from the memories and experiences of the person himself, but also from what is transmitted through genetics, characteristics of the nervous system, temperament, the functioning of internal organs and the general biological organization of the body. The subconscious includes: instincts and reflexes; hereditary predispositions; physical memory; emotional reactions; habits and automatisms; survival experience; reactions of the nervous, endocrine and immune systems; the influence of the state of internal organs on mood and behavior. The subconscious can be calledmind body. It continuously receives and processes a huge number of internal signals, most of which do not reach normal consciousness. The body monitors the state of its organs, energy levels, danger, stress, pain, hunger, fatigue, and environmental safety. Therefore, the subconscious acts primarily through sensations, impulses, emotions, dreams, intuitive reactions and automatic behavior. Its main task is to preserve life, maintain internal balance and use accumulated experience without the constant participation of consciousness. Superconsciousness The superconscious is the highest level of perception associated with the experience of the soul and the direction of the spirit. If the subconscious is turned to the body, the past and heredity, then the superconscious is turned to the meaning, the future, development and possibilities that have not yet manifested in a person’s ordinary life. The superconscious can manifest itself through: deep intuition; inspiration; creative insights; inner knowledge; moral sense; a sense of purpose; premonitions; unusual sensitivity; perception of symbols and images; experiencing a connection with the world, nature, or a higher order. Within the framework of the new psychology, the superconscious can be understood asmind of soul and spirit. It doesn't so much analyze what is already known as it helps a person see a new direction, feel the meaning and go beyond the usual patterns of thinking. The supposedly supersensitive, or extrasensory, aspect of perception can also be attributed to the superconscious. However, such abilities should be considered an area for research, observation, and verification, rather than automatically accepting any unusual sensation as objective knowledge. Difference The subconscious stores and processes the body's experience. The superconscious reveals the experience of the soul and the direction of the spirit. The subconscious is associated primarily with the past: heredity, survival, habits and accumulated memory. The superconscious is associated primarily with the future: development, creativity, purpose and new opportunities. The subconscious speaks through sensations, fears, desires, tension and automatic reactions. The superconscious speaks through inspiration, inner clarity, symbols, insights and a sense of right direction. The role of consciousness Consciousness is between the subconscious and the superconscious. It receives signals from below - from the body, emotions, instincts and hereditary programs - and signals from above - from meaning, conscience, intuition, soul and spirit. The task of consciousness is not to suppress one of these levels, but to distinguish them and make an informed decision. A person becomes more whole when: hears the body, but does not become a slave to instincts; respects the experience of ancestors, but does not automatically repeat their mistakes; accepts intuition, but tests it with reality; feels the direction of the soul, but embodies it with responsible actions. Thus, in the new psychology: The subconscious is the accumulated wisdom and memory of the body. Consciousness is a space of observation, discrimination and choice. The superconscious is the highest level of knowledge, creativity and direction, connected with the soul and spirit. Human harmony arises when the body, subconscious, consciousness and superconscious do not oppose each other, but act as a single system. Interaction Imagine a person as a tree. Roots- subconscious. They store all past experience and feed the system. Trunk - consciousness. It connects the past with the present and makes decisions. Crown- superconsciousness. She is drawn to new things, creates ideas and discovers unknown possibilities. Full model Then human psychology may look like this: Body— it works. Psyche— perceives and processes information. Subconscious- stores experience and automates behavior. Consciousness— realizes and chooses. Superconsciousness— creates something new and helps to go beyond the usual. Soul(in a philosophical sense) - sets deep values ​​and a sense of authenticity. Spirit(in a philosophical sense) - guides a person towards chosen ideals and helps to remain faithful to them. The main idea of ​​the new psychology In this model, human development is not a struggle between the conscious and subconscious, but rather their coordinated work. Past experience supports the individual, consciousness makes conscious choices in the present, and creativity and the search for new solutions enable progress. At the same time, philosophical concepts of soul and spirit help describe questions of meaning and values, while observable processes of the psyche, memory, attention, and creativity remain the subject of scientific research. Body The body is the material basis of a person and the first level of conscious life. It is not a passive shell. The body is a complex, self-regulating living system that continuously perceives the surrounding world, processes information, and maintains life. In the new psychology, the body is seen as the bearer of its own biological wisdom. It has: ability to self-heal; innate development programs; adaptation mechanisms; memory of past experiences; a system of internal communication between organs, the nervous, immune and endocrine systems. The body constantly collects information from both the external and internal environment. It perceives: temperature; pressure; chemical composition of blood; hormone levels; position in space; condition of muscles and joints; pain; famine; thirst; fatigue; safety or danger. Most of these processes occur without the participation of consciousness. Therefore, the body can be considered as an independent system of perception and regulation. It is the body that creates the basis for the work of the subconscious mind. When the body is depleted, overloaded, or chronically inflamed, it impacts emotions, thinking, behavior, and decision-making. Taking care of your body is not only about physical health, but also the foundation of psychological well-being. In the new psychology, the body is seen not as a “machine,” but as a living partner of consciousness. Through breathing, movement, nutrition, sleep, touch and interaction with the environment, a person maintains a connection with his own nature. The main task of the body is to preserve life, maintain internal balance and create conditions for personal development. The body is the foundation of a person. Without a strong foundation, it is impossible to fully realize the potential of the subconscious, conscious, superconscious, soul, and spirit.

title: Seven levels of man
excerpt: 1. Body The material basis of man. Its task is to live, move, recover, and interact with the surrounding world. 2. Subconscious The subconscious is the collective experience of the body. It includes: genetic programs; in
text: 1. Body The material basis of man. Its task is to live, move, recover, and interact with the surrounding world. 2. Subconscious The subconscious is the collective experience of the body. It includes: genetic programs; innate reflexes; instincts; immune memory; epigenetic influences; automatic reactions of the body; habits; experience accumulated by the person himself. In your model, this could also include the hypothesis that the body has its own distributed information processing: not only the brain, but also the nervous system, gut, heart, immune, and endocrine systems participate in regulating a person's behavior and well-being. This is partially consistent with modern research on the gut-brain axis, but the idea of ​​a complete "body intelligence" requires further testing. You can say: The subconscious is the mind of the body. 3. Consciousness Consciousness is the observer and the controller. It connects the body, psyche and higher levels of personality. This is where the choice comes in. 4. Psyche The psyche is the operating system of the personality. It unites: emotions; memory; thinking; imagination; attention; language; ability to learn. If the subconscious stores programs, then the psyche constantly uses and changes them. 5. Superconsciousness This is where the philosophical part of the model begins. In your concept: Superconsciousness is the experience and knowledge of the soul and spirit that has not yet become part of ordinary consciousness. It manifests itself as: inspiration; intuition; creative insights; sense of meaning; moral sense; deep insights. If we're talking about extrasensory perception, that's a separate hypothesis. To date, science has no generally accepted evidence for the existence of extrasensory abilities. Therefore, if we include them in the concept of new psychology, it would be more accurate to refer to them asarea for research, and not as an established fact. You can say: The superconscious is a source of new knowledge that goes beyond the accumulated experience of the individual. 6. Soul The soul answers the question: Who am I? She stores: personal individuality; values; the ability to love; sense of beauty; conscience; internal authenticity. 7. Spirit The Spirit answers the question: Where am I going? It defines: purpose; direction of development; will; the ability to overcome oneself; connection with ideals. The main idea Cha person is considered asmulti-level system: the body carries biological memory; the subconscious automatically controls the life of the organism; the psyche processes experience; consciousness makes a choice; the superconscious opens up new possibilities; the soul defines the inner essence; the spirit sets the direction of development. Social connections Humans are social beings. Their personalities are formed, developed, and revealed through relationships with others. Social connections are a space in which a person learns love, trust, cooperation, responsibility and mutual assistance. In the new psychology, relationships are viewed not only as a means of communication, but also as a vital factor in psychological development. The main levels of social connections are: family; genus; Friends; communities; team; society; humanity. Each level influences the formation of personality, values, worldview and behavior. Through communication, a person gains knowledge, experience, support and the opportunity to see himself through the eyes of other people. Healthy social connections are based on: respect; trust; honesty; mutual responsibility; cooperation; freedom of the individual; justice; mutual support. The breakdown of social connections leads to loneliness, mistrust, alienation and weakening of psychological resilience. Therefore, one of the tasks of the new psychology is to develop a culture of communication, the ability to resolve conflicts, cooperate, and create communities in which people can reveal their abilities. Participating in a creative community is especially important. When people unite around shared values ​​and goals, a collective potential emerges that far exceeds the capabilities of any individual. Social connections also serve as a space for the transmission of knowledge, traditions, culture, and experience between generations. Through this, individuals become part of the continuous history of their family, their people, and all of humanity. Social connections answer the question: "Who am I walking through life with?" They connect personal development with the well-being of others and remind us that personal development and social development are inseparable. A person reveals himself most fully when he not only receives support from society, but also becomes a source of support, knowledge, creativity and creation for others. Environment The environment is the space of human life, including nature, human-made infrastructure and technology. In the new psychology, the environment is viewed not as a background, but as an active factor influencing physical condition, psyche, behavior, relationships and quality of life. Humans constantly interact with the world around them. This interaction occurs on three levels. Nature Nature is the natural environment for human existence. Light, air, water, soil, plants, animals, the changing seasons and natural rhythms influence health, emotional state, attention and the ability to recover. Contact with nature helps reduce stress, restore internal resources and feel connected to life. Caring for nature simultaneously becomes caring for people. City The city is an artificial environment created by society. Architecture, transportation, noise levels, safety, the availability of green spaces, public spaces, and cultural life influence psychological well-being, the quality of communication, and lifestyle. The city can both support human development and create chronic tension, a feeling of isolation and overload. Therefore, one of the goals of the new psychology is to create an environment in which it is easier for a person to live, communicate, learn, create, and recuperate. Technologies Technology is an extension of human capabilities. They enhance a person's ability to communicate, learn, create, and solve complex problems. However, technology can not only help, but also distract, increase information overload, addiction, and social isolation. New psychology views technology as a tool that should serve human development rather than control attention, values, and lifestyle. Artificial intelligence occupies a special place. It can become an assistant in education, creativity, medicine, psychological support and scientific research if its use is based on the principles of ethics, transparency and respect for human freedom. Unity of man and environment The environment answers the question: “What kind of world do I live in and what kind of world do I create around myself?” Man is simultaneously a part of the environment and its creator. By changing the world around him, he changes himself. Conversely, by developing oneself, a person is able to create a healthier, more beautiful, safer and harmonious environment for others. The primary goal of the new psychology is to help people learn to live in harmony with nature, use technology wisely, and collaborate to create a society that fosters personal development and the well-being of future generations. Interaction with nature and the environment Humans do not exist separately from the surrounding world. They are part of a unified natural system and constantly exchange matter, energy, and information with it. In the new psychology, the environment is viewed not only as a place where a person lives, but also as an active participant in his development. Every breath, every sip of water, every ray of light and every contact with living nature become part of a person’s inner life. Nature Nature is the primary environment for human existence. It has shaped man for millions of years and continues to influence his body, psyche and lifestyle. Forests, mountains, rivers, sea, plants, animals, soil, sunlight, the change of day and night, the seasons - all this creates a natural environment to which humans are evolutionarily adapted. Regular interaction with nature promotes: physical recovery; emotional balance; stress reduction; development of observation skills; creative thinking; a feeling of unity with life. Artificial environment Cities, buildings, roads, industry and digital infrastructure are the result of human activity. The built environment can enhance quality of life, but if poorly designed, it can create noise, pollution, information overload, and feelings of alienation. The human task is to create a space that supports health, cooperation, creativity and inner balance. Technological environment Modern technologies significantly expand human capabilities. They help us learn, communicate, create new knowledge, and solve complex problems. However, technology must remain a tool for humans. When a person begins to submit to technology, he or she loses the ability to concentrate, communicate, and make independent decisions, and their inner balance is disrupted. Therefore, new psychology views the development of digital culture as an important part of psychological health. Interaction A person constantly influences the world around him. Every thought becomes an action. Every action changes the environment. The changed environment again affects the person. Thus, a continuous cycle of mutual development arises. Environmental awareness New psychology views caring for nature not only as an ecological task, but also as a manifestation of psychological maturity. A person who treats the earth, water, air, plants, animals and other people with care simultaneously strengthens his own inner state and creates conditions for the well-being of future generations. The main principle Man is not the master of nature and is not separated from it. It is part of a single living system. Human health cannot be completely separated from the health of the family, society and the environment. Personal development becomes complete when a person learns to live in harmony with himself, with other people and with the world of which he is a part. Interaction with the environment answers the question: "How do I influence the world, and how does the world influence me?" It is in this continuous interaction that a responsible attitude towards life, nature, society and the future is born.

title: From the psychology of survival to the psychology of creation
excerpt: Throughout most of its history, man has been learning to survive. The struggle for food, safety, and protection of family and clan shaped many of our psychological mechanisms. Fear, anxiety, aggression, vigilance, and th
text: Throughout most of its history, man has been learning to survive. The struggle for food, safety, and protection of family and clan shaped many of our psychological mechanisms. Fear, anxiety, aggression, vigilance, and the desire to control the surrounding world helped us maintain life in the face of constant danger. Modern psychology pays close attention to these mechanisms. It studies trauma, stress, anxiety disorders, depression, addictions, and other conditions that reduce quality of life. This approach is of great value because it helps people restore inner balance and overcome suffering. However, recovery is not yet development. A person who has freed himself from fear does not necessarily become a creator. A person who has overcome depression does not necessarily find the meaning of life. A person who has learned to cope with stress does not necessarily begin to create something valuable for the world. Therefore, New Psychology DREVO suggests taking the next step. Its task is not only to help a person survive, but also to help him learn to live a full life. The psychology of creation begins where the struggle for simple survival ends. She asks new questions. Not only: "How to get rid of suffering?" but also: "How to reveal your abilities?" "How to learn to love?" "How to create?" "How can I leave the world better than I found it?" In the psychology of survival, protection becomes the most important thing. In the psychology of creation, development becomes the main thing. Survival psychology teaches us to avoid danger. The psychology of creation teaches us to create opportunities. Survival psychology seeks to preserve life. The psychology of creation seeks to reveal its potential. This doesn't mean abandoning the understanding of trauma, pain, or illness. On the contrary, helping someone overcome suffering remains a necessary step. But it is seen as the beginning of the journey, not its final destination. The new psychology of DREVO considers man as a creative being. The highest manifestation of maturity is not the ability to defend oneself, but the ability to create. Create knowledge. Create culture. Create families. Create communities. Create technologies. To create beauty. Create conditions in which other people and future generations can develop. True development begins when a person stops living only by the question of his own survival and begins to recognize himself as a participant in the development of life. The main goal of the New Psychology DREVO is to help people move from survival to creation, from reaction to conscious choice, from fear to responsibility, from consumption to creativity, from the struggle for life to participation in its development. The psychology of the future is not only the science of how to reduce suffering. This is the science of how to develop a person so that he becomes a source of development for himself, society, nature and future generations. MANIFESTO OF THE NEW PSYCHOLOGY Science of the Whole Man Humanity is entering an era when old ideas about man are no longer sufficient. Modern psychology has made great strides in studying behavior, emotions, memory, thinking, and brain function. However, humans are far more complex than a set of neural processes or behavioral patterns. New psychology proposes to view a person as a holistic living system in which the body, psyche, consciousness, values, relationships, environment, and internal search for meaning are interconnected. We recognize the achievements of modern science and consider them the foundation for further development. At the same time, we are open to exploring questions that have not yet received definitive answers: the nature of consciousness, subjective experience, creativity, intuition, the meaning of life, and other profound aspects of human existence. Basic principles We argue that a person is an integral system that includes several interconnected levels. Body— the foundation of life, possessing its own biological wisdom and the ability to self-regulate. Subconscious— a deep system of automatic processes, experiential memory, hereditary programs and bodily adaptation. Psyche— a system of perception, thinking, emotions, memory, learning and interaction with the surrounding world. Consciousness- the ability to observe, perceive, discern and freely choose the direction of action. Superconsciousness— a space of creativity, inspiration, deep insights, and the search for new possibilities. Its nature requires further scientific research. Soul— a philosophical concept denoting the inner core of a person, their values, sense of authenticity, and experience of meaning. Spirit— a philosophical concept denoting a person’s striving for ideals, the ability to remain faithful to one’s principles and overcome difficulties for the sake of the chosen path. Values We believe that human development is impossible without an internal moral foundation. Love. Freedom. Responsibility. Dignity. Honesty. Justice. Creativity. Cooperation. Respect for life. Creation. These values ​​do not pit people against each other, but create the basis for the joint development of the individual, society and civilization. Community A person develops through relationships. Family. Friendship. Genus. Culture. Education. Scientific cooperation. Society. Psychological health cannot be considered separately from the quality of human relationships. Nature Man is a part of nature. Its well-being cannot be separated from the state of water, air, soil, forests, animals and the entire ecosystem of the Earth. Caring for nature is also caring for people. Technologies Technologies should expand human capabilities, not replace humans. Artificial intelligence should contribute to the development of personality, education, science, and medicine, while preserving human freedom of choice, dignity, and responsibility. Scientific approach New psychology does not reject science. It expands the field of research. Anything that can be verified should be investigated by scientific methods. Anything that does not yet have sufficient evidence must remain the subject of open, honest and critical study, and not of unconditional belief or denial. The main goal The main goal of the new psychology is not only to reduce suffering. The main goal is to unlock human potential. Help a person become healthier. More free. More conscious. More responsible. More creative. More capable of love. More capable of creating a world in which future generations can live with dignity. Our vision We see a person not as a problem that needs to be fixed. We see man as a continuously evolving system, capable of knowing, creating, loving, cooperating and transforming the world. The new psychology is not a rejection of the past. This is the next stage of understanding man. A stage in which science, philosophy, culture and human experience do not oppose each other, but together help to more deeply understand the nature of the individual and its place in the world. By knowing a person, we know the world. By changing ourselves, we change the future. The principle of psychological ecology The inner world of a person is like a living ecosystem New psychology views a person as a complex living ecosystem in which the body, psyche, consciousness, subconscious, superconscious, soul, spirit, values, social connections and the environment form a single interconnected system. Just as environmental pollution disrupts the functioning of ecosystems, informational, emotional and social pollution disrupts a person’s internal balance. Psychological ecology is the science and practice of maintaining a healthy internal human environment. Basic Law Everything that a person lets into himself gradually becomes part of his inner world. This applies not only to food and air, but also to: information; words; emotions; music; images; human communication; digital environment; habits; culture; knowledge; daily thoughts. Every external signal becomes a kind of food for the psyche. Therefore, a person must take care not only of the cleanliness of his body, but also of the cleanliness of his internal environment. Psychological pollution Sources of psychological pollution can be: constant fear; hatred; aggression; lie; manipulation; information noise; chronic stress; destructive addictions; humiliation of dignity; toxic relationship. Long-term exposure to such factors can reduce psychological stability, impair quality of life, and hinder personal development. Psychological nutrition Just as the body needs healthy food, the psyche needs quality psychological nutrition. These include: Love; respect; knowledge; creativity; beauty; music; nature; friendship; honest dialogue; sense of meaning; training; physical activity; rest; silence. Psychological nutrition creates conditions for internal growth. Internal immunity The task of the new psychology is not to isolate a person from the world, but to develop his internal stability. Psychological immunity includes the ability to: critically evaluate information; recognize manipulation; maintain emotional balance; recover from difficulties; preserve your own values; build healthy relationships. The stronger the internal immunity, the less destructive the impact of an unfavorable environment. Ecological principle of development A person develops most harmoniously when his inner world is in harmony with the surrounding world. Caring for nature, the health of society and one’s own internal state are different manifestations of the same process – the preservation and development of life. Therefore, the new psychology considers ecology not only as an attitude towards nature, but also as a principle of thinking, communication, education, upbringing and culture. The main principle Everything is interconnected. Thoughts influence emotions. Emotions affect the body. The body influences the mind. Consciousness influences actions. Actions change society. Society changes the environment. The environment influences people again. Understanding this interconnection, a person ceases to perceive himself as a separate being and begins to recognize himself as part of a single system of life. Psychological ecology is the art of maintaining the purity of one's inner world while simultaneously creating a healthier world around oneself.

title: New Psychology DREVO
excerpt: Man as a living ecosystem Introduction The new psychology of DREVO is a philosophical and scientific concept that views humans as integral living systems, constantly interacting with themselves, society, nature, and the
text: Man as a living ecosystem Introduction The new psychology of DREVO is a philosophical and scientific concept that views humans as integral living systems, constantly interacting with themselves, society, nature, and the environment. Name WOODIt was not chosen by chance. A tree is one of the most perfect forms of life. It has strong roots, a powerful trunk, a developed crown, continuously exchanges matter and energy with the surrounding world, grows, regenerates, and bears fruit. A person develops according to the same laws. It is impossible to strengthen the crown if the roots are destroyed. It is impossible to have a strong trunk without healthy soil. It is impossible to obtain fruits without a long growing process. This is why the new psychology views a person as a living system, and not as a collection of individual functions. The basic principle Everything in a person is interconnected. Changes in one part of the system inevitably affect the others. Personality development occurs not through the struggle of individual parts of a person, but through their harmonious interaction. Ten levels of man 1. Body The foundation of life. A source of biological energy, health and interaction with the environment. 2. Subconscious Deep memory of the body. Automatic life programs. Instincts. Bodily memory. Hereditary traits. Biological adaptation. 3. Psyche The system of perception and processing of information. Emotions. Memory. Thinking. Imagination. Training. 4. Consciousness Space of observation and free choice. Consciousness connects all levels of a person and allows him to consciously direct his life. 5. Superconsciousness A source of creativity, inspiration, deep insights and the search for new opportunities. The superconscious is considered as an area whose nature requires further philosophical and scientific research. 6. Soul The inner core of personality. The source of love, conscience, beauty, compassion and a sense of self-authenticity. 7. Spirit Vector of human development. Will. Purpose. The ability to follow your values ​​even in difficult circumstances. 8. Values ​​and meaning Inner compass of personality. They determine not only a person’s goals, but also the ways to achieve them. 9. Social connections A person develops through relationships. Family. Community. Culture. Education. Joint creativity. 10. Interaction with nature and the environment Man is part of a single ecosystem of life. Nature, society and technology shape the conditions of its development, and man, in turn, influences them with his decisions and actions. The principle of psychological ecology The inner world of a person is like a living ecosystem. Thoughts. Emotions. Information. Relationship. Food. Music. Culture. Nature. All of them are an environment in which personality develops. Just as environmental pollution destroys forests, informational, emotional and social pollution can disrupt a person’s inner balance. Therefore, caring for psychological health begins with caring for the quality of the environment in which a person lives. The principle of growth A tree never grows by destroying its own roots. Likewise, a person cannot develop by destroying his body, psyche, relationships or environment. True development always strengthens the system as a whole. The principle of interrelation The body influences the psyche. The psyche influences consciousness. Consciousness influences actions. Actions shape character. Character influences society. Society changes the environment. The environment influences people again. Development occurs in a circle, forming a continuous cycle of life. The main goal The new psychology of DREVO is aimed not only at overcoming psychological difficulties. Its goal is to help people become more holistic, conscious, healthy, and responsible, to discover their potential, and to learn to live in harmony with themselves, other people, and the world around them. Motto Strong roots. Clear consciousness. Living soul. Creative spirit. Harmony with the world. The new psychology of DREVO views human development as a tree's growth: the deeper the roots, the higher the crown can rise. True development begins not with self-defeat, but with understanding one's nature, respect for life, and the desire to create conditions in which not only the individual but also society as a whole can grow. Definition of a healthy person A healthy person— is a person whose body, psyche, consciousness, values, relationships with people and interaction with the environment are in a state of dynamic harmony, allowing him to live fully, develop, love, create and take responsibility for his actions. Health is more than just the absence of illness. It is a person's ability to maintain inner balance, recover from difficulties, make informed decisions, and realize one's potential. In the New Psychology of DREVO, human health is manifested in several interconnected dimensions. Physical health The body has sufficient vital energy, is capable of movement, recovery and adaptation to changing conditions. Mental health The psyche flexibly perceives reality, regulates emotions, learns from experience, and helps a person effectively interact with the surrounding world. Mindfulness Consciousness allows a person to understand themselves, distinguish between automatic reactions and conscious decisions, take responsibility for their own lives and maintain the ability to make free choices. Value integrity A person's actions are consistent with their deepest values. There is consistency between what they think, say, and do. Social health A person is capable of building relationships based on respect, trust, cooperation, and mutual responsibility. They know how to receive support and become its provider. Environmental health People recognize their interconnectedness with nature, society, and technology. They strive not to destroy the environment of which they are a part, but to support its sustainability and development. Ability to develop A healthy person is not "complete." They retain the ability to learn, reflect on experiences, acknowledge mistakes, change, and develop new abilities throughout their lives. The main criterion of health The main sign of health isnot the perfection of a person, but his ability to maintain and restore harmony within himself and in relationships with the outside world. A healthy person is able to: to love without losing one's own dignity; to be free without denying responsibility; maintain internal stability in conditions of uncertainty; collaborate without losing individuality; create more life than destruction; leave behind people, communities, and the environment in better condition than they found them before his involvement. In DREVO's New Psychology, health is not a final state, but a continuous process of harmonious development of individuals, society, and nature. Practical methods of personal development The TREVO principle Human development begins not with a struggle against oneself, but with strengthening all levels of one’s life. Just as a tree cannot grow only through its branches or only through its roots, so a person develops harmoniously only when the body, psyche, consciousness, values, relationships and interaction with the surrounding world develop. The new psychology of DREVO offers a practice of continuous development through ten interconnected areas. 1. Body development The basis of personal development is a healthy body. Practices: good sleep; natural nutrition; movement and exercise; breathing practices; massage and body therapy; hardening; nature walks; recovery after exercise. The main goal is to increase the body's vital resources. 2. Development of the subconscious The subconscious changes through repetition of experience. Practices: formation of healthy habits; working with automatic reactions; development of physical sensitivity; conscious breathing; keeping a diary of observations; working with emotional triggers; learning new skills to the point of automatism. The main goal is to make internal programs allies of a person. 3. Development of the psyche The psyche develops through diverse life experiences. Practices: training; reading; solving complex problems; development of emotional literacy; creative activity; development of memory and attention; learning foreign languages; music and art. The main goal is to increase flexibility of thinking and emotional stability. 4. Development of consciousness Consciousness develops through observation and conscious choice. Practices: reflection; meditation or other mindfulness practices; keeping a diary; analysis of own decisions; goal setting; development of critical thinking; regular self-education. The main goal is to increase freedom of choice. 5. Development of the superconscious The superconscious is revealed through creativity, the search for something new and deep attention to one’s own experience. Practices: creative projects; research activities; free writing; contemplation of nature; working with symbols and images; development of intuitive thinking with subsequent testing of emerging ideas; participation in scientific and philosophical discussions. The main goal is to expand the ability to see new possibilities. 6. Soul development The soul develops through the experience of human values. Practices: Gratitude; helping others; art; sincere communication; development of compassion; maintaining internal integrity; search for personal meaning. The main goal is to maintain internal integrity. 7. Development of the spirit The spirit is strengthened through action. Practices: fulfillment of given promises; discipline; voluntary overcoming of difficulties; service to society; long-term projects; development of courage and responsibility. The main goal is to connect beliefs and actions. 8. Development of values Values ​​become reality only when they are manifested in everyday life. Practices: regularly reflecting on your decisions; discussion of moral issues; participation in socially useful projects; development of a culture of communication; learning from life experience. The main goal is to align worldview and lifestyle. 9. Development of social connections Personality develops through cooperation. Practices: creating a family; friendship; participation in communities; joint creativity; teaching; teaching others; conflict resolution through dialogue. The main goal is to create relationships in which each participant develops. 10. Development of interaction with the environment A person develops along with the world that he creates around himself. Practices: contact with nature; eco-friendly lifestyle; participation in environmental restoration; intelligent use of technology; creating a beautiful and harmonious space; development of environmental culture. The main goal is to leave the world better than you found it.

title: The law of continuous development
excerpt: You cannot develop one level of personality while completely ignoring the others. A weak body limits the psyche. The unconscious psyche limits freedom of choice. Loss of values ​​destroys relationships. Broken relationsh
text: You cannot develop one level of personality while completely ignoring the others. A weak body limits the psyche. The unconscious psyche limits freedom of choice. Loss of values ​​destroys relationships. Broken relationships weaken society. A broken society degrades the environment. Therefore, development must always be holistic. The main principle of DREVO Every day, a person can do at least one thing that will strengthen their body, deepen their understanding of themselves, improve their relationships with people, or benefit the world around them. It is from such small daily actions that a mature personality gradually grows, just as a great tree grows from a small seed. New Psychology Practices DREVO The law of small steps Personality develops not through rare heroic deeds, but through small daily actions. Every day strengthens habits. Each week shapes a lifestyle. Every year changes personality. Daily practices Body good sleep; movement for at least 30-60 minutes; breathing exercises; quality nutrition; water; staying outdoors; short warm-up every hour if you have a sedentary job. Question of the day: What strengthened my body today? Subconscious observation of automatic reactions; forming one useful habit; conscious breathing during stress; An evening recording of the emotional events of the day. Question of the day: Which of my habits helped me today and which ones hindered me? Psyche reading; training; solving intellectual problems; creative activity; development of emotional literacy. Question of the day: What new things did I understand today? Consciousness 10-20 minutes of silence, meditation or focused reflection; analysis of your decisions; planning the next day. Question of the day: What decisions today were truly mine? Superconsciousness free creativity; a walk alone; recording new ideas; contemplation of nature; search for non-standard solutions. Question of the day: What new thought came to me today? Soul Gratitude; a good deed; sincere conversation; music; art; prayer or contemplation - for those who adhere to the corresponding tradition. Question of the day: What made me more alive today? Spirit keeping one's word to oneself; overcoming a minor difficulty; discipline; action for a long-term goal. Question of the day: Where did I show strength of character today? Values one action according to one's beliefs; honesty; respect for people. Question of the day: Was my life consistent with my values ​​today? Social connections help one person; listen without judgment; express gratitude; support a loved one. Question of the day: Who is better off today thanks to me? Environment order at home and at work; caring for nature; conscious use of technology; time without screen. Question of the day: What kind of world did I leave behind today? Weekly practices Every week a person conducts a "tree audit". Roots How does the body feel? Do you have the strength? What needs to be restored? Trunk What emotions were predominant? What habits have developed? What has changed? Crown What new ideas emerged? What did you manage to create? Fruit What useful things have I done for others? What has changed around me? Question of the week Have I become stronger, wiser and kinder compared to last week? Monthly practices Once a month, a deep self-assessment is carried out. health; relationship; training; creativity; finance; spiritual development; contribution to society; interaction with nature. New goals are being set for the next month. Annual practices Every year a person takes stock of his development. Not by the amount of money earned. Not by the number of things. And then, what kind of person he became. Questions of the Year What new things have I learned? What did you learn? Who did you help? What did you create? Which of my values ​​have become stronger? What fears did you manage to overcome? How has my attitude towards people changed? What was made better by my presence? Which projects will outlive me? Day of Silence Once a year, a person devotes one day to a complete re-evaluation of his life. Without a phone. No rush. In nature or in silence. He reflects: Who am I now? Where am I going? What are my true values? What needs to be changed? After this, a new annual development plan is formed. The main law of development Every day strengthens the roots. Each week forms the trunk. Creates new branches every month. Every year bears fruit. This is how a tree grows. This is how a person develops. The main goal of the New Psychology DREVO is not to become a perfect person, but to become a little more conscious, healthy, free, responsible, and capable of contributing to the world every day. What is love? Love in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, love is viewed as a natural state of a mature personality, aimed at preserving, developing and revealing life. Love is not just a feeling. Not just emotion. Not just biological attraction. Love is an attitude towards life that is expressed through care, respect, responsibility and the desire to develop another person, oneself and the world around us. What is love? Love is the desire to preserve, develop and reveal life. A person can love: another person; child; family; friends; your own business; nature; knowledge; art; Homeland; humanity. In all cases, love is manifested in the same way. It promotes development, not destruction. Love and development Love is always aimed at growth. A loving parent helps a child become independent. A loving teacher helps a student to discover his abilities. A loving doctor strives to restore health. A loving person does not seek to possess another person. He strives to help him become more free, mature and happier. That's why love doesn't hold back. Love helps you grow. Love and freedom True love is impossible without freedom. Where there is violence, constant control, or the desire to completely subjugate another to one's will, love gradually gives way to dependence or fear. Love respects another person's right to be themselves. It does not abolish responsibility and mutual obligations, but it excludes the treatment of a person as property. Love and responsibility Love is not limited to feelings. It manifests itself through actions. Care. Loyalty. Honesty. Support. The ability to be there in difficult times. Responsibility makes love sustainable. Love and respect Love begins with recognizing the worth of another person. She doesn't demand perfection. She accepts a person as an individual, recognizing his right to development, mistakes and change. Respect creates a space in which love can exist for a long time. Love and Creation Love always creates. She creates: family; trust; friendship; culture; knowledge; cooperation; safety; future. Where love disappears, it becomes more difficult for a person to create together with others. Love for oneself Loving yourself does not mean being selfish. It means respect for one's own life, health, dignity and development. A person who takes care of himself is more able to take care of others. Love for oneself and love for others are not opposed. They support each other. Love and Humanity The highest form of love becomes the desire to preserve and develop life in all its manifestations. Such love is shown through: raising children; helping people; scientific discoveries; protection of nature; development of culture; creation of a just society; service to future generations. Love becomes the driving force of creative civilization. The main principle Love cannot be measured in words. It is measured by how much more life, freedom, trust, development and creation there is after meeting a person. True love does not make a person weaker. She helps him bring out the best in him. Definition Love is a conscious desire to preserve, develop and reveal life, manifested through respect, care, responsibility, freedom and creative actions. In the New Psychology of DREVO, love is viewed as one of the highest forms of personal maturity. It unites the body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, and spirit into a single direction—the development of life. Love is the energy of creation that transforms existence into development, relationships into cooperation, and a person into a source of life for others. Note.The last phrase uses the word "energy" in a philosophical, not physical, sense. Within DREVO, love is understood as a driving force of personality, not as a measurable form of physical energy. Revealing the Soul What does it mean to open your soul? In the New Psychology of DREVO, soul revelation is the process of gradually revealing a person's inner essence through their thoughts, feelings, actions, creativity, and relationships with the world. The soul cannot be artificially created or changed. It is not acquired from without. It is revealed when a person begins to live in harmony with their inner nature. Opening up the soul is not about finding a new self, but about returning to your true self. What prevents the soul from opening up? The soul does not disappear, but its manifestation can be limited by various factors: constant fear; living contrary to one's own values; self-deception; chronic stress; dependencies; internal conflicts; destructive relationships; lack of meaning; loss of connection with nature, creativity and people. When a person lives solely under the influence of external expectations or automatic reactions, his inner potential remains untapped. Signs of soul opening The opening of the soul is manifested not by unusual experiences, but by a change in the person himself. He becomes: more sincere; more free internally; more responsible; more capable of love; more creative; more resilient in the face of difficulties; more attentive to other people; more capable of creating than destroying. A person stops constantly asking: "What will the world give me?" And more and more often he asks the question: "What value can I bring to the world?" Paths to Soul Discovery The revelation of the soul occurs through life. Through: Love; creativity; service to people; knowledge; honesty with yourself; acceptance of responsibility; overcoming difficulties; communication; contemplation of nature; creating a family and raising children; participation in the life of society; preservation of culture; work filled with meaning. Each of these paths helps a person express his values ​​in specific actions. The role of consciousness and will Consciousness helps to hear the inner voice. Will helps to bring it to life. Without consciousness, a person may not notice his true aspirations. Without will, he may never realize them. Therefore, opening the soul requires not only sensitivity, but also daily inner work. The main principle The soul is not revealed when a person strives to appear to be someone else. It is revealed when his thoughts, words and actions become one. Authenticity gives birth to inner freedom. Inner freedom gives birth to creativity. Creativity gives birth to creation. And creation becomes a natural expression of an open soul. An open soul is not a special state available to a select few. It is a way of life in which a person increasingly realizes their best qualities, lives in harmony with their values, and benefits others and the world.

title: The purpose of man
excerpt: What is purpose? In the New Psychology of DREVO, purpose is a natural direction of human development, in which one's abilities, values, and desire to contribute to life are most fully revealed. Purpose is not one predete
text: What is purpose? In the New Psychology of DREVO, purpose is a natural direction of human development, in which one's abilities, values, and desire to contribute to life are most fully revealed. Purpose is not one predetermined profession or one event that needs to be found. This is the path on which a person most fully realizes his nature, serves people and reveals his inner potential. Each person possesses a unique combination of abilities, character, life experiences, and values. It is the interaction of these that shapes their purpose. Purpose is born in life Purpose cannot be learned only from books or other people's advice. It opens gradually: through experience; through labor; through creativity; through mistakes; through overcoming difficulties; through relationships with people; through service to society. Every decision made helps a person to better understand himself. Signs of your path A person approaches his destiny when: his activities are consistent with his values; abilities find practical application; work benefits other people; development becomes a natural need; difficulties are perceived as part of growth, not as meaningless suffering; a feeling of inner integrity appears. Purpose does not exclude fatigue or doubts, but it helps to understand why a person continues on his path. Purpose and Society Purpose always goes beyond personal gain. By developing one's abilities, a person simultaneously creates value for others. The teacher imparts knowledge. The doctor helps to maintain health. An engineer creates new technologies. A farmer grows food. The artist reveals beauty to people. A parent raises a new generation. Every work becomes part of the overall development of society. Purpose and responsibility The right to follow one's destiny is inseparable from responsibility. Freedom without responsibility turns into arbitrariness. Responsibility without freedom becomes coercion. True purpose combines freedom of choice with responsibility for the consequences of one's decisions. Revealing Purpose Purpose is revealed when a person: strengthens your body; develops the psyche and consciousness; educates the will; lives in accordance with his values; builds healthy relationships; cares about the environment; constantly learning and developing; transforms knowledge into creative actions. In this integrity, inner potential becomes a real contribution to life. The main principle Purpose is not about finding your place in the world. Purpose is constant participation in the development of the world, while revealing oneself. The person doesn't just ask: "What do I live for?" He begins to respond with his life. Definition A person's purpose is a path of consciously revealing one's abilities, values, and will, aimed at creating, developing life, and benefiting other people. In the New Psychology of DREVO, purpose is understood not as an end point, but as an ongoing process. As a person develops, their knowledge, capabilities, and forms of service to the world change, but the main goal remains constant—to leave behind more life, goodness, knowledge, and creativity than existed before their arrival. Strengthening the spirit What does it mean to strengthen the spirit? In DREVO's New Psychology, spirit is an inner strength that helps a person remain true to their values, move toward their purpose, and not give up on their path in the face of difficulties. If the soul answers the question: "Who am I?" then the spirit answers: “What do I live for and what am I ready to bring to the world?” Strengthening your spirit means developing the ability to live in accordance with your convictions, even when it requires courage, patience, and self-discipline. What weakens the spirit? The spirit weakens when a person: lives contrary to his values; constantly refuses to go back on his decisions; shifts responsibility to others; afraid of change; loses the meaning of life; stops developing; allows fear to completely determine one's actions. Weakening of the spirit is not manifested in a lack of strength, but in the loss of inner direction. What strengthens the spirit? The spirit is strengthened through real actions. Every time a person consciously chooses creation over destruction, responsibility over indifference, honesty over lies, he strengthens his spirit. The main practices are: keeping one's word; keeping promises; acceptance of responsibility; voluntary overcoming of difficulties; continuous learning; service to people; caring for nature; creative work; protection of justice; development of discipline; cultivation of patience; Gratitude. The spirit grows not from words, but from actions. Will and spirit Willpower is the ability to control oneself and make conscious choices. The Spirit determines the direction of this choice. Will answers the question: "Can I do this?" The spirit answers: "Why am I doing this?" When willpower is combined with high values, inner stability appears.
