Trials Trials are not only a source of suffering, but also an opportunity for growth. Difficulties allow a person to see: how true he is to his principles; is he able to maintain dignity; is able to help others even in difficult conditions; is able to continue on after failures. The spirit is strengthened not by the absence of trials, but by how a person goes through them. Signs of a strong spirit A man with a strong spirit: maintains dignity; accepts responsibility; knows how to admit mistakes; does not lose humanity in conflict; capable of long-term work; keeps hope alive in difficult times; inspires by example, not just by words; strives to create more than to destroy. The main principle A strong spirit is not a desire to dominate others. This is the ability to manage oneself. The more a person is able to control his own thoughts, emotions, actions and desires, the freer he becomes. Freedom does not begin when external restrictions disappear. Freedom begins when a person becomes his own master. Strengthening the spirit is a continuous process of cultivating inner freedom, responsibility, and the ability to consciously choose the path of creation, regardless of external circumstances. Causes of psychological problems The basic principle In the New Psychology DREVO, a psychological problem is not considered as a separate illness of the personality, but asviolation of harmony between human levels. A person is a single system. When one or more of its levels lose coherence, internal conflicts, emotional tension, behavioral disturbances and deterioration in quality of life arise. A psychological problem is not a person’s enemy. This is a signal that a certain part of the system needs attention, restoration or development. The main causes of psychological problems 1. Disconnection from the body Lack of sleep. Chronic fatigue. Malnutrition. Lack of movement. Chronic pain. Hormonal and other diseases. When the body is exhausted, the psyche and consciousness also lose stability. 2. Disruption of the subconscious Automatic reactions formed by traumatic experiences. Destructive habits. Chronic fear. Unprocessed emotional experiences. The subconscious continues to protect a person even when previous methods of protection no longer help. 3. Mental conflict A person wants opposite things at the same time. For example: freedom and complete security; closeness and complete independence; change and maintaining the familiar. Unresolved internal contradictions create long-term tension. 4. Loss of awareness When a person stops noticing his own thoughts, feelings and actions, he begins to live automatically. Automatism gradually deprives a person of freedom of choice. 5. Weakening of the will The person knows what needs to be done, but is unable to implement his decision. A feeling of powerlessness gradually arises. 6. Loss of meaning When a person ceases to understand why he lives and develops, even familiar things can lose their inner value. This may be accompanied by feelings of emptiness, apathy and loss of motivation. 7. Conflict of values Suffering occurs when a person is forced to live contrary to his own beliefs or constantly acts against his conscience. The deeper this conflict, the greater the internal tension. 8. Disruption of social connections Loneliness. Distrust. Destructive relationships. Lack of support. Insulation. A person develops through relationships. Therefore, the destruction of social connections weakens psychological resilience. 9. Unfavorable environment Constant noise. Information overload. Aggressive social environment. Lack of contact with nature. Environmental issues. The environment gradually becomes part of a person’s inner world. 10. Violation of psychological ecology Every day a person takes in a huge amount of information. If a large part of it consists of fear, aggression, lies, humiliation, manipulation and constant stress, internal balance is gradually disturbed. The psyche needs not only protection from physical threats, but also a healthy information environment. Compensation principle When one level of a person weakens, other levels often try to compensate for its work. For example: the body can signal with pain; emotions - anxiety; behavior - addiction; relationships - conflicts. Therefore, symptoms should be viewed not only as a problem, but also as a possible indication of a deeper imbalance. The main principle In the New Psychology DREVO, the psychologist’s task is not only to reduce symptoms. The main task is to understand,at what level is harmony violated?, what factors support this condition and how can human integrity be restored. Mental health does not return when a single symptom disappears. It returns when the body, psyche, consciousness, will, values, relationships and environment begin to work as a single system again. Any psychological problem is not a death sentence for the individual, but an invitation to restore internal balance and further development.

title: Laws of personality development
excerpt: The law of life Life strives for development. Every living organism has an internal drive for growth, adaptation and self-preservation. Development is a natural state of man. Stopping development leads to gradual degrada
text: The law of life Life strives for development. Every living organism has an internal drive for growth, adaptation and self-preservation. Development is a natural state of man. Stopping development leads to gradual degradation. Law of Integrity A human being is a single system. The body, subconscious, psyche, consciousness, superconsciousness, soul, spirit, values, social connections and the environment constantly influence each other. It is impossible to change one part of the system without affecting the others. The law of cause and effect Every thought influences emotions. Emotions influence decisions. Decisions become actions. Actions become habits. Habits shape character. Character determines a person's life path. The Law of Awareness Development begins with observation. A person can change only what he can understand. Mindfulness turns automatic life into free choice. The Law of Will Willpower is the ability to control oneself and make conscious choices. The greater a person's ability to control his thoughts, emotions and actions, the greater his inner freedom. Law of Responsibility Freedom is impossible without responsibility. Every decision has consequences. A person becomes mature when he accepts responsibility for his thoughts, words, actions and their impact on other people and the world around him. The Law of Harmony True development does not destroy the system. The development of the body should not come at the cost of the destruction of the psyche. Personal development should not destroy the family. Economic development should not destroy nature. Harmony is the ability to develop while maintaining the stability of the entire system. The Law of Continuous Learning A person develops throughout his life. Every new experience becomes a source of knowledge. Every mistake becomes an opportunity for growth. Learning ends only with life. The Law of Overcoming Growth is impossible without overcoming difficulties. Challenges are not the opposite of growth. They are a natural part of it. By overcoming obstacles, a person develops strength, wisdom and resilience. Law of Cooperation A person reveals his potential through interaction with other people. Competition promotes the development of individual abilities. Cooperation promotes the development of civilization. The Law of Psychological Ecology A person's inner world depends on the environment in which he lives. Information, relationships, culture, nature and technology constantly shape the state of the psyche. Taking care of your internal and external environment is a necessary condition for psychological health. The Law of Creation The highest form of development is creation. Human development becomes complete when he begins to create not only for himself, but also for others. Creation transforms knowledge into culture, work into heritage, and life into a source of social development. The Law of Destiny Each person has a unique combination of abilities, experiences and values. Purpose is revealed when a person uses his abilities for the development of life, society and future generations. Law of Inheritance The true value of life is determined not by the amount accumulated, but by what a person leaves behind. Knowledge. Children. Culture. Scientific discoveries. Good works. Created communities. Restored nature. True development continues even after man's departure. The Main Law of New Psychology DREVO A person develops harmoniously when each of his decisions simultaneously strengthens him, benefits other people and contributes to the preservation and development of life in all its manifestations. This is precisely the path of a mature individual, a creative society and a sustainable civilization. Psychology of the Future From the science of problems to the science of development The psychology of the future studies not only the causes of suffering, but also the laws of human development. Its goal is not simply to help people adapt to the existing world, but to reveal their ability to create a healthier, more just and harmonious world. A person is viewed not as an object of treatment, but as an active participant in his own life and the development of society. Man as a living system The psychology of the future considers a person as an integral system in which the following are interconnected: body; subconscious; psyche; consciousness; will; superconsciousness; soul; spirit; values ​​and meaning; social connections; environment. The development of one level inevitably affects all the others. Therefore, it is impossible to understand a person by studying only the brain, only behavior, or only the social environment. From personality to ecosystem A person never develops alone. His health depends on: families; culture; education; nature; economics; technologies; quality of human relationships. Future psychology views the individual as part of a broader ecosystem of life. Therefore, caring for people is impossible without caring for society and the environment. Science and openness to new ideas The psychology of the future is based on the achievements of modern science: psychology; neuroscience; biology; medicine; pedagogy; sociology. At the same time, it remains open to exploring new questions about the nature of consciousness, creativity, subjective experience, and other phenomena that have not yet received a full scientific explanation. A new idea becomes part of science only after it has been tested, reproducible, and critically analyzed. Development instead of correction The main goal of the psychology of the future is not to make a person “normal”. The main goal is to help him become more mature, free and capable of creation. Psychological development includes: health promotion; development of thinking; education of will; disclosure of abilities; development of emotional maturity; strengthening relationships; formation of responsibility; search for meaning; realization of purpose. Psychology of creation The highest form of development becomes the ability to create. Create: knowledge; culture; technologies; family; communities; works of art; scientific discoveries; environmental projects; conditions for the development of future generations. Creation becomes a natural continuation of inner growth. Man and technology Artificial intelligence, robotics and biotechnology will change the life of humanity. Therefore, the psychology of the future must answer not only the question: "How does a person interact with a person?" but also to the questions: "How does a person interact with artificial intelligence?" "What qualities will remain uniquely human?" Technology should expand human capabilities, not replace freedom of choice, responsibility and individual dignity. Psychology of the Future Civilization The development of the individual is inseparable from the development of civilization. True progress is not determined solely by economic growth and technological advances. It is determined by the fact that how much people become: healthier; more free; more responsible; more cooperative; more creative. It is the quality of a person that determines the quality of the future society. DREVO's Vision The new psychology of DREVO views humans as living, self-developing systems capable of consciously participating in the development of life. Its goal is to combine the achievements of science, practical experience and human philosophical understanding into a single system of knowledge. It does not contrast body and consciousness, personality and society, man and nature, technology and humanism. She strives to understand the laws by which life develops and to help people live in harmony with these laws. The main goal The psychology of the future is the science of unlocking human potential, strengthening the individual, developing society, and preserving life in all its manifestations. Her main question is not: "What's wrong with man?" A: “What can a person become if conditions are created for his harmonious development?” From the psychology of survival to the psychology of creation Throughout most of its history, man has been learning to survive. The struggle for food, safety, and protection of family and clan shaped many of our psychological mechanisms. Fear, anxiety, aggression, vigilance, and the desire to control the surrounding world helped us maintain life in the face of constant danger. Modern psychology pays close attention to these mechanisms. It studies trauma, stress, anxiety disorders, depression, addictions, and other conditions that reduce quality of life. This approach is of great value because it helps people restore inner balance and overcome suffering. However, recovery is not yet development. A person who has freed himself from fear does not necessarily become a creator. A person who has overcome depression does not necessarily find the meaning of life. A person who has learned to cope with stress does not necessarily begin to create something valuable for the world. Therefore, New Psychology DREVO suggests taking the next step. Its task is not only to help a person survive, but also to help him learn to live a full life. The psychology of creation begins where the struggle for simple survival ends. She asks new questions. Not only: "How to get rid of suffering?" but also: "How to reveal your abilities?" "How to learn to love?" "How to create?" "How can I leave the world better than I found it?" In the psychology of survival, protection becomes the most important thing. In the psychology of creation, development becomes the main thing. Survival psychology teaches us to avoid danger. The psychology of creation teaches us to create opportunities. Survival psychology seeks to preserve life. The psychology of creation seeks to reveal its potential. This doesn't mean abandoning the understanding of trauma, pain, or illness. On the contrary, helping someone overcome suffering remains a necessary step. But it is seen as the beginning of the journey, not its final destination. The new psychology of DREVO considers man as a creative being. The highest manifestation of maturity is not the ability to defend oneself, but the ability to create. Create knowledge. Create culture. Create families. Create communities. Create technologies. To create beauty. Create conditions in which other people and future generations can develop. True development begins when a person stops living only by the question of his own survival and begins to recognize himself as a participant in the development of life. The main goal of the New Psychology DREVO is to help people move from survival to creation, from reaction to conscious choice, from fear to responsibility, from consumption to creativity, from the struggle for life to participation in its development. The psychology of the future is not only the science of how to reduce suffering. This is the science of how to develop a person so that he becomes a source of development for himself, society, nature and future generations. title: The Principle of the Human Biofield
excerpt: In the New Psychology DREVO, a person is viewed as not only a biochemical, but also a bioelectrical system. Every cell in the body is involved in electrical processes. The nervous system transmits signals using electrica
text: In the New Psychology DREVO, a person is viewed as not only a biochemical, but also a bioelectrical system. Every cell in the body is involved in electrical processes. The nervous system transmits signals using electrical impulses. The heart creates powerful electrical activity. The brain constantly generates electrical rhythms. Muscles, internal organs and other tissues also have their own bioelectrical activity. The combination of these processes forms the electromagnetic fields of the body, which can be recorded by modern scientific methods. As part of the New Psychology DREVO human biofieldis considered as one of the manifestations of its physiological state and the interaction of the organism with the environment. We use the term"aura"as a philosophical and cultural designation of the integral human field, understanding that its properties and boundaries require further research. Thus, DREVO's New Psychology does not claim that all traditional notions about the aura have already been scientifically confirmed. It proceeds from the premise that humans possess measurable bioelectrical activity, while the question of its more complex manifestations remains open to scientific study. Practical principle Changes in the state of the body, psyche and lifestyle are reflected in the physiological processes of the body, including its bioelectrical activity. Therefore, caring for the health of the body, emotional state, quality of sleep, movement, breathing, relationships and the environment is simultaneously caring for the holistic state of a person. The more harmoniously the body functions, the more coordinated its internal physiological processes become. Studying this coordination is one of the promising goals of DREVO's New Psychology. Principle of biofield interaction In the New Psychology of DREVO, a person is viewed as an open living system, continuously interacting with the surrounding world and other people. Each organism creates its own bioelectrical and biomagnetic activity associated with the functioning of the heart, brain, nervous system and other organs. When people meet, several levels of interaction occur simultaneously: biological; psychological; social; informational; and, according to the DREVO research hypothesis, biofield. Under biofield interactionThe possible influence of physiological electromagnetic processes in one organism on another is understood. This hypothesis requires further experimental verification and is not considered an established scientific fact. Regardless of the outcome of such studies, it is clear that people are capable of synchronizing through breathing, speech rhythm, movement, facial expression, attention, emotions, and shared activities. These processes create a sense of mutual understanding, trust, or, conversely, tension. The new psychology of DREVO suggests that a harmonious human state promotes healthier interactions with others. Therefore, personal development is viewed not only as an internal process but also as a contribution to the quality of relationships and the environment in which others live. The principle of mutual influence Every person influences others with their state of mind, words, actions and lifestyle. Every interaction leaves a trace. Therefore, by developing one's own integrity, a person simultaneously contributes to the development of his community. In DREVO's New Psychology, personal health is viewed not as an isolated state, but as part of a broader ecology of human relationships, in which the internal state of one person can affect the well-being of others through a multitude of interconnected mechanisms, some of which have already been well studied, while others still await scientific explanation. Biofield, aura and horizontal flows Biofield in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, a person is viewed as an open living system, constantly exchanging information, matter, heat, signals, and emotional states with the outside world. The body has measurable bioelectrical activity. The work of the heart, brain, nervous system, muscles and internal organs is accompanied by electrical and magnetic processes. The combination of these processes in the DREVO model is calledhuman biofield. However, the biofield is not considered as a separate mystical substance, but as one of the levels of manifestation of the holistic state of the organism. What is an aura? In the New Psychology DREVO, the aura is considered as an external area of ​​manifestation of a person’s state. It can be understood as a combination of several simultaneously existing factors: bioelectric and biomagnetic processes; thermal radiation of the body; breath and odors; postures, movements and facial expressions; emotional state; voice and rhythm of speech; attention; psychological influence on others. Thus, the aura is not only a supposed energy field. This is the holistic space of a person’s presence, through which others perceive his state. A person may not yet utter a single word, but others already notice his tension, calmness, openness, fear, strength or fatigue. Biofield and aura In the DREVO model, biofield and aura are related, but not completely identical concepts. Biofieldrefers primarily to the internal physiological and bioelectrical processes of the body. Aurais a broader concept and describes how a person's holistic state manifests itself around him and is perceived by other people. You can say: the biofield is created by the vital activity of the organism; The aura is an image of its external manifestation. Horizontal flows Horizontal flows are the exchange between a person and the surrounding world. They are aimed at: from person to person; from individual to family; from individual to community; from society to the individual; from man to nature; from the environment to humans. While the vertical flow in the DREVO model is associated with spirit, purpose, and direction toward higher values, the horizontal flows relate to earthly life, relationships, and exchange. The vertical answers the question: “What higher thing am I connected with and what do I live for?” The horizontal answers: “Who and what do I interact with in this world?” Types of horizontal flows Physical flow Exchange of heat, touch, movement, substances and physiological signals. Emotional flow People transmit mood, anxiety, calmness, joy, confidence and tension to each other. This happens through voice, facial expression, behavior and quality of presence. Information flow Exchange of words, knowledge, images, ideas and symbols. Through it, culture, learning and collective intelligence are formed. Social Stream Exchange of support, labor, trust, responsibility and resources. Biofield flow The DREVO philosophical research model suggests that bioelectrical and biomagnetic processes of organisms can be one of the additional elements of human interaction. The extent and mechanism of such influence require further scientific study. Aura and the human condition The aura is not permanent. It changes along with the person's condition. It can be influenced by: dream; health; breath; stress; nutrition; physical activity; emotional experiences; relationship; environment; inner meaning; meditation and state of attention. A calm, healthy, and internally consistent person is usually perceived differently than a person who is exhausted, frightened, or aggressive. This does not necessarily require a mystical explanation. Much of this perception can occur through known physiological and psychological cues. Interaction of auras When people are close to each other, their spaces of presence overlap. They begin to influence each other through: breath; voice; sight; movement; touch; emotional state; attention; expectations; trust or fear. Common conditions may arise within a group. For example: calmness; voltage; inspiration; aggression; trust; a sense of unity. In the DREVO model this can be described as the interaction and coordination of auras and horizontal flows. Aura boundaries A healthy aura does not mean maximum openness to everything. A person needs psychological and physical boundaries. Boundaries help: distinguish between your own and other people's emotions; preserve your own values; do not give in to constant pressure; choose with whom and how to interact; protect attention and internal state. A strong aura does not mean dominance over others. It is the ability to maintain integrity in interaction. Harmonization of horizontal flows Horizontal flows become healthy when the exchange is based on: respect; honesty; freedom; reciprocity; responsibility; clear boundaries; cooperation; creation. Destructive currents arise where: manipulation; humiliation; violence; constant fear; exploitation; lie; emotional infection of hatred. Therefore, psychological ecology includes concern not only for the internal state, but also for the quality of exchange between people. Vertical and horizontal A holistic person exists at the intersection of two directions. Vertical flowconnects it with spirit, meaning, purpose and higher values. Horizontal flowsconnect him with people, society, nature and the material world. Without vertical, a person can lose direction. Without horizontal line - connection with real life. Harmony arises when inner values ​​are expressed in relationships and actions. The main principle The aura reflects a person's state. Horizontal flows show the quality of its exchange with the world. The vertical flow sets the direction. The biofield connects these processes with the vital activity of the organism. The more the body, psyche, consciousness, soul and spirit are aligned, the more integral a person’s presence becomes. Definition The biofield is the totality of the body's bioelectric and biomagnetic processes. The aura is the holistic space of the external manifestation of a person's physical, emotional, psychological, and philosophical state. Horizontal flows are the processes of exchange between the individual, other people, society, and nature. In the New Psychology DREVO, these concepts form a unified model of interaction between the individual and the world. The vertical gives a person direction. The horizontal creates relationships. The aura reveals the inner state. The biofield reflects the life of the organism. In their coherence, a person's holistic presence in the world is born.

title: Level One - Life and Instinct
excerpt: The most ancient level is associated with the preservation of the organism. Its main tasks are: breath; nutrition; protection; search for safety; avoidance of pain; procreation; automatic response to threat. At the physi
text: The most ancient level is associated with the preservation of the organism. Its main tasks are: breath; nutrition; protection; search for safety; avoidance of pain; procreation; automatic response to threat. At the physiological level, these processes involve the brainstem, hypothalamus, autonomic nervous system and other ancient regulatory structures. In popular culture, this level is sometimes referred to as the "reptilian brain," but modern neuroscience considers this division overly simplistic. The brain does not consist of three independent layers, successively built on top of each other. Ancient and new structures work together. Psychological question of the level: "Am I safe to live?" Main need: preservation of life. Second level - Emotions and attachment As social animals evolved, emotional connections became increasingly important. Emotions helped to quickly assess what was happening: dangerous or safe; pleasant or unpleasant; yours or someone else's; to approach or move away. This level includes: fear; joy; anger; attachment; pleasure; care; jealousy; emotional memory. These processes involve not just the “limbic system,” but distributed brain networks including the amygdala, hypothalamus, hippocampus, insular, and prefrontal cortex. Psychological question of the level: "What do I feel and where do I belong?" Main need: emotional connection. The third level is Social belonging For humans, survival depended heavily on the group. Therefore, the following abilities were developed: recognize faces and intentions; understand status and roles; imitate; cooperate; learn from others; follow the rules; to feel shame, guilt and pride; protect family and community. At this level, a person begins to perceive himself not only as a separate organism, but also as part of a family, clan, and group. Psychological question of the level: "Who are my people and what is my place among them?" Main need: belonging and recognition. Level Four: Reason and Modeling the World The development of the cerebral cortex has expanded the human ability to analyze information and create internal models of reality. The following arise: speech; logics; abstract thinking; cause and effect analysis; planning; complex training; use of symbols; technical creativity. Reason allows a person to act not only on the basis of immediate emotion, but also taking into account knowledge and possible consequences. Psychological question of the level: "How does the world work?" Main need: understanding. Level Five – Consciousness and Introspection Consciousness allows a person not only to think, but also to observe his own thinking. He begins to notice: your reactions; motives; fears; beliefs; internal contradictions. The ability to say arises: "I feel anger, but I am not obligated to act under its influence." This is where the space between impulse and action appears. Psychological question of the level: "What's going on inside me?" Main need: clarity and awareness. Level Six – Will and Self-Government Awareness creates the possibility of choice, but choice becomes reality only through the will. Will allows: hold the target; manage attention; delay instant gratification; keep promises; change habits; act despite fear; maintain direction in difficult conditions. Physiologically, self-management is associated with the joint work of the prefrontal cortex, attention, memory, motivation, and emotional regulation systems. Psychological question of the level: "Am I able to control myself?" Main need: inner freedom. Level Seven – Values ​​and Morals A person is capable of evaluating actions not only according to the principle of “pleasant - unpleasant” or “profitable - unprofitable”. He starts asking: is this fair; is it worthy; will it cause harm; does this correspond to my beliefs? At this level the following arise: moral principles; conscience; responsibility; respect for dignity; sense of justice; the ability to give up profit for the sake of values. Morality is formed under the influence of biological prerequisites, upbringing, culture, personal experience and conscious reflection. Psychological question of the level: "What is right?" Main need: internal integrity. Level Eight – Soul and Authenticity In the philosophical model of DREVO, the soul denotes the inner core of the personality. This level is associated with: a sense of the true self; love; conscience; compassion; experience of beauty; creativity; inner honesty; deep personal values. Scientifically, the soul is not defined as a separate organ or measurable structure. In the DREVO model, this concept is used to describe the holistic subjective experience and moral individuality of a person. Psychological question of the level: "Who am I really?" Main need: authenticity. Level Nine - Spirit and Direction Spirit in the DREVO model reflects a person's ability to direct life toward goals that extend beyond immediate comfort. It manifests itself through: courage; loyalty to principles; purpose; long-term thinking; service; the ability to endure difficulties for the sake of meaning; concern for the future. If the soul determines the inner content of the personality, then the spirit sets the direction of its movement. Psychological question of the level: "What do I live for?" Main need: meaning. Level Ten - Creation At this level, a person ceases to be just a consumer of a ready-made world. He begins to create: knowledge; family; culture; art; technologies; enterprises; communities; new forms of cooperation; restored nature. Creation is a transition from internal development to external contribution. Psychological question of the level: "What will be better because of me?" Main need: implementation. Level Eleven - Service and Legacy The highest social function of the individual becomes the ability to act for the sake of life, which will continue after it. The man thinks: about children; about the students; about society; about nature; about future generations; about knowledge and systems that can work without it. Here the personality goes beyond personal success. Psychological question of the level: "What will live after me?" Main need: continuation of meaning in time. Personality as a vertical of development Levels do not replace each other. Higher functions do not destroy lower ones. A mature person continues to need security, emotion, belonging, and recognition. But he ceases to be completely controlled by these needs alone. Development means that each subsequent level is able to comprehend and guide the previous ones. Instinct gives energy to life. Emotions give her experience. Reason helps to understand. Consciousness creates choice. Will embodies choice. Values ​​define the boundaries of what is acceptable. The soul retains its authenticity. The spirit sets the direction. Creation turns potential into benefit. Service and legacy connect a person's life with the future. Highest social function The highest social function of man lies not only in the ability to adapt to society. It manifests itself in the ability to: understand others; to unite people; create trust; to transfer knowledge; resolve conflicts; to shape culture; build institutions; to care for those whom a person will never see in person. It is this ability that makes civilization possible. In the philosophical model of DREVO, the developed cerebral cortex can be metaphorically calledinterface of the soul and higher social functions, because through the work of the brain, a person’s internal values ​​are transformed into speech, relationships, moral decisions, creativity and constructive projects. But the expression “antenna of the soul” remains a philosophical metaphor, not a proven neurophysiological mechanism. DREVO's Personality Evolution Formula Life → Instinct → Emotion → Belonging → Reason → Awareness → Will → Values ​​→ Soul → Spirit → Creation → Service → Heritage. This sequence is not a rigid ladder. All levels interact simultaneously. However, it shows the general direction of development: from preserving one's own life to the ability to preserve and develop life around oneself. Definition The evolution of personality levels is a gradual increase in the complexity of the ways in which a person maintains life, feels, thinks, is aware of himself, manages behavior, builds relationships, forms values, creates meaning, and makes a creative contribution to the future. In the New Psychology of DREVO, maturity is achieved not by rejecting ancient levels, but by their harmonious inclusion into a higher system of consciousness, responsibility and service. A person begins with the instinct for life, but it doesn't end there. The highest level of their development occurs when they transform the life they receive into a source of life, knowledge, and opportunity for others. Laws of personality development Introduction Personality development is not a random process. It follows certain patterns that manifest themselves regardless of a person's culture, age, or profession. In New Psychology DREVO, these patterns are called the laws of personality development. They describe not strict rules, but principles, the understanding of which helps a person consciously build their life. 1. Law of Integrity A human being is a single living system. The body, subconscious, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, values, relationships and environment constantly influence each other. The development of one level should not occur at the expense of the destruction of others. Real development strengthens the entire system.

title: 2. The law of cause and effect
excerpt: Every thought influences emotions. Emotions influence decisions. Decisions become actions. Actions become habits. Habits shape character. Character determines a person's life path. By understanding the reasons for one's
text:
Every thought influences emotions. Emotions influence decisions. Decisions become actions. Actions become habits. Habits shape character. Character determines a person's life path. By understanding the reasons for one's actions, one gains the ability to change their consequences. 3. The Law of Conscious Choice Freedom begins where conscious choice appears. Consciousness allows us to see different possibilities. Willpower helps to implement the chosen decision. The higher a person’s awareness, the greater his inner freedom. 4. Law of Responsibility Every freedom comes with responsibility. A person becomes mature when he stops looking for someone to blame and begins to take responsibility for his own thoughts, words and actions. Responsibility is the ability to recognize the consequences of one's decisions and to take part in their correction or development. 5. The law of continuous development Development continues throughout life. Every day lived either strengthens a person or gradually weakens him. There is no stop in development. Even inaction changes personality. 6. The Law of Small Steps Big changes come from small daily actions. Habits have a more profound influence on personality than rare emotional outbursts. It is consistency that creates sustainable development. 7. The Law of Overcoming Growth is impossible without overcoming difficulties. Trials in themselves do not make a person stronger. What makes him stronger is how he responds to these challenges. Every difficulty overcome increases experience, resilience and inner maturity. 8. The Law of Meaning A person is capable of overcoming difficulties for a long time if he understands why he is doing it. Meaning transforms efforts into development. Without meaning, even success can seem empty. 9. Law of Cooperation Personality develops faster in interaction with other people. Knowledge sharing, mutual support, co-creation and trust enhance the development of each participant. True personal growth does not isolate a person from society, but makes him more useful to it. 10. The Law of Psychological Ecology Everything that a person regularly lets into his life gradually becomes part of his inner world. Information. Communication. Music. Culture. Nature. Digital environment. Every external factor influences the quality of inner life. Therefore, caring for your internal ecology is just as important as caring for your physical health. 11. The Law of Creation Development reaches maturity when a person begins not only to receive, but also to create. Creativity can manifest itself in raising children, scientific discoveries, art, entrepreneurship, caring for nature, helping people, or sharing knowledge. A person reveals himself most fully when his abilities become a source of benefit to others. 12. Law of Inheritance The highest form of development is the ability to leave behind not only material results, but also knowledge, culture, good deeds, healthy relationships and conditions for the development of future generations. A person becomes truly mature when he begins to think not only about his own life, but also about what kind of world will remain after it. The main law of DREVO Everything is interconnected. By developing oneself, a person influences the family. By developing the family, he influences society. By developing society, it influences nature. By changing the world around him, he again changes himself. Therefore, true personal development is not a movement towards personal perfection at any cost, but a continuous strengthening of harmony between the individual, society and the surrounding world. It is in this harmony that the New Psychology of DREVO sees the basis of health, freedom, maturity and a creative future. Foundations of DREVO New Psychology Foundations of DREVO New Psychology New Psychology as a Unified Living System Author: Oleksandr Rud @sssvetomir This is not just a book on psychology. This is an attempt to take a new look at a person - as a holistic, living and continuously developing system in which the body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, values, relationships and the surrounding world form a single whole. The new psychology of DREVO combines modern scientific knowledge with a philosophical understanding of human nature. Its goal is not only to help people overcome psychological difficulties but also to unlock their inner potential, teach them to live consciously and harmoniously, collaborate, create, and leave a positive legacy. This book invites the reader to become an explorer of their own personality and to follow the path from self-knowledge to development, from development to creation, and from creation to service to life. Like a tree, a person grows throughout their life. And the deeper their roots, the higher they can rise and the more benefit they can bring to the world. Content: Part I. Fundamentals of the New Psychology DREVO Manifesto of the New Psychology. The principle of psychological ecology. What is a human being? Ten levels of man. Laws of personality development. Part II. Human Architecture Body. Subconscious. Psyche. Consciousness. Will. Superconsciousness. Soul. Spirit. Values ​​and meaning. Social connections. Interaction with nature. The connection between the psyche, hormones and the body Sleep in New Psychology Human biofield. Biofield interaction. Soul, biofield and spirit Part III. Laws of Personality Development The law of life Law of Integrity The law of cause and effect The Law of Awareness The Law of Will Law of Responsibility The Law of Harmony The Law of Overcoming Law of Cooperation The Law of Psychological Ecology The Law of Creation The Law of Destiny Law of Inheritance Law of exchange The law of growth The Law of Service Part IV. Causes of Psychological Problems Why does a person suffer? What is fear? What is anxiety? What is depression? What is laziness? What is addiction? What is aggression? What is loneliness? What is burnout? What is happiness? What is love? Part V. Practice daily practices; weekly; Monthly; annual; psychological ecology; development of will; revelation of the soul; strengthening of the spirit; search for purpose; family development; community development; diary of desires; daily newspaper; dream diary; Diary of desires as a way of shaping reality; Meditation as autogenic training. Part VI. Psychology of Society family psychology; psychology of the family; community psychology; psychology of culture; psychology of the state; psychology of civilization; psychology of cooperation; psychology of war and peace. Part VII. Psychology of the Future Human and artificial intelligence. Psychology of space civilization. Ecology of consciousness. Collective intelligence. Biotechnology and the psyche. Digital ecology. Psychology of future generations. Examples of positive affirmations, desires and thoughts Example of a Wish Diary (for shaping reality) Definition of maturity Personality Development Map Psychological immunity Ecology of information Architecture of a happy life Karma in New Psychology The legacy of man How to become happy? What will remain after me? PREAMBLE New Psychology DREVO Humanity is entering an era of profound change. The development of artificial intelligence, biotechnology, the digital environment, global communications, and changing lifestyles require a new understanding of humanity. We have learned to create highly complex technologies, but we still lack a clear understanding of ourselves. Modern psychology has made significant advances in the study of emotions, behavior, memory, thinking, and brain function. However, a person cannot be reduced to neural processes, individual mental functions, or social roles. It is a complex living system in which the body, subconscious, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, values, relationships with people and interaction with the outside world continuously influence each other. The new psychology of DREVO suggests considering a person as such an integral system. It does not reject the achievements of modern science, but seeks to combine knowledge from psychology, neuroscience, biology, medicine, pedagogy, philosophy, ecology and social sciences into a single model of personal development. At the same time, New Psychology clearly distinguishes between two areas of knowledge. Where scientific evidence exists, it relies on modern research. Where the subject is the soul, spirit, meaning of life, values ​​or inner experience of a person, she views them as philosophical categories open to further research and understanding. The main goal of New Psychology is not only to help people cope with psychological difficulties. Its task is much broader. Help a person become healthier. More free. More conscious. More responsible. More creative. Happier. More capable of love. More able to collaborate. More capable of creating a world in which future generations can live with dignity. At the center of the New Psychology DREVO is the idea of ​​development. A person is not seen as a bearer of problems, diagnoses or limitations. He is seen as a constantly evolving individual with enormous potential for learning, creation, collaboration and transformation of the world around him. The basis of this system is several interrelated principles. Human integrity. Development instead of fighting symptoms. Awareness instead of automatism. Responsibility instead of looking for the guilty. Cooperation instead of destructive competition. Creation instead of consumption. Psychological ecology instead of information pollution. Respect for life in all its manifestations. The new psychology of DREVO views personal development as a path that passes through many interconnected stages. From understanding your own body to understanding your psyche. From the psyche to awareness. From awareness to free choice. From choice to will. From will to habits. From habits to character. From character to creation. From creation to service. From service to legacy. Like a tree, a person takes root in life, strengthens his inner trunk, reveals his abilities, creates fruits and leaves behind new seeds from which future generations can grow. That is why the symbol of this system is a tree. It reflects continuous growth, the interconnectedness of all parts of a living system, the ability to overcome difficulties and benefit the surrounding world. The new psychology of DREVO is not only a personality theory. This is a philosophy of development. A practical system for raising a mature person. The basis of psychological ecology of the future. And an invitation to a shared exploration of human nature, in which science, philosophy, culture, and personal experience help us to understand humanity more deeply and unlock our creative potential. By developing a person, we develop society.
By developing society, we create the future.
By developing the future, we preserve life.

title: Foundations of the New Psychology
excerpt: The new psychology can view humans not as the bearer of symptoms or a set of cognitive processes, but as a holistic, evolving system. It integrates knowledge from the natural, social, and human sciences, maintaining a cr
text:
The new psychology can view humans not as the bearer of symptoms or a set of cognitive processes, but as a holistic, evolving system. It integrates knowledge from the natural, social, and human sciences, maintaining a critical approach to hypotheses and relying on verifiable data where possible. 1. Human integrity
A person is a unity of body, psyche, consciousness, relationships with others, and the environment. Changes in one area can impact others. 2. Development instead of eliminating problems
Psychology helps not only overcome difficulties but also develop strengths: resilience, creativity, the ability to learn, collaborate, and make decisions. 3. Meaning and values
Understanding your own values ​​and life goals impacts well-being, motivation, and ability to cope with challenges. 4. Unity of reason and emotions
Emotions and thinking work together. Emotions convey information, and rational thinking helps us understand and use it. 5. The body and mind are interconnected
Sleep, nutrition, physical activity, illness, and stress all affect psychological well-being, just as mental well-being can affect physical well-being. 6. Man is a part of society and nature
Mental well-being is associated with the quality of relationships, a sense of belonging, a safe environment, and contact with nature. 7. Awareness and responsibility
A person is able to observe their thoughts, emotions and habits, gradually changing their behavior through conscious choice. 8. Scientific verifiability
Any new theory must be testable. Ideas concerning consciousness, spiritual experience, or new methods of assistance can be explored, but they should not be declared established facts without sufficient evidence. 9. Individuality
There is no one-size-fits-all developmental path. Assistance methods must take into account individual characteristics, culture, age, and life experience. 10. Continuous development
Psychological development continues throughout life. The goal is not to achieve an "ideal state," but to be able to learn, adapt, and maintain internal resilience in the face of change. Such a system can be considered as the basis of an interdisciplinary psychology that combines the achievements of modern science with philosophical questions about personality, the meaning of life, and human development, without mixing ideological ideas with established scientific knowledge. MANIFESTO OF THE NEW PSYCHOLOGY Science of the Whole Man Humanity is entering an era when old ideas about man are no longer sufficient. Modern psychology has made great strides in studying behavior, emotions, memory, thinking, and brain function. However, humans are far more complex than a set of neural processes or behavioral patterns. New psychology proposes to view a person as a holistic living system in which the body, psyche, consciousness, values, relationships, environment, and internal search for meaning are interconnected. We recognize the achievements of modern science and consider them the foundation for further development. At the same time, we are open to exploring questions that have not yet received definitive answers: the nature of consciousness, subjective experience, creativity, intuition, the meaning of life, and other profound aspects of human existence. Basic principles We argue that a person is an integral system that includes several interconnected levels. Body— the foundation of life, possessing its own biological wisdom and the ability to self-regulate. Subconscious— a deep system of automatic processes, experiential memory, hereditary programs and bodily adaptation. Psyche— a system of perception, thinking, emotions, memory, learning and interaction with the surrounding world. Consciousness- the ability to observe, perceive, discern and freely choose the direction of action. Superconsciousness— a space of creativity, inspiration, deep insights, and the search for new possibilities. Its nature requires further scientific research. Soul— a philosophical concept denoting the inner core of a person, their values, sense of authenticity, and experience of meaning. Spirit— a philosophical concept denoting a person’s striving for ideals, the ability to remain faithful to one’s principles and overcome difficulties for the sake of the chosen path. Values We believe that human development is impossible without an internal moral foundation. Love. Freedom. Responsibility. Dignity. Honesty. Justice. Creativity. Cooperation. Respect for life. Creation. These values ​​do not pit people against each other, but create the basis for the joint development of the individual, society and civilization. Community A person develops through relationships. Family. Friendship. Genus. Culture. Education. Scientific cooperation. Society. Psychological health cannot be considered separately from the quality of human relationships. Nature Man is a part of nature. Its well-being cannot be separated from the state of water, air, soil, forests, animals and the entire ecosystem of the Earth. Caring for nature is also caring for people. Technologies Technologies should expand human capabilities, not replace humans. Artificial intelligence should contribute to the development of personality, education, science, and medicine, while preserving human freedom of choice, dignity, and responsibility. Scientific approach New psychology does not reject science. It expands the field of research. Anything that can be verified should be investigated by scientific methods. Anything that does not yet have sufficient evidence must remain the subject of open, honest and critical study, and not of unconditional belief or denial. The main goal The main goal of the new psychology is not only to reduce suffering. The main goal is to unlock human potential. Help a person become healthier. More free. More conscious. More responsible. More creative. More capable of love. More capable of creating a world in which future generations can live with dignity. Our vision We see a person not as a problem that needs to be fixed. We see man as a continuously evolving system, capable of knowing, creating, loving, cooperating and transforming the world. The new psychology is not a rejection of the past. This is the next stage of understanding man. A stage in which science, philosophy, culture and human experience do not oppose each other, but together help to more deeply understand the nature of the individual and its place in the world. By knowing a person, we know the world. By changing ourselves, we change the future. The principle of psychological ecology The inner world of a person is like a living ecosystem New psychology views a person as a complex living ecosystem in which the body, psyche, consciousness, subconscious, superconscious, soul, spirit, values, social connections and the environment form a single interconnected system. Just as environmental pollution disrupts the functioning of ecosystems, informational, emotional and social pollution disrupts a person’s internal balance. Psychological ecology is the science and practice of maintaining a healthy internal human environment. Basic Law Everything that a person lets into himself gradually becomes part of his inner world. This applies not only to food and air, but also to: information; words; emotions; music; images; human communication; digital environment; habits; culture; knowledge; daily thoughts. Every external signal becomes a kind of food for the psyche. Therefore, a person must take care not only of the cleanliness of his body, but also of the cleanliness of his internal environment. Psychological pollution Sources of psychological pollution can be: constant fear; hatred; aggression; lie; manipulation; information noise; chronic stress; destructive addictions; humiliation of dignity; toxic relationship. Long-term exposure to such factors can reduce psychological stability, impair quality of life, and hinder personal development. Psychological nutrition Just as the body needs healthy food, the psyche needs quality psychological nutrition. These include: Love; respect; knowledge; creativity; beauty; music; nature; friendship; honest dialogue; sense of meaning; training; physical activity; rest; silence. Psychological nutrition creates conditions for internal growth. Internal immunity The task of the new psychology is not to isolate a person from the world, but to develop his internal stability. Psychological immunity includes the ability to: critically evaluate information; recognize manipulation; maintain emotional balance; recover from difficulties; preserve your own values; build healthy relationships. The stronger the internal immunity, the less destructive the impact of an unfavorable environment. Ecological principle of development A person develops most harmoniously when his inner world is in harmony with the surrounding world. Caring for nature, the health of society and one’s own internal state are different manifestations of the same process – the preservation and development of life. Therefore, the new psychology considers ecology not only as an attitude towards nature, but also as a principle of thinking, communication, education, upbringing and culture. The main principle Everything is interconnected. Thoughts influence emotions. Emotions affect the body. The body influences the mind. Consciousness influences actions. Actions change society. Society changes the environment. The environment influences people again. Understanding this interconnection, a person ceases to perceive himself as a separate being and begins to recognize himself as part of a single system of life. Psychological ecology is the art of maintaining the purity of one's inner world while simultaneously creating a healthier world around oneself.

title: What is a human being?
excerpt: In the New Psychology of DREVO, a person is viewed as a holistic, living, self-developing system, capable of self-awareness, making free choices, creating new things, and bearing responsibility for the consequences of th
text: In the New Psychology of DREVO, a person is viewed as a holistic, living, self-developing system, capable of self-awareness, making free choices, creating new things, and bearing responsibility for the consequences of their actions. A human being is not only a biological organism. He is not only the bearer of the psyche. It is not limited to consciousness, intelligence or social roles. A person is a unity of many interconnected levels, each of which performs its own function in the development of personality. This system includes: the body is the material basis of life; subconscious - accumulated experience and automatic adaptation mechanisms; psyche - the system of perception, thinking, emotions and memory; consciousness is the ability to be aware and choose; will - the ability to control oneself and implement conscious choices; superconsciousness is a space of creativity, inspiration and the search for new opportunities; soul - the inner core of the personality, its values ​​and authenticity (in the philosophical sense); spirit - the direction of development, meaning and desire for creation (in the philosophical sense); values ​​and meaning are the inner compass of life; social connections are a space for joint development; interaction with nature, society and technology - the environment in which a person lives and which he himself transforms. Man is constantly evolving. He is able to change himself through learning, experience, awareness, work, relationships and creativity. At the same time, a person does not exist in isolation. He is part of the family. Part of the family. Part of the community. Part of society. Part of nature. And part of human history. Every decision he makes has an impact not only on himself, but also on the people around him, society, and future generations. Therefore, human development cannot be separated from the development of the environment in which he lives. The main feature of a person The main characteristic of a person is the ability not only to adapt to the world, but also to consciously change oneself and the surrounding reality. It is the ability to be aware, to make free choices, to cooperate and to create that distinguishes a person as an individual. Definition A person is a holistic, self-developing biopsychosocial system with the capacity for awareness, free choice, learning, cooperation, and creativity. The DREVO philosophical model of New Psychology also views human development through the concepts of soul, spirit, values, and meaning as levels that define the individual's inner direction. The main goal of a person is not only to preserve his own life. The main goal is to realize one's potential, make a creative contribution to the lives of others, and leave behind a world healthier, fairer, wiser, and more harmonious than it was before one came. Below is a chapter that could become a central model.New Psychology DREVO. Ten levels of man Man as a multi-level system In the New Psychology DREVO, a person is viewed as a holistic living system consisting of ten interconnected levels. Each level performs its own function. None of them exist separately. Personal development occurs when all levels are in a state of harmony and support each other. I. Body Function:life and interaction with the material world. The body is the foundation of a person. It provides movement, metabolism, perception of the environment, restoration and biological existence. The main question: "How to preserve and strengthen life?" II. Subconscious Function:automatic life management. The subconscious is a deep system of biological and acquired programs. It includes innate mechanisms, habits, automatic reactions, bodily memory, adaptation and accumulated experience. The main question: "What experiences are already guiding my reactions?" III. Psyche Function:perception and processing of information. The psyche unites emotions, memory, thinking, imagination, attention and learning. It helps a person understand what is happening and adapt to the surrounding world. The main question: "What is happening around me and inside me?" IV. Consciousness Function:awareness and choice. Consciousness allows a person to observe himself, analyze what is happening and make informed decisions. It is consciousness that makes a person the author of his own life. The main question: "What do I choose?" V. Will Function:self-management. Willpower is the ability to control oneself and make conscious choices. It connects intention with action, helping people follow their values ​​even when it takes effort. The main question: "Am I able to implement my choice?" VI. Soul Function:the inner core of personality. In the DREVO philosophical model, the soul is the source of authenticity, love, conscience, beauty and deep values. She is responsible for the internal integrity of a person. The main question: "Who am I?" VII. Spirit Function:direction of development. The spirit determines the vector of a person’s life. It is associated with purpose, courage, responsibility and the desire to create. The main question: "What do I live for?" VIII. Values ​​and Meaning Function:internal compass. Values ​​help us distinguish between what is important and what is unimportant. Meaning unites all levels of personality into a single direction of life. The main question: "Why this particular path?" IX. Social Connections Function:joint development. A person reveals himself through relationships. Family. Genus. Community. Society. It is through cooperation that a person realizes a significant part of his potential. The main question: "Who am I growing with and what am I creating with others?" X. Interaction with the environment Function:the unity of man and the world. Humans constantly interact with nature, society, culture and technology. He not only receives the influence of the environment, but also changes it himself with his decisions and actions. The main question: “What world shapes me and what world do I create?” Unity of levels All ten levels form a single system. The body creates the basis of life. The subconscious stores experience. The psyche perceives the world. Consciousness makes a choice. Will turns choice into action. The soul retains its inner authenticity. The spirit determines the direction of development. Values ​​give meaning to life. Social connections allow a person to develop together with others. The environment creates conditions in which human potential is revealed. Violation of harmony at one level gradually affects the entire system. Therefore, the goal of the New Psychology DREVO is not to develop a single ability, but to harmoniously develop all ten levels of a person. The main principle A person becomes truly mature when all ten levels of his personality work in harmony, and his knowledge, values, and actions are aimed at the development of life, society, and future generations. Laws of personality development Introduction In the New Psychology DREVO, personal development is viewed as a natural process of revealing human potential. Just as a tree develops according to the laws of nature, a person develops according to certain psychological patterns. These laws are not physical laws of nature. They represent principles describing the most general conditions for the harmonious development of the individual. Understanding these laws helps a person consciously build their life, develop their abilities and create conditions for the development of other people. The First Law is the Law of Life Life strives for development. Every living organism has an innate ability to grow, adapt, and improve the way it interacts with its environment. Development is a natural state of man. When development stops, the loss of acquired abilities gradually begins. The Second Law is the Law of Integrity Everything is interconnected. The body influences the psyche. The psyche influences consciousness. Consciousness influences the will. Will influences actions. Actions change relationships. Relationships change society. Society influences a person. Therefore, development must occur harmoniously, and not only in one area of ​​life. The Third Law is the Law of Awareness A person can change only what he can understand. Mindfulness allows you to see your own thoughts, emotions, habits and beliefs. Without awareness, a person acts automatically. Awareness turns reaction into choice. The Fourth Law is the Law of Choice Every person constantly makes choices. Even refusing to make a decision is a choice. Each choice gradually shapes the direction of life. Human freedom is not manifested in the absence of restrictions, but in the ability to choose one's attitude and actions in existing circumstances. The Fifth Law is the Law of Will Choice becomes reality only through action. Will connects intention with action. Every promise fulfilled strengthens the will. Every refusal of one's own decision weakens the ability to control oneself. The Sixth Law is the Law of Habit Repeated actions become part of the personality. Thoughts turn into solutions. Decisions turn into actions. Actions become habits. Habits gradually shape character. Therefore, personality develops through daily practice.

title: The Seventh Law is the Law of Responsibility
excerpt: Freedom is impossible without responsibility. Every action has consequences. A mature person accepts responsibility not only for his own life, but also for the impact of his actions on other people and the world around h
text: Freedom is impossible without responsibility. Every action has consequences. A mature person accepts responsibility not only for his own life, but also for the impact of his actions on other people and the world around him. The Eighth Law is the Law of Cooperation A person develops through other people. Personality is revealed in family, community, culture and society. Knowledge sharing, collaboration, and mutual support accelerate the development of each participant. True development is impossible without respect for the dignity of another person. The Ninth Law is the Law of Creation The highest form of development is the ability to create. Creation manifests itself in different forms: raising children; scientific discoveries; art; technologies; entrepreneurship; education; helping people; restoration of nature. The more a person creates value for others, the more fully his potential is revealed. The Tenth Law is the Law of Heritage Real development continues after man. Every person leaves a trace behind. It can manifest itself in: knowledge; well-mannered people; family; created organizations; works of culture; scientific discoveries; restored nature; social changes. Heritage becomes a continuation of the individual over time. The main law of DREVO All previous laws are united by one principle. Personal development is harmonious when a person consciously reveals their abilities, strengthens their body, develops their psyche and consciousness, cultivates their will, remains true to their values, collaborates with other people, and directs the results of their labor toward the development of life. It is this path that transforms a person from a participant in the struggle for survival into a creator of the future. DREVO's development formula Awareness → Choice → Will → Action → Habit → Character → Creation → Heritage. This sequence shows that personal development begins with an internal understanding of oneself, progresses through daily actions, and culminates in a person's contribution to the lives of others and future generations. Part II. Human Architecture Man as a living multi-level system In the New Psychology of DREVO, a person is viewed as a holistic living system, in which each level performs its own function and simultaneously interacts with all the others. It is impossible to fully understand a person by looking only at the body, only at the brain, or only at behavior. Its development occurs due to the interaction of biological, psychological, social and ideological processes. Human architecture describes the internal structure of this system. It shows how thoughts are born, decisions are made, values ​​are formed, personality is revealed and human life is created. First level - Body The main question: What allows me to live? The body is the material basis of a person. It ensures life, movement, metabolism, perception of the surrounding world and interaction with the external environment. Through the body a person receives energy, sensations and experience. Without a healthy body, the full development of other levels of personality is impossible. The second level is the Subconscious The main question: What experience already guides me? The subconscious is a deep system of automatic processes of the body. It includes: innate programs; instincts; automatic skills; physical memory; emotional reactions; hereditary characteristics; formed habits. The subconscious helps a person react quickly without overloading the consciousness with constant analysis. The third level is the Psyche The main question: What's going on around me? The psyche perceives the surrounding world. She feels. Analyzes. Remembers. Compares. Imagines. Studying. It is the psyche that transforms the flow of information into personal experience. The fourth level is Consciousness The main question: What do I choose? Consciousness observes what is happening. It is capable of analyzing thoughts, feelings and actions. Consciousness makes free choice possible and allows a person to go beyond automatic reactions. Fifth level - Will The main question: Am I able to implement my choice? Will is a person's ability to control himself. It connects decision with action. Thanks to will, a person is able to follow his values ​​even when it requires effort. The sixth level is the Superconscious. The main question: What new opportunities are opening up for me? The superconscious is a space of creativity, inspiration, intuitive insights and the search for new solutions. In DREVO's New Psychology, the nature of the superconscious is viewed as an open area of ​​research, encompassing creative experience, subjective experiences, and questions that have not yet received a definitive scientific explanation. Seventh level - Soul The main question: Who am I? The soul is the inner core of the personality. It combines a sense of authenticity, love, conscience, the ability to empathize, the experience of beauty and deep values. Within the framework of DREVO, this is a philosophical concept that describes a person’s inner experience. Eighth level - Spirit The main question: What do I live for? The spirit determines the direction of personality development. It is associated with the will to create, the pursuit of ideals, the ability to remain true to one's beliefs and act for long-term goals. Level Nine – Values ​​and Meaning The main question: Why this particular path? Values ​​help us distinguish between good and evil, important and unimportant. Meaning unites all levels of personality into a single direction of life. It answers the question of why a person uses his abilities. Level Ten - Social Connections The main question: Who am I developing with? A person reveals himself through relationships. Family. Genus. Community. Society. Culture. Cooperation. Social connections create a space for mutual learning, support and joint development. Level Eleven - Interaction with Nature and the Environment The main question: What world do I live in and what world do I create? Man is a part of nature and at the same time creates an artificial environment. Nature, cities, culture and technology constantly influence his health, thinking and lifestyle. In turn, a person changes the world around him with his decisions. The twelfth level is the human biofield. The main question: How does the body interact with the environment at the physiological level? The human body creates bioelectrical and biomagnetic activity associated with the functioning of the heart, brain, nervous system and other organs. In New Psychology DREVO, the biofield is considered a physiological manifestation of the organism's vital activity and a promising direction for further research. Unified system Each level has its own purpose. The body creates the basis of life. The subconscious stores experience. The psyche perceives the world. Consciousness makes a choice. Will turns choice into action. The superconscious opens up new possibilities. The soul helps to maintain authenticity. The spirit sets the direction of development. Values ​​define meaning. Social connections allow a person to open up among people. The environment creates living conditions. The biofield reflects the physiological activity of the organism and its interaction with the outside world. All levels form a single system. A change in one level gradually affects all the others. The main principle Human architecture is like a tree. The body and the subconscious are the roots. Psyche, consciousness and will are the trunk. Superconsciousness, soul and spirit - the crown. Values ​​are the direction of growth. Social connections form a forest. Nature and the environment - soil, water, air and light. It is precisely through the coordinated work of all levels that a person becomes a holistic, free and creative individual. Body The body is the material basis of a person and the first level of conscious life. It is not a passive shell. The body is a complex, self-regulating living system that continuously perceives the surrounding world, processes information, and maintains life. In the new psychology, the body is seen as the bearer of its own biological wisdom. It has: ability to self-heal; innate development programs; adaptation mechanisms; memory of past experiences; a system of internal communication between organs, the nervous, immune and endocrine systems. The body constantly collects information from both the external and internal environment. It perceives: temperature; pressure; chemical composition of blood; hormone levels; position in space; condition of muscles and joints; pain; famine; thirst; fatigue; safety or danger. Most of these processes occur without the participation of consciousness. Therefore, the body can be considered as an independent system of perception and regulation. It is the body that creates the basis for the work of the subconscious mind. When the body is depleted, overloaded, or chronically inflamed, it impacts emotions, thinking, behavior, and decision-making. Taking care of your body is not only about physical health, but also the foundation of psychological well-being. In the new psychology, the body is seen not as a “machine,” but as a living partner of consciousness. Through breathing, movement, nutrition, sleep, touch and interaction with the environment, a person maintains a connection with his own nature. The main task of the body is to preserve life, maintain internal balance and create conditions for personal development. The body is the foundation of a person. Without a strong foundation, it is impossible to fully realize the potential of the subconscious, conscious, superconscious, soul, and spirit.

title: Subconscious
excerpt: The Subconscious in New Psychology DREVO In New Psychology DREVO, the subconscious is viewed as a deep system of automatic human control, combining the body's biological memory, acquired life experience, and adaptation m
text: The Subconscious in New Psychology DREVO In New Psychology DREVO, the subconscious is viewed as a deep system of automatic human control, combining the body's biological memory, acquired life experience, and adaptation mechanisms. The subconscious works continuously. It does not require constant participation of consciousness. It is thanks to the subconscious that a person is able to breathe, maintain balance, quickly respond to familiar situations, use acquired skills, and perform thousands of complex actions automatically. The subconscious is peculiar"the brain of the body", which continuously processes a huge amount of information necessary to maintain life and adapt the organism to the environment. What does the subconscious include? The subconscious combines several levels of accumulated experience. Biological memory The body stores information about its own development and ways of maintaining life. This includes self-regulation mechanisms, innate reflexes and processes that ensure the functioning of internal organs. Experience gained Repetitive actions gradually become automatic. The skills of walking, writing, speaking, driving a car and many other actions, after training, come under the control of the subconscious. Emotional memory The subconscious stores a person's emotional experience. It affects reaction speed, alertness level, sense of security and habitual behavior patterns. Hereditary features Modern science confirms the influence of heredity and some epigenetic mechanisms on human development. In the New Psychology of DREVO, it is assumed that the innate characteristics of the organism become part of the foundation on which automatic ways of human interaction with the world are formed. Bodily memory The body is capable of retaining the effects of long-term stress, habits, past illnesses, and physical experience. These processes manifest themselves in posture, muscle tone, breathing, movement patterns, and other features of the body's functioning. How does the subconscious work? The subconscious constantly compares new information with already accumulated experience. If the situation is familiar, it offers a ready-made response.
