Five levels of responsibility The first level is responsibility for the body A person cares about his health. Understands that his lifestyle affects the quality of his future. The second level is responsibility for the psyche A person learns to understand his emotions. Doesn't shift them entirely onto other people. Looks for ways to constructively cope with stress and worries. The third level is responsibility for actions The man keeps his promises. Admits mistakes. Corrects the consequences of his actions, if possible. He does not justify himself by circumstances where he could have acted differently. The fourth level is responsibility for relationships A person understands that trust is built through actions. He is responsible for his words. Respects the dignity of other people. Strives to maintain cooperation and honesty. The fifth level is responsibility for the future The highest form of responsibility manifests itself when a person thinks not only about himself. He asks questions: How will my decisions affect the children? To society? To nature? For future generations? This is where personal responsibility becomes responsibility to life. What hinders responsibility? Responsibility is weakened by: the habit of blaming others; search for excuses; shifting decisions onto others; fear of admitting a mistake; passivity; the belief that "nothing depends on me." Such attitudes gradually deprive a person of inner strength. Responsibility and freedom Freedom without responsibility turns into arbitrariness. Responsibility without freedom becomes coercion. A mature personality combines freedom of choice with a willingness to take responsibility for the consequences of that choice. Responsibility and creation Every creative project begins with responsibility. For the quality of your work. For the people. For resources. For promises. For long-term consequences. The more responsibility a person has, the more trust he inspires. And trust becomes the basis for cooperation. Practice of the Law of Responsibility Every evening it is useful to ask yourself the following questions: What depended on me today? Which decisions were really mine? Have I kept my promises? If I made a mistake, what can I do to correct it? What action did I take today that made me a more mature person? This practice gradually turns responsibility into a natural character trait. The main principle Responsibility does not limit freedom. It makes freedom creative. A person becomes stronger not when he gains more power over others. He becomes stronger when he learns to manage his own life. Definition The Law of Responsibility is a fundamental law of the New Psychology DREVO, according to which personal development is determined by a person's willingness to accept responsibility for their thoughts, decisions, actions, their consequences, and their own development. Responsibility is the foundation of maturity, trust, and inner freedom. It is what transforms knowledge into action, freedom into creativity, and personal life into a source of benefit for society and future generations. Responsibility is the moment when a person stops expecting the world to change on its own and begins to ask, "What depends on me today?" It is with this question that true personal growth begins. The Law of Harmony The Law of Harmony in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, harmony is not seen as the absence of difficulties or a constant feeling of peace. Harmony is a state of coordinated development of all aspects of the personality and its interaction with the surrounding world. A person becomes harmonious not when his life becomes ideal. He becomes harmonious when his body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, relationships and lifestyle begin to support each other. Harmony is balance in movement. What is the Law of Harmony? The law of harmony is a fundamental principle according to which the sustainable development of the individual, society and nature is possible only with the coordinated interaction of all elements of the system. If one part develops at the expense of another, over time the stability of the entire system is disrupted. Harmony begins within Inner harmony arises when a person lives in accordance with his values. He is not torn between what he thinks, says and does. His thoughts. His words. His actions. His goals in life. They do not contradict each other. It is precisely internal harmony that becomes the source of psychological stability. Harmony of the ten levels of man The law of harmony manifests itself in the coordinated development of all levels of personality. Bodygives energy. Subconsciousforms useful habits. Psychehelps to understand and regulate emotions. Consciousnessallows us to understand the world. Will turns decisions into actions. Soulreveals love, conscience and beauty. Spiritsets the direction of life. Valuesdetermine life guidelines. Social connectionscreate a space of trust and cooperation. Interaction with naturereminds a person that he is part of a single life. Harmony arises when none of these levels develops at the expense of the destruction of the others. Harmony in relationships A person cannot be completely happy alone. Harmonious relationships are built on: respect; trust; freedom; responsibility; mutual support; honesty. Harmony does not mean the absence of conflict. It means the ability to resolve them without destroying relationships. Harmony with nature Man is a part of nature. Therefore, environmental destruction inevitably affects the quality of human life. Caring for nature becomes caring for man himself. Harmony with nature does not mean rejecting the development of technology. It is a search for a development that preserves life. Harmony and development Harmony does not mean stopping. All living things develop. It's changing. Adapts. True harmony lies in the ability to maintain inner balance during times of change. Like a tree that grows every year, remaining the same. What destroys harmony? The harmony is gradually being disturbed: extremes; constant internal conflict; life contrary to one's values; chronic stress; destructive addictions; neglect of health; isolation from people; loss of meaning in life. Harmony is gradually lost. And it is also being restored gradually. Practice of the Law of Harmony Every day it is useful to ask yourself: Did I take care of my body today? Did you maintain inner peace? Were my actions consistent with my values? Did I pay attention to my loved ones? Have you created anything useful today? Did you spend time in nature? Was today a harmonious day? These questions help to gradually build a holistic life. The main principle Harmony does not mean equal development of all aspects of life. It means their consistency. When one part of the personality grows, helping others grow, a person becomes stronger, happier and freer. Definition The Law of Harmony is a fundamental law of the New Psychology DREVO, according to which sustainable personal development is achieved through the coordinated development of the body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, values, relationships, and interaction with nature. Harmony is not an end goal, but a way of life. It is born when a person's inner world, actions, and relationships with the outside world cease to contradict each other and begin to function as a unified system. Like a tree, in which the roots, trunk, branches, leaves and fruits do not exist separately, but support each other, a person becomes truly harmonious when all aspects of his personality are united into a single direction of life.

title: The Law of Overcoming
excerpt: The Law of Overcoming in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, development is impossible without overcoming. All living things face obstacles. The seed overcomes the thickness of the earth. The tree can wi
text: The Law of Overcoming in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, development is impossible without overcoming. All living things face obstacles. The seed overcomes the thickness of the earth. The tree can withstand the wind. The river goes around the stones. A person develops by overcoming his own limitations and life’s difficulties. Difficulties in themselves do not make a person stronger. What makes him stronger is how he responds to them. It is overcoming that transforms experience into maturity. What is the Law of Overcoming? The Law of Overcoming is a fundamental principle according to which personal development occurs through consciously overcoming internal and external obstacles, leading to increased strength, wisdom, freedom and maturity. An obstacle is not only a test. This is an opportunity for development. Why are difficulties necessary? If a person never encounters resistance, many of his abilities remain untapped. It is difficulties that help develop: will; patience; responsibility; courage; creativity; ability to cooperate. Overcoming becomes a natural part of development. What needs to be overcome? First of all, a person overcomes himself. Your fears. Laziness. Uncertainty. Destructive habits. Impulsive reactions. Limiting beliefs. Often the main obstacle is not the outside world, but internal limitations. Overcoming and the Ten Levels of Man Each level of personality has its own challenges. Body- fatigue, illness, the need to take care of health. Subconscious- changing bad habits. Psyche- managing fear, anxiety, anger and despair. Consciousness- overcoming misconceptions, stereotypes and self-deception. Will- choosing the right one, not the easy one. Soul- maintaining love and humanity even after pain and disappointment. Spirit- fidelity to one's path in times of uncertainty. Values- the ability to not change one's principles for the sake of immediate gain. Social connections- the ability to forgive, cooperate and resolve conflicts. Interaction with nature- respect for the laws of life and the ability to live in harmony with the surrounding world. What prevents you from overcoming? Development is slowed down by: fear of failure; striving for constant comfort; the habit of blaming circumstances; expecting problems to go away on their own; refusal to learn from mistakes. Every avoidance of difficulty often makes future difficulties greater. How to overcome difficulties correctly? In New Psychology DREVO recommends: accept the existence of the problem; keep calm; break a large task into small steps; seek knowledge and help; don't stop after the first failures; perceive mistakes as a source of experience; remember your values ​​and purpose. Overcoming is not a fight at any cost. This is a conscious movement forward. Overcoming and happiness Happiness does not come after all difficulties disappear. It appears when a person feels that he is able to go through them with dignity. Inner strength does not come from the absence of challenges. It is born from the experience of overcoming them. Practice of the Law of Overcoming Every evening it is useful to ask yourself the following questions: What was the hardest thing today? What have I overcome? What did this trial teach me? Which of my inner strengths has become a little stronger? What's the next step I'll take tomorrow? These questions help turn difficulties into a source of development. The main principle Obstacles do not always stand in a person's way. Very often they are the way. Every challenge overcome makes a person stronger, wiser and freer. Overcoming is seen not as a struggle against life, but as a natural process of development. Every challenge becomes an opportunity to strengthen the body, psyche, will, spirit, and the ability to create goodness even in difficult circumstances. Just as a tree grows stronger through resistance to the wind, a person grows stronger through the difficulties he goes through with dignity, awareness and fidelity to his values. Law of Cooperation The Law of Cooperation in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, cooperation is considered one of the fundamental laws of life. Life develops not only thanks to competition. It develops primarily through interaction. Cells form an organism. The organs work together. Trees unite into a forest. Bees create a hive. People build families, communities and civilizations. The higher the level of development of life, the more complex and deeper cooperation becomes. Therefore, the ability to cooperate is one of the main signs of a mature personality. What is the Law of Cooperation? The law of cooperation is a fundamental principle according to which the sustainable development of the individual, society, and civilization is achieved through voluntary interaction based on trust, mutual respect, knowledge sharing, and joint creation. Collaboration does not cancel out individuality. It helps her to open up. Why is cooperation stronger than loneliness? One person can do a lot. But the capabilities of any person are limited. When different knowledge, talents and experiences come together, something emerges that cannot be created alone. This phenomenon can be called collective creation. Each person retains his own uniqueness. But together people are capable of creating new qualities of the system.

title: The basis of cooperation
excerpt: This cooperation is built on five principles. Trust Without trust, long-term interaction is impossible. It is created by honesty, consistency and keeping promises. Respect Every person has dignity, knowledge and experien
text: This cooperation is built on five principles. Trust Without trust, long-term interaction is impossible. It is created by honesty, consistency and keeping promises. Respect Every person has dignity, knowledge and experience. Respect allows you to see the value of another person even when your views differ. Voluntariness True cooperation cannot be achieved through coercion. It is born from free choice. Common goal People are able to unite when they understand why they are acting together. A common goal unites different abilities into a single direction. Mutual benefit Healthy collaboration creates value for all participants. It is not built on exploitation. It is built on joint development. Cooperation and personal development The ability to collaborate requires development: empathy; communication; responsibility; listening skills; ability to negotiate; willingness to share knowledge; conflict resolution skills. Thus, cooperation becomes a school of maturity. The Law of Cooperation and the Ten Levels of Man Cooperation manifests itself at all levels of personality. Body— joint work and mutual care help maintain health. Subconscious— joint activities form useful habits. Psyche— support from other people strengthens emotional resilience. Consciousness— knowledge sharing accelerates learning. Will— shared commitments help maintain discipline. Soul- Cooperation develops love, compassion and gratitude. Spirit— common values ​​unite people around creative goals. Social connections— become a space of trust and mutual assistance. Nature— shows many examples of interdependence and cooperation of living systems. What destroys cooperation? It is weakened by: lie; egoism; arrogance; distrust; inability to listen; the desire to use people; constant competition for superiority. When trust disappears, cooperation breaks down. Practice of the Law of Cooperation It is useful to ask yourself questions every day: Who did I help today? Who did I learn something from today? Did our overall results improve as a result of working together? Do I create trust through my actions? What can I do tomorrow to make our collaboration stronger? Such questions gradually form a culture of co-creation. The main principle Personal development does not end with one's own success. True maturity is demonstrated when a person is able to combine his or her abilities with those of other people for the common good. Definition The Law of Cooperation is a fundamental law of the New Psychology of DREVO, according to which the most sustainable development of the individual, society, and civilization is achieved through the voluntary unification of people based on trust, respect, a common goal, and joint creation. Collaboration is seen as a natural law of life, allowing each person to unlock their potential and create results greater than the sum of their individual efforts. A single tree can provide shade for one person. A forest can change the climate of an entire region. So it is with people: by pooling their knowledge, labor, and goodwill, they create a future that cannot be built alone. The Law of Psychological Ecology The Law of Psychological Ecology in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, the psyche is viewed as a living ecosystem. Just as nature needs clean water, healthy soil, and clean air, the human psyche needs a healthy information environment, harmonious relationships, adequate rest, and a meaningful life. Psychological health cannot be maintained if a person’s inner world is constantly exposed to destructive influences. Therefore, caring for the psyche becomes as natural a necessity as caring for the body. What is the Law of Psychological Ecology? The law of psychological ecology is a fundamental principle according to which a person's psychological health depends on the quality of their internal and external environment, and harmonious development requires conscious care for the purity of thoughts, emotions, relationships, information, and lifestyle. A person constantly interacts with his psychological environment. And this environment gradually shapes his personality. Internal ecology The inner world of a person consists of: thoughts; emotions; beliefs; habits; memories; values; internal dialogue. If the inner space is constantly filled with fear, hatred, lies or self-destruction, the psyche gradually loses stability. Therefore, caring for the inner world becomes a daily practice. External ecology of the psyche The psyche is constantly influenced by: family; Friends; work environment; culture; books; music; social media; news; nature; architecture of the surrounding space. A person develops in the environment in which he lives. Therefore, it is important not only to change yourself, but also to create a healthy space around you. Seven Sources of Psychological Ecology Body A good night's sleep. Movement. Healthy eating. Physical health supports mental resilience. Information Quality knowledge. Critical thinking. Limiting information noise. Conscious selection of information sources. Emotions The ability to understand and experience feelings. Don't suppress them. But don't let them completely control your life. Relationship Love. Friendship. Trust. Support. A person remains psychologically more stable when around people he can trust. Nature Living world helps restore focus, reduce stress levels and restore a sense of inner balance. Creative activity Work. Creativity. Training. Helping others. Creation strengthens psychological resilience because it fills life with meaning. Inner meaning When a person understands why he lives, it is easier for him to endure difficulties. Meaning becomes an internal source of stability. What pollutes the psyche? Psychological ecology is violated by: chronic stress; constant fear; information overload; lie; aggressive environment; dependencies; lack of rest; destructive relationships; life without meaning. Like environmental pollution, psychological pollution rarely occurs instantly. It accumulates gradually. How to maintain psychological ecology? In New Psychology DREVO recommends: maintain a sleep schedule; be outdoors regularly; limit information noise; develop critical thinking; maintain healthy relationships; engage in physical activity; devote time daily to silence and reflection; keep self-observation diaries; develop gratitude; create a space of beauty and order around you. Psychological ecology is not a one-time measure. It's a way of life. Psychological ecology and society The psychological health of an individual is linked to the state of society. Culture of communication. Education. Trust. Justice. Safety. All this affects people's mental well-being. Therefore, caring for psychological ecology becomes a task not only for the individual, but also for the family, community, state, and civilization. The main principle A person becomes similar to the environment in which he lives. Therefore, while caring about the purity of his inner world and the environment, he simultaneously cares about his future. Definition The Law of Psychological Ecology is a fundamental law of the New Psychology DREVO, according to which psychological health and harmonious development of the individual depend on the quality of the internal and external environment, and their preservation requires conscious care of thoughts, emotions, relationships, information, lifestyle, and the surrounding environment. Psychological ecology is viewed as a continuous process of maintaining conditions in which a person is able to maintain internal stability, develop, cooperate and create. Just as clean soil allows a tree to grow strong, a healthy psychological environment allows a person to reveal their best qualities. By caring for their inner ecology, a person cultivates not only their own happiness but also the future of society. The Law of Creation The Law of Creation in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, creation is considered the highest form of realization of human potential. Every person is capable of consuming. Everyone is capable of destruction. But only a mature personality consciously creates something new. Creation is a natural continuation of development. When a person reveals his abilities, he begins to transform the world around him. It creates knowledge. Relationship. Projects. Beauty. Technologies. Culture. Future. It is through creation that man becomes an active participant in the evolution of life. What is the Law of Creation? The Law of Creation is a fundamental principle that states that personal development reaches its full potential when a person begins to use their knowledge, abilities, and resources to create value that benefits other people, society, nature, and future generations. Creation is a natural expression of maturity. Why does man strive to create? Every person has a need to leave a mark. To create something greater than himself. This could be: child; book; painting; now; scientific discovery; invention; community; business; good deed; an idea that changed the lives of other people. Creation gives life depth and meaning.

title: Creation begins with personality
excerpt: It is impossible to create a stable external world if the internal world is in ruins. Therefore, man's first creation is himself. It creates: your character; your habits; your worldview; your culture of communication. Pe
text: It is impossible to create a stable external world if the internal world is in ruins. Therefore, man's first creation is himself. It creates: your character; your habits; your worldview; your culture of communication. Personality becomes the main work of a person. Seven levels of creation Self-creation Development of body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul and spirit. Building relationships Love. Friendship. Family. Trust. Creation of knowledge Training. Research. Transfer of experience. Teaching. Creation of labor Useful work. Craft. Entrepreneurship. Engineering. Science. Creation of culture Music. Art. Language. Traditions. Beauty. Building a society Communities. Education. Social projects. Cooperation. Creating the future Ecology. Raising children. New technologies. Caring for future generations. What destroys creation? Creation is hindered by: indifference; constant consumption without return; fear of mistakes; envy; destructive thinking; refusal to take responsibility; lack of long-term goals. Destruction often occurs faster than creation. But it is creation that ensures the sustainable development of life. Creation and happiness A person rarely experiences deep satisfaction from consumption alone. The most lasting feeling of fulfillment arises when a person sees the results of his labor and understands that his activity is beneficial. Therefore, creation becomes one of the main sources of happiness. Practice of the Law of Creation Every day it is useful to ask yourself: What new did I create today? Who did it benefit? What has become better thanks to my actions? What skills did I develop today? What contribution have I made to the future? Even a small creative act gradually changes personality. The main principle Life develops through creation. A person discovers his purpose not when he only takes from the world, but when he begins to give and create something. Definition The Law of Creation is a fundamental law of the New Psychology DREVO, according to which the highest form of personal development is manifested in the ability to create values ​​that contribute to the development of man, society, nature, and future generations. Creation is a natural extension of awareness, will, responsibility, and cooperation. It transforms a person's inner potential into real change in the world and makes their life a source of benefit and legacy. Like a tree that draws strength from the earth not for itself, but to grow its crown, provide shade, fruit, and new seeds, a person reaches maturity when he begins to create more life than he consumes. The Law of Destiny The Law of Purpose in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, purpose is not seen as a predetermined fate or as the only “ideal profession”. Purpose is the direction in which a person most fully reveals his abilities, realizes his values ​​and brings the greatest benefit to life. It is not found by chance. It is gradually revealed through personal development, experience, choice and creative activity. Purpose is the path that a person builds through his actions. What is the Law of Destiny? The Law of Purpose is a fundamental principle according to which the harmonious development of an individual occurs when their abilities, values, interests, and activities are combined into a creative direction that benefits the individual, society, and future generations. Purpose answers not only the question: "What do I do?" It answers the question: "What do I live for?" The purpose is revealed gradually Many people expect a sudden epiphany. But more often than not, the purpose becomes clearer step by step. Through training. Through mistakes. Through new projects. Through service to people. Through experience. Each stage of life opens a new part of the path. Therefore, purpose is a process of unfolding, not a one-time discovery. Four Components of Purpose Capabilities What am I best at? What talents can I develop? Values What is really important to me? What principles do I want to remain true to? Benefit How can my knowledge and abilities make other people's lives better? The joy of creation What activities fill me with energy and a sense of meaning even when they require effort? When these four elements come together, a person begins to feel his direction. What prevents you from finding your purpose? Often a person is disturbed by: fear of making a mistake; the desire to meet other people's expectations; living only for material gain; lack of self-knowledge; passivity; refusal to try new things. Purpose is not revealed to one who does nothing. It is revealed in activity. The Purpose and Ten Levels of Man Purpose unites all levels of personality. Bodygives strength to act. Subconsciouscreates habits that support the path. Psychehelps maintain stability. Consciousnessallows you to understand the world and learn. Will helps not to stop. Soulfills activities with love and sincerity. Spiritmaintains direction even in difficult times. Valuesdetermine the meaning of the path. Social connectionshelp to realize one's destiny together with other people. Naturereminds that human activity should support life, not destroy it. Purpose and profession Profession can be part of destiny. But it does not always coincide with it. The same doctor can treat people only for the sake of earning money or see his work as a service to life. The same engineer can simply carry out tasks or create technologies that change the future. Purpose is determined not by the name of the profession, but by the meaning that a person puts into his or her activities. Practice asked for purposes It is useful to regularly ask yourself questions: What do I like to do? What am I best at? What do people thank me for? What problems in the world do I want to solve? What am I willing to do even when it's difficult? What do I want to leave behind? The answers gradually take shape into a direction for life. The main principle Purpose does not come to a person from outside. It is revealed when a person develops, acts and begins to use his abilities for the benefit of life. Definition The Law of Purpose is a fundamental law of the New Psychology DREVO, according to which a person achieves the greatest fullness of development when he or she reveals his or her abilities, lives in accordance with his or her values, and uses his or her potential for creation and service to life. Purpose is the natural result of harmonious personal development. It connects a person's inner potential with the needs of the world, transforming personal success into a long-term contribution to the development of society and future generations. Like a tree that does not choose whether to bear fruit, but reveals its nature through growth, a person reveals his purpose when he becomes what he is capable of being and begins to benefit everything around him. Law of Inheritance The Law of Inheritance in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, human development does not end with personal achievements. The highest stage of maturity is the creation of a legacy. Every person receives something from previous generations: life; language; culture; knowledge; experience; nature; society. But life reaches its fullness when a person begins not only to receive, but also to transmit. Thus, he becomes a link between the past and the future. What is the Law of Inheritance? The Law of Legacy is a fundamental principle that holds that the true value of life is determined by what a person leaves behind and what continues to benefit people, nature, and future generations. Heritage is the natural culmination of a creative life. The legacy begins today Many people think that legacy is created at the end of life. In fact, it is born every day. Every decision. Every action. Every word. Every student. Every tree planted. Every idea conveyed. Every completed project becomes a part of the future. Seven Forms of Heritage Biological heritage Children. Health of future generations. Continuation of life. Moral heritage Honesty. Love. Responsibility. Personal example. Culture of behavior. Intellectual heritage Books. Research. Inventions. Knowledge. Teaching. Creative legacy Projects. Organizations. Enterprises. Architecture. Technologies. Works of art. Social heritage Created communities. Culture of cooperation. Trust. Traditions of mutual assistance. Environmental heritage Planted forests. Restored ecosystems. Preserved natural resources. Careful attitude towards life. Spiritual heritage Wisdom. Philosophy. Ideas. Inspiration. The meaning of life. Something that helps other people become better. Heritage and Purpose Purpose answers the question: "What do I live for?" Heritage responds: "What will live because of me?" When a person connects these two issues, his life begins to go beyond personal success. Legacy and Immortality In the New Psychology of DREVO, immortality is understood not only as a philosophical or religious idea. It manifests itself in the continuation of human influence. People continue to live: in your children; in students; in the created culture; in knowledge; in good deeds; in projects; in a changed nature; in the lives of those they helped. Thus, heritage becomes an extension of the individual.

title: What destroys heritage?
excerpt: The creation of a legacy is hindered by: life only for one's own consumption; indifference; refusal to transfer knowledge; destructive attitude towards people and nature; the pursuit of short-term gain at any cost; lack
text: The creation of a legacy is hindered by: life only for one's own consumption; indifference; refusal to transfer knowledge; destructive attitude towards people and nature; the pursuit of short-term gain at any cost; lack of long-term thinking. A person can leave behind both a constructive and a destructive legacy. Therefore, responsibility for the legacy begins today. Practice of the Law of Inheritance It is useful to regularly ask yourself questions: What will remain after me? What will be better because of my life? What knowledge will I impart? What kind of people will I help raise? Which projects can survive without my participation? What future am I creating with my actions today? These questions help you look beyond your own life. The main principle The true greatness of a man is not determined by how much he has accumulated. It is determined by how much life, goodness, knowledge, beauty and opportunity continues to exist because of it. Definition The Law of Heritage is a fundamental law of the New Psychology of DREVO, according to which the highest form of personal development is the creation of a tangible and intangible legacy that continues to benefit people, society, nature, and future generations. Heritage becomes the natural outcome of a conscious, responsible, and creative life. It connects the past, present, and future, allowing people to become part of the continuous development of human civilization. Like a tree that does not live for its own fruit, but leaves behind new seeds, shade and fertile soil, a person reaches the highest maturity when his life continues to be useful even after his departure. Law of exchange The Law of Exchange in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, life is viewed as a continuous process of exchange. Nothing living exists entirely by itself. The body exchanges substances and energy. Plants exchange gases with the atmosphere. People exchange knowledge, experience, emotions, labor, culture and care. Development becomes possible through exchange. When exchange ceases, life gradually fades away. What is the Law of Exchange? The Law of Exchange is a fundamental principle according to which sustainable development of individuals, society, and nature occurs through the mutual exchange of knowledge, energy, labor, resources, experience, care, and responsibility. Exchange is the basis of cooperation and development. Life exists through exchange Every person constantly receives: air; water; food; knowledge; language; culture; Love; help from other people. At the same time, a person is able to give: your work; knowledge; time; attention; support; creativity; care; experience. Life becomes fulfilling when receiving and giving are in reasonable balance. Types of exchange Biological exchange Breath. Nutrition. Metabolism. The basis of physical life. Emotional exchange Support. Love. Trust. Gratitude. Emotions are transmitted from person to person and influence the psychological atmosphere. Intellectual exchange Training. Teaching. Research. Collaborative search for knowledge. The more people share knowledge, the faster society develops. Social sharing Joint work. Mutual assistance. Economy. Voluntary cooperation. Everyone makes their contribution and receives the results of joint activities. Cultural exchange Passing on traditions. Arts. Language. Stories. Culture develops through constant exchange between generations and peoples. Spiritual and moral exchange Good deeds. Inspiration. Wisdom. Service. These forms of exchange cannot be measured in material terms, but they are often the ones that change people's lives the most. Violation of the Law of Exchange The exchange is disrupted when a person: only takes and gives nothing; or constantly gives away, completely forgetting about his own health and recovery. Both extremes destroy harmony. Healthy exchange is based on reciprocity and respect. The Law of Exchange and the Ten Levels of Man Each level of personality participates in the exchange. Body— metabolism and energy. Subconscious- exchange of habits through imitation and learning. Psyche— exchange of emotions and mood. Consciousness— exchange of knowledge and ideas. Will— exchange of trust through fulfilling promises. Soul— exchange of love, beauty and kindness. Spirit— exchange of meaning and inspiration. Values— exchange of culture and moral principles. Social connections— exchange of assistance, experience and cooperation. Nature— continuous exchange between a person and the surrounding world. Practice of the Law of Exchange Every evening it is useful to ask yourself the following questions: What useful things did I get today? What useful thing have I given away today? Is the world a little better because of my actions? Have I lost the balance between caring for others and caring for myself? What can I convey to people tomorrow? Questions like these help maintain a healthy exchange with life. The main principle Life does not develop through accumulation. It develops through movement. That which circulates freely sustains life. What is constantly kept only for oneself gradually loses value. Definition The Law of Exchange is a fundamental law of the New Psychology DREVO, according to which the development of man, society, and nature occurs through the continuous mutual exchange of resources, knowledge, experience, labor, emotions, culture, and care. Exchange is seen as a natural mechanism of life, uniting people, strengthening cooperation, and creating conditions for shared development. Harmony is achieved when a person is able not only to receive but also to consciously give, maintaining a balance between personal well-being and contribution to the world around them. Just as a tree receives water and sunlight and then gives off oxygen, shade, fruits and seeds, a person becomes a part of life when he learns to turn everything he receives into benefit for others. The law of growth The Law of Growth in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, growth is seen as a natural property of life. All living things strive for development. The seed becomes a tree. The child becomes an adult. Knowledge becomes wisdom. Experience becomes maturity. Life cannot remain unchanged for long. It either develops. Or it gradually loses its capabilities. Therefore, growth is one of the fundamental laws of life. What is the Law of Growth? The law of growth is a fundamental principle according to which a person, like all living things, has a natural desire for development, and his personality is revealed through the continuous improvement of his abilities, character, relationships and life purpose. Growth is a natural state of life. Growth begins within Real growth doesn't begin with external achievements. It starts with internal changes. Thinking is changing. Habits change. Values ​​are changing. Actions change. It is the inner growth that gradually changes the outer life. Growth takes time In nature, it is impossible to accelerate the growth of a tree tenfold without consequences. A person develops in the same way. Real growth requires: time; patience; regular practice; errors; experience. Trying to get quick results often leads to superficial development. Human growth and ten levels Every level of personality has the potential to grow. Bodybecomes stronger through movement and care. Subconsciousdevelops through new healthy habits. Psychelearns resilience. Consciousnessexpands knowledge and understanding of the world. Will is strengthened through discipline. Soulis revealed through love, creativity and compassion. Spiritbecomes stronger through fidelity to purpose. Valuesbecome deeper through life experience. Social connectionsdevelop through trust and cooperation. Interaction with naturehelps a person feel part of life. Growth becomes harmonious only when the whole personality develops. What hinders growth? Growth is slowed down by: fear of change; striving for constant comfort; the belief that “I already know everything”; refusal to study; life without goals; lack of practice; fear of mistakes. The biggest obstacle is often not a lack of ability, but a cessation of development. How does growth occur? Growth goes through several stages. Awareness. The person understands the need for change. ↓ Training. Gains new knowledge. ↓ Practice. It's starting to work. ↓ Repetition. Forms habits. ↓ Mastery. New qualities become a natural part of the personality. ↓ Transfer of experience. A person begins to help others develop. It is the transfer of knowledge that becomes the pinnacle of one’s own growth. Growth and mistakes Mistakes are part of development. It is not the mistake that hinders growth. Growth stops when a person stops drawing conclusions. Every mistake becomes a new step if it turns into experience. Practice of the Law of Growth Every evening it is useful to ask yourself: What new things did I learn today? Which of my abilities has become stronger? What have today's difficulties taught me? What kind of person have I become today compared to yesterday? What will be the next step in my development? These questions help us see growth even in small changes. The main principle Growth never ends. As long as a person is able to learn, love, create and share experiences, his development continues. Definition The Law of Growth is a fundamental law of the New Psychology DREVO, according to which life naturally strives for development, and a person reveals their potential through the continuous improvement of the body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, relationships, and creative activity. Growth is not a one-time event, but a way of life. It occurs gradually, through learning, practice, overcoming challenges, and accumulating experience, transforming a person's potential into maturity, wisdom, and legacy. Like a tree that imperceptibly adds new rings each year, a person grows not through one great event, but through thousands of daily steps. True growth is impossible to see in a single day, but it is precisely this growth that, over time, changes a person's entire life.

title: The Law of Service
excerpt: The Law of Service in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, service is seen as the highest form of personal maturity. Development begins with taking care of yourself. Continues through family developme
text: The Law of Service in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, service is seen as the highest form of personal maturity. Development begins with taking care of yourself. Continues through family development. It is revealed in cooperation with society. And it reaches fullness when a person begins to use his abilities to serve life. Service does not mean self-sacrifice or self-denial. It means the conscious use of one's knowledge, talent, experience and work for the common good. What is the Law of Service? The law of service is a fundamental principle according to which a person reaches the highest level of development when he uses his abilities and opportunities for creation, helping other people, developing society, preserving nature and the well-being of future generations. Service does not mean giving up personal happiness. This is its extension. What does it mean to serve? To serve is to create value. It is not necessary to perform great feats. Service is demonstrated in daily life. The doctor serves by maintaining people's health. A teacher serves by imparting knowledge. An engineer serves by creating useful technologies. A farmer serves by growing food. Parents serve by raising their children. Every person is capable of serving through his own work. Service begins with oneself You can't help others for long while completely destroying yourself. Therefore, the first service is the development of one’s own personality. Healthy body. Stable psyche. Clear consciousness. Strong will. An open soul. Strengthened spirit. The stronger a person is, the more good he can bring to the world. Service and the Ten Levels of Man Each level of personality participates in service. Bodygives strength to help. Subconsciousforms habits of care and responsibility. Psychedevelops empathy and the ability to support others. Consciousnessallows you to find useful solutions. Will helps to translate good intentions into action. Soulgives birth to love, compassion and sincerity. Spiritreminds us that life has a meaning beyond personal gain. Valuesdetermine the moral direction of actions. Social connectionsallow us to combine efforts for a common cause. Naturebecomes an object of care, and not just a source of resources. What is not service? Service does not mean: denial of one's own needs; life of constant self-sacrifice; the desire to earn love at any cost; blind obedience; renunciation of personal freedom. True service is always voluntary. It preserves the dignity of both the one who helps and the one who receives help. What hinders service? The development of the ministry is hindered by: egoism; indifference; the desire to live only for one's own comfort; the belief that one person cannot change anything; lack of a sense of responsibility for the world. Every person is capable of changing at least a small part of the life around them. Practice of the Law of Service Every evening it is useful to ask yourself: Who did I help today? What benefit did my work bring? What has become better thanks to my actions? Did I use my abilities for good? How can I make the world a little better tomorrow? These questions gradually make service a natural part of life. The main principle True success is not measured solely by what a person has achieved. It is measured by how much life, goodness, knowledge, health, beauty and opportunity has come into being through its existence. Definition The Law of Service is a fundamental law of the New Psychology DREVO, according to which the highest form of personal development is manifested in the voluntary use of one's abilities, knowledge, and resources for creation, helping people, developing society, preserving nature, and caring for future generations. Service is a natural extension of awareness, responsibility, cooperation, and creativity. It allows a person to transcend personal interests and become an active participant in the unfolding of life. Like a tree that doesn't choose who to give shade or fruit to, a mature person naturally shares what has grown within them. This is precisely the highest form of human strength—the ability to transform one's own life into a source of life for others. Causes of psychological problems The basic principle In the New Psychology DREVO, a psychological problem is not considered as a separate illness of the personality, but asviolation of harmony between human levels. A person is a single system. When one or more of its levels lose coherence, internal conflicts, emotional tension, behavioral disturbances and deterioration in quality of life arise. A psychological problem is not a person’s enemy. This is a signal that a certain part of the system needs attention, restoration or development. The main causes of psychological problems 1. Disconnection from the body Lack of sleep. Chronic fatigue. Malnutrition. Lack of movement. Chronic pain. Hormonal and other diseases. When the body is exhausted, the psyche and consciousness also lose stability. 2. Disruption of the subconscious Automatic reactions formed by traumatic experiences. Destructive habits. Chronic fear. Unprocessed emotional experiences. The subconscious continues to protect a person even when previous methods of protection no longer help. 3. Mental conflict A person wants opposite things at the same time. For example: freedom and complete security; closeness and complete independence; change and maintaining the familiar. Unresolved internal contradictions create long-term tension. 4. Loss of awareness When a person stops noticing his own thoughts, feelings and actions, he begins to live automatically. Automatism gradually deprives a person of freedom of choice. 5. Weakening of the will The person knows what needs to be done, but is unable to implement his decision. A feeling of powerlessness gradually arises. 6. Loss of meaning When a person ceases to understand why he lives and develops, even familiar things can lose their inner value. This may be accompanied by feelings of emptiness, apathy and loss of motivation. 7. Conflict of values Suffering occurs when a person is forced to live contrary to his own beliefs or constantly acts against his conscience. The deeper this conflict, the greater the internal tension. 8. Disruption of social connections Loneliness. Distrust. Destructive relationships. Lack of support. Insulation. A person develops through relationships. Therefore, the destruction of social connections weakens psychological resilience. 9. Unfavorable environment Constant noise. Information overload. Aggressive social environment. Lack of contact with nature. Environmental issues. The environment gradually becomes part of a person’s inner world. 10. Violation of psychological ecology Every day a person takes in a huge amount of information. If a large part of it consists of fear, aggression, lies, humiliation, manipulation and constant stress, internal balance is gradually disturbed. The psyche needs not only protection from physical threats, but also a healthy information environment. Compensation principle When one level of a person weakens, other levels often try to compensate for its work. For example: the body can signal with pain; emotions - anxiety; behavior - addiction; relationships - conflicts. Therefore, symptoms should be viewed not only as a problem, but also as a possible indication of a deeper imbalance. The main principle In the New Psychology DREVO, the psychologist’s task is not only to reduce symptoms. The main task is to understand,at what level is harmony violated?, what factors support this condition and how can human integrity be restored. Mental health does not return when a single symptom disappears. It returns when the body, psyche, consciousness, will, values, relationships and environment begin to work as a single system again. Any psychological problem is not a death sentence for the individual, but an invitation to restore internal balance and further development. Why does a person suffer? Suffering in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, suffering is not seen as a punishment or a meaningless accident. Suffering is a signal. It informs a person that harmony has been disturbed at one or more levels of his life. Just as physical pain warns of damage to the body, psychological suffering indicates the need to pay attention to an internal or external problem. Suffering becomes the language in which life communicates to a person the need for change. The main causes of suffering Violation of integrity A human being consists of interconnected levels. Body. Subconscious. Psyche. Consciousness. Will. Soul. Spirit. Values. Social connections. Environment. When a deep contradiction arises between them, internal tension appears. The greater the gap, the greater the suffering. Conflict between reality and expectations A person often suffers not only because of what is happening, but also because of the discrepancy between what is and how he would like the world to be. Not every disappointment can be resolved, but a person is able to learn to understand the situation in a new way, change their actions and look for ways to adapt. Conflict of values When a person regularly acts contrary to his own conscience and deepest convictions, an internal conflict arises. This contradiction gradually weakens the sense of integrity and may be accompanied by anxiety, guilt, or loss of meaning. Unmet needs The body and psyche need: security; love; respect; freedom; accessories; development; meaning. Long-term failure to satisfy important needs can become a source of suffering. Loss of meaning A person is capable of enduring great difficulties if he understands what he lives for. When the sense of meaning disappears, even an outwardly prosperous life can feel empty. Destruction of relationships Man develops among people. Loneliness, betrayal, violence, loss of loved ones and long-term conflicts can cause deep psychological pain. Therefore, the quality of relationships is one of the most important components of psychological health. Illness and physical pain Suffering may have physiological causes. Injuries. Chronic diseases. Disorders of the nervous or hormonal system. Psychological and biological causes often interact with each other. Therefore, caring for your health is part of caring for your mental health. Development through overcoming Not every suffering is the result of a mistake. Sometimes difficulties accompany learning, growing up, mastering a new skill, or overcoming life's challenges. Such experiences can become a source of growth if a person receives support, maintains meaning, and gradually finds ways to cope with them. Is it possible to completely get rid of suffering? Suffering is a part of human life. It is impossible to live life without ever encountering loss, mistakes, illness, or uncertainty. However, a person is capable of changing their attitude towards difficulties, learning to cope with them and reducing the suffering that arises from destructive habits, conflicts or lack of meaning. Psychology does not strive to eliminate all difficulties, but to develop the ability to live fully despite them. Transforming suffering into development In the New Psychology of DREVO, suffering becomes a point of choice. A person can: break down; run away; blame; or understand the reason for what is happening, change yourself and start a new stage of development. It is this choice that determines the future path of the individual. The main principle Suffering in itself does not make a person stronger. A person develops by how he responds to suffering. Awareness. Acceptance of responsibility. Search for solutions. Support from other people. Creative actions. They are the ones who turn pain into a source of growth. Definition Suffering is a psychophysiological and personal experience that occurs when a person's integrity is violated, important needs are not met, internal conflicts occur, illnesses occur, losses occur, or difficult life circumstances are encountered. In the New Psychology of DREVO, suffering is viewed not as a goal in life or as a punishment, but as a signal that encourages a person to restore harmony, rethink their path, and continue to develop. Suffering shows that something requires attention. But it is the person's conscious response that determines whether it becomes the beginning of destruction or the beginning of growth.

title: What is fear?
excerpt: Fear in the New Psychology of DREVO In DREVO's New Psychology, fear is viewed as a natural defense mechanism of the psyche, the purpose of which is to preserve a person's life and warn them of potential danger. Fear is n
text: Fear in the New Psychology of DREVO In DREVO's New Psychology, fear is viewed as a natural defense mechanism of the psyche, the purpose of which is to preserve a person's life and warn them of potential danger. Fear is not man's enemy. It is one of the most ancient defense systems of the body. Thanks to fear, a person is able to avoid threats, make decisions faster, and mobilize forces in critical situations. Therefore, fear in itself is not a psychological problem. It becomes a problem when it begins to manage a person’s life instead of him. What is fear? Fear is a psychophysiological reaction of the body to a real or perceived threat. When the brain perceives danger, the body begins to prepare for action. The functioning of the nervous system changes. The heartbeat accelerates. Breathing becomes more rapid. The muscles tense. Attention increases. The body goes into high alert mode. All these changes help to increase the likelihood of survival. Why does fear arise? Fear appears when the psyche evaluates a situation as dangerous. The danger may be: physical; social; emotional; economic; moral; existential. Sometimes the danger is real. Sometimes it exists only in a person's expectations. The psyche reacts not only to events, but also to their subjective assessment. Types of fear Fear can be conditionally divided into several levels. Biological fear Fear for life and health. It helps to avoid physical threats. Social fear Fear of rejection. Ridiculed. Lose respect. To be left alone. Psychological fear Fear of mistakes. Failures. Changes. Loss of control. Unknowns. Existential fear Fear of death. Loneliness. Meaninglessness. Loss of one's own self. Such questions are studied not only by psychology, but also by philosophy. Fear and the subconscious The subconscious strives to preserve life. Therefore, it often overestimates the danger rather than underestimates it. This was useful during human evolution. However, in modern life, the same mechanisms can cause excessive anxiety in situations that are not objectively life-threatening. Fear and consciousness Consciousness is able to assess the situation more accurately. It helps answer the questions: Is there really a danger? How big is it? What can I do? Thus consciousness does not destroy fear. It helps to use it as a source of information. Fear and will Fear does not disappear through willpower. Willpower helps a person act despite fear if the action corresponds to his values ​​and is truly necessary. Courage is not the absence of fear. Courage is the ability to remain aware and act responsibly in spite of it. When does fear become a problem? Fear ceases to perform a protective function when: appears without an objective reason; becomes permanent; completely controls human behavior; deprives of freedom of choice; interferes with development; turns into chronic anxiety or avoidance. In such cases, a person may need psychological or medical help. How to work with fear? In New Psychology DREVO, the goal is not to eliminate fear. The task is to learn to understand it. Useful: identify the source of fear; separate real threats from perceived ones; strengthen the body and health; develop awareness; gradually encounter surmountable difficulties; seek support if fear becomes excessive. Fear decreases as knowledge, experience and confidence increase. The main principle Fear seeks to protect life. Consciousness helps to understand the situation. Will helps to act. Values ​​determine direction. When these elements work in concert, fear ceases to be a person's master and becomes his advisor. Definition Fear is a natural psychophysiological reaction of the body to a real or perceived threat, designed to protect life and increase readiness for action. In DREVO's New Psychology, fear is viewed as a necessary self-preservation mechanism. Its purpose is to warn of danger, not to control a person's life. A person's maturity is determined not by the absence of fear, but by the ability to understand it, to distinguish real threats from imaginary ones, and to make informed decisions guided by reason, will, and one's values. What is anxiety? Anxiety in the New Psychology of DREVO In New Psychology DREVO, anxiety is viewed as a state of heightened readiness of the psyche and body for possible danger, uncertainty, or future events. While fear arises as a reaction to a specific threat, anxiety is more often associated with the anticipation of a possible threat. Fear answers the question: "Is the danger here yet?" Anxiety asks: "What if danger appears?" What is anxiety? Anxiety is a psychophysiological state of anticipation of possible danger, accompanied by increased attention, internal tension and the body's readiness for action. It helps a person to notice risks in advance, plan for the future and avoid potential threats. Therefore, anxiety, like fear, is a natural part of the psyche. Why is anxiety necessary? Without anxiety, a person would be too careless. It is anxiety that helps: prepare for the exam; check security; plan a trip; take care of your health; think about the future; avoid rash decisions. Moderate anxiety helps a person to be attentive and responsible. When does anxiety become a problem? Anxiety stops helping when it becomes too much. It begins to drain a person. Appears: constant internal stress; difficulty relaxing; sleep disturbance; the feeling that “something is about to happen”; inability to concentrate; chronic fatigue; avoidance of ordinary life situations. In such cases, anxiety no longer protects a person, but limits his life. Why does anxiety arise? Anxiety can be increased by various factors. Biological: chronic fatigue; lack of sleep; some diseases; hormonal imbalances; use of certain substances, including excess caffeine. Psychological: uncertainty; difficult life experience; internal conflicts; constant expectation of failure. Social: instability; information overload; long-term conflicts; lack of support. Usually anxiety arises under the influence of several factors at the same time. Anxiety and the body Anxiety always manifests itself not only in thoughts. It is reflected in the body. May appear: increased heart rate; muscle tension; shallow breathing; a feeling of heaviness in the chest; sweating; shiver; digestive problems; feeling of fatigue. This is associated with the activation of the nervous system and the preparation of the body for possible actions. Anxiety and consciousness Consciousness can both increase and decrease anxiety. When a person constantly imagines the worst possible scenarios, anxiety increases. If he analyzes the situation, checks the facts and makes a realistic plan of action, the anxiety level often decreases. Therefore, knowledge and clarity reduce uncertainty. Anxiety and will Willpower helps a person not to submit completely to anxiety. It allows you to continue to act even when internal anxiety persists. Overcoming anxiety does not happen through fighting feelings, but through gradually strengthening confidence, experience, and the ability to cope with difficulties. How to reduce anxiety? In the New Psychology DREVO, anxiety is seen as a signal requiring attention. Useful: identify the source of uncertainty; separate real risks from assumptions; restore sleep and rest patterns; maintain physical activity; limit information overload; discuss your experiences with loved ones or a specialist; focus on what is truly under your control. If anxiety becomes persistent and seriously disrupts your life, it is important to seek professional help. The main principle Anxiety warns of possible danger. Consciousness evaluates its probability. Will helps to act. Experience gradually transforms the unknown into the known. The more understanding and inner stability a person acquires, the less room there is for helpless anxiety. Definition Anxiety is a natural psychophysiological state of anticipation of possible danger or uncertainty, which helps a person prepare for future events and take precautions. In DREVO's New Psychology, anxiety is viewed as a useful coping mechanism that only becomes a problem when it no longer corresponds to the real situation, deprives a person of freedom of choice, and interferes with a fulfilling life. Fear warns of present danger. Anxiety warns of possible future danger. Personal maturity lies in the ability to distinguish between the two and maintain clarity of thought even in the face of uncertainty.

title: What is depression?
excerpt: Depression in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, depression is viewed as a state of profound exhaustion in a person, in which the coordinated functioning of the body, psyche, consciousness, will,
text: Depression in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, depression is viewed as a state of profound exhaustion in a person, in which the coordinated functioning of the body, psyche, consciousness, will, social connections, and life purpose is disrupted. Depression is not a weakness of character. Not a lack of willpower. Not laziness. It is a complex condition that can have biological, psychological and social causes. Therefore, a person facing depression does not need condemnation, but understanding, support and, in many cases, professional help. What is depression? Depression is a persistent condition in which a person experiences a significant decline in mood and interest in life over a long period of time, accompanied by changes in thinking, emotions, behavior, and body function. Modern psychology and psychiatry consider depression to be one of the most common mental disorders, requiring careful diagnosis and selection of assistance. Why does depression occur? In the New Psychology of DREVO, depression is viewed as the result of an imbalance on several levels of personality. Biological level A person's condition can be influenced by: hereditary predisposition; features of brain function; hormonal changes; chronic diseases; prolonged fatigue; sleep disorders. Psychological level Depression can be associated with: heavy losses; long-term stress; psychological trauma; internal conflicts; a feeling of helplessness; chronic anxiety. Social level Of great importance are: loneliness; lack of support; violence; poverty; social isolation; destruction of significant relationships. Existential level For some people, depression is accompanied by: loss of meaning in life; a feeling of emptiness; lack of future; loss of a sense of self-worth. Not every person with depression experiences this exact thing, but for some people, these issues do become a significant part of their experience. How does depression manifest itself? Depression may be accompanied by: persistent decline in mood; loss of interest in usual activities; constant fatigue; sleep disorders; change in appetite; difficulties in concentration; a feeling of hopelessness; decreased self-esteem; a feeling of the meaninglessness of what is happening. Manifestations can vary significantly among different people. Depression and willpower Often, it seems to those around you that all a person needs to do is “pull himself together.” This is a misconception. When depressed, it can be really difficult for a person to perform even simple tasks. Decreased activity is part of the condition itself, not a sign of lack of character. Therefore, assistance should take into account the real capabilities of the person, and not be based on accusations. Recovery In the New Psychology of DREVO, recovery is seen as a gradual process of returning to wholeness. It may include: medical care; psychotherapy; support from family and friends; sleep restoration; physical activity; gradual return to everyday life; search for meaning and purpose; community participation; creative activity. The path to recovery is individual for each person. What can loved ones do? For a person with depression the following are especially important: respect; patience; willingness to listen; absence of judgment; assistance in seeking professional support; preservation of human dignity. Sometimes the most valuable thing is not finding the right words, but simply being there. The main principle Depression does not define a person's personality. It is a serious condition that can change one's perception of the world, but does not negate the value of the individual. Even when a person no longer sees hope, the possibility of recovery may remain. Therefore, care, knowledge, treatment and support become part of the path to recovery. Definition Depression is a complex mental condition that occurs as a result of the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors and is characterized by a persistent decline in mood, loss of interest in life, changes in thinking, behavior and overall functioning of a person. In DREVO's New Psychology, depression is viewed as a disruption of the individual's integrity, requiring a comprehensive approach that integrates care for the body, mind, relationships, meaning in life, and professional help. A person is greater than their illness. Even in the darkest periods of their life, recovery remains possible if understanding, support, and a path to gradual wholeness are available. Important.If someone is experiencing suicidal thoughts, feelings of complete hopelessness, or is unable to cope with daily life, it is essential to consult a doctor or mental health professional as soon as possible. Depression is a treatable condition, and prompt help can make a crucial difference. What is laziness? Laziness in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, laziness is not seen as an innate human flaw, but as a condition that arises when energy, motivation, meaning, health, or internal harmony between levels of personality are disrupted. In many cases, a person does not stop acting because he “does not want to.” It stops acting because some part of its system is not ready for action. Therefore, laziness is not a diagnosis or a character trait. This is a signal that requires understanding. What is laziness? Laziness is a person’s decreased willingness to perform necessary actions when there is an objective opportunity to do them. It can be short-term or long-term. Sometimes laziness is a normal need of the body for rest. Sometimes it is a manifestation of deeper psychological or physiological problems. Why does laziness arise? In New Psychology DREVO, laziness can have different causes. Body wasting If the body does not have enough sleep, rest, nutrition or movement, it begins to conserve energy. In this case, the desire to remain inactive is a protective reaction of the body. The body needs to recover first. Mental exhaustion Long-term stress, anxiety, burnout, or constant tension reduce a person's ability to function. The psyche begins to avoid additional stress. Lack of meaning It is difficult for a person to do something for a long time in which he sees no point. If an activity is perceived as alien, meaningless, or contrary to internal values, motivation gradually decreases. Personality conflict Sometimes one part of a person wants to take action. The other one is afraid. The third one doubts. Such an internal conflict creates a feeling of laziness, although in fact the person finds himself between opposing aspirations. Lack of discipline Not all activities bring pleasure. Some important tasks require habit, organization and strong will. If these qualities are not yet sufficiently developed, it becomes difficult for a person to regularly perform necessary tasks. Laziness and the subconscious The subconscious strives to save energy. If a person does not understand why he needs to perform a difficult task, the subconscious prefers to conserve resources. Therefore, personal development requires that the conscious mind explain to the subconscious the meaning of future efforts. Once the meaning becomes clear, resistance often decreases. Laziness and will Willpower does not destroy laziness. It helps to start moving despite a temporary lack of desire. However, strong will should not be used to constantly ignore the needs of the body. Sometimes a person needs to show discipline. Sometimes it's time to give yourself a break. Wisdom lies in the ability to distinguish between these situations. When does laziness become a problem? Laziness begins to limit a person’s development if: becomes permanent; deprives one of the opportunity to realize one’s abilities; leads to the destruction of health, relationships or work; becomes a habitual way of avoiding responsibility. In such cases, it is important to look not only for ways to force yourself to act, but also for the reasons for the loss of internal energy or motivation. How to overcome laziness? In New Psychology DREVO recommends not fighting laziness, but understanding its origins. It's helpful to ask yourself a few questions. Did my body rest? Is my body healthy? Do I have a clear goal? Does this matter align with my values? Am I trying to avoid fear or failure? What would be the first small step? Very often, a small but completed step destroys the feeling of inner immobility. The main principle Laziness is rarely the real reason for inaction. Most often it is a consequence. A consequence of fatigue. Fear. Loss of meaning. Internal conflict. Or an insufficiently developed habit of action. By understanding the reason, a person gets the opportunity to change his state. Definition Laziness is a state of decreased readiness to act that arises from exhaustion, lack of meaning, internal conflict, lack of discipline, or other biological, psychological, or social factors. In the New Psychology of DREVO, laziness is not seen as a personality flaw, but as a signal that one or more levels of a person require attention, restoration, or development. True overcoming of laziness begins not with coercion, but with understanding. When the body gains strength, the mind gains clarity, the will gains direction, and life gains meaning, action becomes a natural extension of one's inner state.

title: What is addiction?
excerpt: Addiction in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, addiction is viewed as a condition in which a person gradually loses the freedom to control themselves, and the satisfaction of one need begins to
text: Addiction in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, addiction is viewed as a condition in which a person gradually loses the freedom to control themselves, and the satisfaction of one need begins to subjugate other aspects of life. Addiction can be to substances, activities, relationships, technologies, or other sources of strong reinforcement. Its main feature is not the object of addiction itself, but that a person loses the ability to choose freely. What is addiction? Addiction is a persistent condition in which the desire for a particular substance, activity, person, or experience begins to prevail over a person's conscious choice, personal values, and long-term interests. It is the loss of inner freedom that distinguishes addiction from ordinary habit. How does addiction occur? Addiction develops gradually. Typically this process goes through several stages. Interest. A person gains new experience. Repetition. The experience begins to bring pleasure, relief, or a sense of security. Habit. The behavior becomes regular. Need. It becomes difficult for a person to do without this source of satisfaction. Loss of freedom. Behavior begins to control a person, and not a person - his behavior. Why does addiction occur? In the New Psychology DREVO, addiction is seen as a result of a disturbance in internal balance. It can be aggravated by a combination of several factors. Biological reasons Certain substances or behaviors can activate the brain's reward systems. In addition, hereditary predisposition, metabolic characteristics and health conditions can have an impact. Psychological reasons A person may be looking for a way to reduce: anxiety; loneliness; internal pain; feeling of emptiness; stress; emotional stress. If addiction temporarily alleviates feelings, there is a risk of it becoming entrenched. Social reasons Of great importance are: environment; family relationships; culture; availability of the dependency object; stressful environment; lack of support. Existential reasons For some people, addiction becomes an attempt to fill an inner emptiness, a lack of meaning in life, or a loss of direction. This is not always the main reason, but for some people this factor does play an important role. Types of dependencies Addiction can manifest itself in different ways. For example: alcoholic; nicotine; narcotic; gaming; digital; social media addiction; shopping addiction; food; emotional dependence; workaholism. Despite the differences in form, they are united by the gradual loss of freedom of choice. Dependence and freedom In the DREVO philosophy, freedom means a person’s ability to consciously manage their life. Addiction gradually limits this ability. The subconscious begins to demand a familiar source of satisfaction. Consciousness is finding it increasingly difficult to make independent decisions. The will weakens. Therefore, addiction is seen as a violation of the individual’s inner freedom. Is it possible to overcome addiction? Yes. But overcoming is rarely just a matter of giving up the object of dependence. It is important to restore the entire personality system. This may include: medical care; psychotherapy; family and community support; developing new habits; health promotion; restoration of the meaning of life; development of will; participation in creative activities. The more healthy sources of joy and meaning appear in a person’s life, the easier it is for him to give up destructive addiction. The main principle A person does not strive for dependence itself. He is trying to satisfy some important need. If you can understand this need and find a healthier way to meet it, the path to recovery becomes much more realistic. True liberation begins not with fighting addiction, but with restoring inner freedom. Definition Addiction is a state of loss of inner freedom, in which the desire for a certain substance, action, person or experience begins to control a person’s behavior, limiting their ability to make conscious choices. In the New Psychology of DREVO, addiction is viewed as a disruption in the coordinated functioning of the body, psyche, consciousness, will, values, and social connections. Recovery begins with restoring the ability to independently choose the direction of one's life. Free is not the one who can get everything he wants. Free is the one who can control his desires, not be controlled by them. What is aggression? Aggression in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, aggression is viewed as a natural psychophysiological reaction of mobilization that arises in response to a threat, obstacle, injustice, or violation of important human needs. Aggression in itself is neither good nor evil. This is the energy of action. It can be aimed at both destruction and protection, restoration of justice and overcoming difficulties. What matters most is not the presence of aggression, but how a person manages it. What is aggression? Aggression is a state of heightened mobilization of the body and psyche, aimed at overcoming an obstacle, protecting oneself, one's loved ones, one's values, or achieving a significant goal. During aggression, the body switches to active action mode. The heartbeat accelerates. Muscle tone increases. Concentration of attention is enhanced. The body is preparing to act. Why is aggression necessary? Without aggression, a person would not be able to: protect your life; protect the child; defend personal boundaries; overcome danger; fight against injustice; persistently achieve difficult goals. Thus, aggression is part of the survival system and active behavior. Why does aggression arise? Aggression can arise for various reasons. For example: real threat; feeling of injustice; violation of personal boundaries; fear; chronic stress; physical pain; strong disappointment; feeling of powerlessness; prolonged emotional stress. Sometimes aggression becomes a way to hide deeper feelings, such as anxiety, shame, or feelings of vulnerability. Aggression and violence In New Psychology DREVO these concepts are distinguished.
