Aggression- this is the internal energy of mobilization. Violence- this is a way of expressing it that causes unjustified harm to another person. Not all aggression leads to violence. A person can use his inner strength to: protection; sports; creativity; persistent work; leadership; social activities. A mature personality knows how to transform aggression into creative action. Aggression and will When aggression is driven solely by emotions, a person risks acting impulsively. When aggression is controlled by consciousness, will and values, it becomes a source of courage, determination and the ability to defend life. Willpower does not suppress aggression. She helps to direct it in a constructive direction. Suppressed aggression Constantly suppressing aggression can also be harmful. A person stops protecting his boundaries. Afraid to say no. Accumulates internal tension. Or one day experiences an uncontrollable emotional outburst. Therefore, the task is not to eliminate aggression, but to develop the ability to express it safely and responsibly. How to transform aggression? In the New Psychology of DREVO, aggression is seen as energy that can be directed. This is helped by: physical activity; open dialogue; development of self-control; protection of personal boundaries; creativity; socially useful activity; conflict resolution training; development of emotional maturity. Energy that could have become destructive can be transformed into a creative force. The main principle Aggression is not given to man for destruction. It is given to protect life and overcome obstacles. Personal maturity is determined not by the absence of aggression, but by the ability to manage it while maintaining respect for oneself, other people, and human dignity. Definition Aggression is a natural psychophysiological reaction of the body's mobilization that occurs when a threat, obstacle, or violation of significant needs is perceived and is intended for active defense, overcoming difficulties, or restoring justice. In DREVO's New Psychology, aggression is viewed as a source of inner strength that can be directed toward either destruction or creation. The direction of this strength is determined by a person's consciousness, will, values, and responsibility. It's not aggression that makes a person dangerous. It's the inability to control one's own power that makes one dangerous. What is loneliness? Loneliness in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, loneliness is viewed as the experience of a lack of deep connection with other people, oneself, nature, society, or life meaning. Loneliness is not determined by the number of people around you. A person can be alone and feel inner peace. And he can be among thousands of people and feel deep loneliness. Therefore, loneliness is, first of all, a state of internal connection, and not physical isolation. What is loneliness? Loneliness is a psychological experience of loss or lack of significant connections, in which a person feels separated from other people, the world, or oneself. The main reason for loneliness is not the lack of communication, but the lack of a sense of true understanding, acceptance and belonging. Why does loneliness arise? In New Psychology DREVO, loneliness can arise for various reasons. Destruction of social ties Loss of loved ones. Divorce. Moving. Insulation. Conflicts. Rejection. All of these events can weaken the sense of belonging. Losing touch with yourself Sometimes a person stops understanding: who is he; what does he want; what does he live for? In this case, inner loneliness arises. Even good relationships with other people are not always able to completely eliminate it. Loss of common values True intimacy is built on more than just time spent together. It is built on trust, respect, mutual understanding and common meanings. When these foundations disappear, a person can feel lonely even when close to loved ones. Modern lifestyle The development of digital technologies has significantly increased the number of contacts. But the amount of communication does not always mean the depth of the relationship. Sometimes a person receives a lot of messages, but rarely feels that he is truly understood. Loneliness and the body Loneliness affects more than just the psyche. It may be accompanied by: chronic stress; sleep disturbance; increased anxiety; decreased energy; deterioration of general well-being. Research shows that long-term social isolation may be associated with poor physical and mental health. Useful solitude and painful loneliness In the New Psychology DREVO, two states are distinguished. Solitude- this is a voluntary stay alone with oneself. It helps a person to relax, reflect, learn, create and better understand himself. Loneliness— is an experience of internal lack of connection that a person does not choose and which is often accompanied by pain. Solitude develops. Loneliness can be draining. How to overcome loneliness? Overcoming loneliness doesn't start with increasing the number of people you meet. It starts with rebuilding real connections. Useful: develop friendship; participate in community life; help other people; find common interests; spend time in nature; engage in joint creative work; learn to talk openly about your feelings; reconnect with your own values ​​and meaning. Sometimes the support of a psychologist or psychotherapist is also necessary, especially if loneliness is associated with bereavement, depression or social anxiety. Loneliness and development Paradoxically, the experience of loneliness sometimes becomes the beginning of deep internal changes. It is during such periods that a person can: get to know yourself better; reconsider values; change your lifestyle; find a new purpose; build more mature relationships. It is not loneliness itself that develops a person. It is how he goes through this experience that develops him. The main principle A person develops through connections. Connection with yourself. With loved ones. With society. With nature. With culture. With the future. The deeper these connections, the more stable the personality becomes. Definition Loneliness is a psychological state that occurs when one feels a lack of meaningful connections with others, oneself, society, nature, or purpose in life. In the New Psychology of DREVO, loneliness is seen as a signal of the need to restore relationships, mutual understanding and inner integrity, and not as an immutable personality trait. A person is like a tree. One tree can stand alone, but a true forest emerges through connections. Similarly, a person becomes truly strong not when they completely dispense with others, but when they are able to build deep, free, and creative relationships.

title: What is burnout?
excerpt: Burnout in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, burnout is considered a state of chronic exhaustion of a person, which occurs when the expenditure of physical, emotional and psychological resources exceeds t
text: Burnout in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, burnout is considered a state of chronic exhaustion of a person, which occurs when the expenditure of physical, emotional and psychological resources exceeds their restoration over a long period of time. Burnout doesn't happen overnight. It develops gradually. First, the energy disappears. Then interest. Then a sense of meaning. If a person continues to live in the same way, the body begins to limit his activity in order to preserve vital resources. Thus, burnout can be seen as a protective reaction of the body to prolonged overload. What is burnout? Burnout is a state of prolonged physical, emotional, and psychological exhaustion, accompanied by a decrease in motivation, performance, sense of effectiveness, and interest in activities. The World Health Organization defines burnout as a phenomenon associated with chronic workplace stress that has not been successfully managed. More broadly, such exhaustion can also occur in other areas of life. Why does burnout occur? In New Psychology DREVO, burnout develops when the balance between giving and recovery is disrupted. The main reasons may be: chronic stress; lack of adequate rest; permanent responsibility; emotional stress; lack of support; lack of meaning in activity; inability to influence the situation; conflict between human values ​​and environmental demands. The longer this imbalance persists, the higher the risk of burnout. How does burnout develop? Burnout usually goes through several stages. Enthusiasm. The person works with full dedication. Overload. Resources begin to be used up faster than they can be restored. Exhaustion. Fatigue, irritability and loss of interest appear. Indifference. A person stops experiencing joy from what was previously important. Devastation. Even simple tasks begin to require excessive effort. Burnout and the Body Burnout affects more than just the psyche. It may be accompanied by: chronic fatigue; sleep disturbance; muscle tension; decreased immune protection; headaches; impaired concentration; a feeling of constant lack of energy. The body begins to communicate that the previous regime can no longer be maintained. Burnout and meaning One of the characteristics of burnout is the gradual loss of meaning in one's activities. The person can continue to perform their usual work. But the feeling of inner connection with what it is being done for disappears. In the New Psychology DREVO, meaning is considered one of the most important sources of psychological energy. When it disappears, the exhaustion intensifies. How is burnout different from laziness? Laziness is often associated with a lack of readiness to initiate action. Burnout occurs after a long period of overactivity and overload. A lazy person often still has strength, but does not want to use it. A person suffering from burnout often wants to take action, but feels that they have almost no internal resources left. How to recover? Recovery doesn't start with increasing the load. It starts with resource recovery. This may include: complete rest; normalization of sleep; reduction of chronic stress; physical activity; restoration of relations; change of operating mode; rethinking life goals; seeking professional help if necessary. Sometimes recovery requires changing not only your lifestyle, but also your work organization or environment. The main principle Burnout does not mean a person is weak. It means that his system has been running for too long without sufficient recovery. The body stops demanding feats. He begins to demand care. Restoring energy does not mean giving up on development. This is a necessary condition for further growth. Definition Burnout is a state of chronic physical, emotional and psychological exhaustion that occurs as a result of a long-term discrepancy between the expenditure and restoration of a person's vital resources. In the New Psychology of DREVO, burnout is viewed as an imbalance between the body, psyche, consciousness, will, values, and lifestyle. Overcoming it requires restoring personal integrity, not just a temporary break. A person is like a tree. If a tree continually produces fruit but does not receive water, light, and nourishment, it gradually stops growing. Likewise, a person cannot give endlessly without replenishing their inner strength. What is happiness? Happiness in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, happiness is viewed as a state of inner harmony that occurs when a person lives in harmony with themselves, their values, the people around them, and the world. Happiness is not constant joy. Not the absence of difficulties. Not endless pleasure. Happiness is a feeling of fullness of life, in which a person feels that he is developing, loving, creating and moving in the right direction for himself. What is happiness? Happiness is a state of harmonious interaction between the body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, social connections and the meaning of life. When these levels are aligned with each other, a person experiences inner integrity. It is this state that becomes the basis of happiness. Why can't you buy happiness? Money can improve the quality of life. They can provide security, comfort, education and new opportunities. But by themselves they do not create: Love; trust; meaning; friendship; inner peace; self-respect; a sense of purpose. Therefore, material well-being is an important part of life, but not the only source of happiness. What makes happiness? In the New Psychology of DREVO, happiness is born from the harmony of several spheres of life. Healthy body When the body receives movement, rest, nutrition and care, it is easier for a person to feel vitality. Calm psyche Emotional stability helps you to overcome difficulties without losing your inner balance. Free consciousness A person is capable of thinking independently, choosing and taking responsibility for his life. Strong will Willpower helps to turn dreams into actions. Moving towards important goals brings deep satisfaction. An open soul A person lives in harmony with his conscience, love and inner values. Strong spirit Life takes on direction. A person understands why he lives and what he strives for. Loving relationship Family. Friends. Community. Cooperation. Love and trust are among the most important sources of human happiness. Creative work A person is happier when he feels that his abilities benefit other people. Work becomes not only a way to earn money, but also a way to leave a good mark on the world. Harmony with nature A person feels like a part of life. He receives strength from nature and at the same time takes care of it. Happiness and pleasure Pleasure and happiness are not the same thing. Pleasure is usually short-lived. It is associated with a specific experience. Happiness is more sustainable. It is connected with the way of life and the feeling of its fulfillment. A person can experience pleasure and remain deeply unhappy. And vice versa - during a difficult period of life, maintain a sense of meaning and inner support. Happiness and development Happiness does not mean the absence of difficulties. It means the ability to see the meaning of one's path even when that path requires effort. Man is developing. Studies. He is mistaken. Overcomes obstacles. Creates something new. And it is this process that makes life fulfilling. In DREVO's New Psychology, happiness is understood not as an end goal, but as a natural state of a person who develops in harmony with themselves and the world. The main principle Happiness cannot be achieved once and for all. It cannot be given as a gift. It can't be bought. It is born every day through lifestyle, actions, relationships, health, development and creation. The more harmoniously a person develops, the deeper his happiness becomes. Definition Happiness is a state of inner harmony and integrity that occurs when a person lives in accordance with their values, realizes their abilities, builds healthy relationships, takes care of their body and mind, and makes a creative contribution to the lives of others. In the New Psychology of DREVO, happiness is viewed not as random luck or a constant emotion, but as the result of the coordinated work of all levels of the personality and its harmonious interaction with society, nature, and the future. Happiness isn't the moment when a person gets everything they want. Happiness is a state in which a person becomes who they are capable of becoming and helps the world around them develop. What is love? Love in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, love is seen as a fundamental force in the development of personality and life. Love is not just a feeling. Not just emotion. Not just a hormonal reaction. Not just romantic relationships. Love is a conscious desire to preserve, develop, protect and reveal life. If fear seeks to save life from danger, then love strives to make life richer, deeper and more beautiful. What is love? Love is a conscious desire for the good of another person, oneself, society, nature and life in general, manifested through respect, care, freedom, responsibility and creativity. Love is always aimed at development. She helps life become stronger. Love as a state of personality Love is born not so much from the desire to possess another person, but from inner maturity. Therefore, love is not only a relationship with another. It becomes a way of existence for the person himself. A loving person strives to create, not to destroy. Unite, not divide. Support, don't suppress. Love and affection Love and affection are not the same thing. Attachment says: "I need you to be happy." Love says: "I want you to live, develop and be happy." Affection is afraid of being lost. Love helps you grow. True love does not negate intimacy and mutual support, but respects the freedom and dignity of the other person. Love and the body Love also manifests itself at the level of the body. In close and trusting relationships, the functioning of the nervous system changes, releasing hormones and neurotransmitters associated with attachment, pleasure, and a sense of security. However, biological processes are only one side of love. They accompany love, but do not exhaust its meaning. Love and the psyche Love creates a sense of security. It helps a person to reveal their abilities. Develop trust. Study. To create. Overcome difficulties. In many cases, it is the experience of love that becomes the basis for an individual’s psychological stability. Love and soul In the New Psychology of DREVO, the soul is the source of love. It is through love that a person experiences unity with other people and feels the value of life. Love helps the soul to open up. The more a person is able to love, the deeper his inner world is revealed. Love and Spirit The spirit determines the direction of life. Love determines the quality of this path. A strong spirit without love can become harshness. Love without spirit can remain only a good intention. Only the union of love and spirit creates the creative power of personality. Love and freedom True love is impossible without freedom. It does not destroy personality. Does not turn a person into property. Doesn't require giving up your own dignity. Love creates a space in which both people can grow. Love as the basis of civilization In a family, love breeds trust. In community there is cooperation. There is solidarity in society. In relation to nature - responsibility. In relation to future generations - care. Thus, love becomes one of the foundations of a sustainable civilization. The main principle Love is not measured by the strength of feelings. It is measured by how much life comes from a person. If there is more trust, freedom, health, beauty, knowledge, cooperation, and hope around a person, then love is manifested in their actions. Definition Love is a conscious desire to preserve, protect, develop and reveal life in all its manifestations, based on respect, freedom, responsibility and creation. In the New Psychology of DREVO, love is considered the highest form of personal maturity, uniting the body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul and spirit into a single direction of development. Love isn't something a person feels. Love is something a person creates. The more life, freedom, goodness, knowledge, and creativity a person brings, the deeper their capacity for love unfolds.

title: Practice
excerpt: From knowledge to action Knowledge in itself does not change a person. A person develops only when knowledge becomes thoughts, thoughts become decisions, decisions become actions, and actions become habits. Practice is t
text: From knowledge to action Knowledge in itself does not change a person. A person develops only when knowledge becomes thoughts, thoughts become decisions, decisions become actions, and actions become habits. Practice is the main tool of the New Psychology DREVO. Its goal is not to change a person overnight, but to create a way of life in which development becomes a natural process. The first principle Every day a person can do at least one action that will strengthen life. This action may be aimed at: body; psyche; consciousness; will; soul; spirit; relationship; nature; society. Small daily actions gradually change the entire human system. The second principle Develop all levels simultaneously. Like a tree, it is impossible to develop just one part. The roots feed the trunk. The trunk supports the branches. The branches produce leaves. Leaves feed the tree. The fruits become the seeds of new life. A person develops in the same way. If only the body is strengthened but relationships are destroyed, development becomes one-sided. If intelligence develops but values ​​are lost, knowledge can be used for harm. Harmonious development requires attention to all levels of personality. The third principle Practice is more important than intention. Intention shows direction. Practice creates result. It is better to do one useful action today than to make great plans that will never be realized. The fourth principle Development begins with oneself. It is impossible to teach health by destroying your own body. It is impossible to cultivate honesty by constantly lying. It is impossible to talk about love without showing respect for people. A man becomes an example before he becomes a teacher. The fifth principle Leave the world a little better every day. This could be: helping a person; new knowledge; planted tree; restored health; created work; problem solved; a kind word; an honest act. Creation comes from small daily actions. The sixth principle Regularity is more important than intensity. A one-time effort rarely changes a life. Constant practice changes a person. Just as a tree grows every day, personality develops through regular actions. The Seventh Principle Development never ends. Each stage of life opens up new challenges. A person is capable of developing until the last day of his life. Maturity is not an end point, but the ability to constantly learn, change, and remain open to new experiences. DREVO practice formula Every day ask yourself: What did I do for my body today? What new things have I learned? What decision did I make consciously? What strengthened my will? What helped my soul open up? What action strengthened my spirit? Who did I help today? What have I done for nature or the environment? What did I create today? If there is an honest answer to at least some of these questions, then this day has become a day of development. The main principle of practice Development is measured not by the amount of knowledge, but by the number of good, conscious and creative actions taken. Real psychology does not begin in an office or in a book. It begins at the moment when a person transforms understanding into action, action into habit, habit into character, and character into creative life. Daily practices Daily Development Practice in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, personal development is viewed not as a separate event, but as a way of life. A person changes gradually. Every day forms habits. Habits shape character. Character determines destiny. Therefore, daily actions are much more important than occasional efforts. The main goal of daily practice is to support the harmonious development of all levels of personality. 1. Body practice Pay attention to your body every day. This could be: morning exercises; walk; stretching; strength training; breathing exercises; good sleep; healthy eating. A strong body creates the basis for personal development. 2. Breathing practice A few minutes of calm, conscious breathing can help reduce tension, restore focus, and improve your sense of well-being. Breathing is one of the simplest ways to connect body and mind. 3. Mindfulness practice Ask yourself a few questions every day. What do I feel now? What am I thinking about? Why do I react this way? What's really important today? Mindfulness helps the consciousness manage life, rather than living automatically. 4. Practice gratitude Every day, remember at least three things for which you can be grateful. These could be: People; events; health; nature; new knowledge; own achievements. Gratitude develops the ability to notice the value of life. 5. Teaching practice Learn something new every day. Read. Learn languages. Master the skills. Ask questions. The development of intelligence must continue throughout life. 6. Practice of creation Create something useful every day. Text. Drawing. Music. Product. An idea. Solution to the problem. Planted tree. Helping a person. Creation makes development real. 7. Practice good deeds Every day, do at least one thing that will improve someone else's life. This could be: help; support; a kind word; sincere conversation; collaboration; Gratitude. Personal development is impossible without the development of relationships. 8. Practice of nature Find opportunities to interact with nature every day. Walk. Tree watching. Working in the garden. Contemplation of the sky. Touching the ground. Nature helps people restore their inner balance. 9. Practice of silence Spend a few minutes every day without your phone, conversations, or information noise. Silence helps you hear your own thoughts and feel your inner state. It is in silence that the best solutions are often born. 10. Practice of meaning Before going to bed, ask yourself three questions. What good have I done today? What did you learn today? What will help me become a little better tomorrow? These questions gradually shape the direction of personal development. DREVO's Daily Development Formula Every day it is necessary to strengthen: Body— movement. Psyche- calmness. Consciousness- knowledge. Will- discipline. Soul- love. Spirit- loyalty to one's values. Relationship- good deeds. Nature- care. Society- cooperation. Future- creation. The main principle It is impossible to change your life with one great act. But it can be changed by thousands of small, correct actions. Every day is a new seed. Every habit is a new root. Every good deed is a new branch. Every creative decision is a new fruit. This is how a strong Personality Tree gradually grows. Definition Daily practices are a system of regular actions aimed at the harmonious development of the body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, social connections, and a person's relationship with nature and society. In the New Psychology of DREVO, daily practice is considered the main tool for personal development, since it is repeated actions that gradually shape habits, character, and lifestyle. A person doesn't become what they dream about. A person becomes what they do every day. Weekly practices Weekly Development Practice in New Psychology DREVO While daily practices help a person maintain inner balance, weekly ones allow one to see the bigger picture of their life. A week is a natural cycle of analysis, recovery and direction adjustment. Each week, a person gets the opportunity to stop, evaluate their actions, strengthen relationships, recuperate, and take the next step forward. 1. Recovery Day Make time for proper rest. The body needs restoration no less than work. Rest is not a waste of time. It is a condition for further development. 2. Analysis of the week Once a week, answer yourself these questions: What went well? What didn't work? What have I learned? What mistakes did you make? What do I want to change next week? Self-analysis helps transform experience into knowledge. 3. Setting goals Identify a few key tasks for the next week. It is important to choose goals that are not only work-related. No less important are the goals: health; families; training; creativity; communication; rest. A harmonious life requires the development of all its aspects. 4. Time for family and friends Spend time with the people who really matter. Live communication builds trust. Joint work. Joint vacation. Shared memories. This is how strong relationships are born. 5. Practice of nature Spend a few hours outside the urban environment. Forest. Park. Lake. Mountains. Working in the garden. Observing nature helps restore focus, reduce stress, and feel connected to the world around us. 6. Teaching practice Take the time to learn a new topic in depth. Not for the exam. Not for the sake of the report. For the sake of my own development. Study what expands your understanding of the world. 7. Practice of creation Create something new every week. Write an article. Plant a tree. Develop a project. Do something useful. Help the community. Creation turns knowledge into real change. 8. Practice of service Do at least one selfless act. Help the person. Support the project. Pass on the knowledge. Become a mentor. When a person makes the world a better place, not only society develops. He himself is also developing.

Freer. If every day helps a person move forward, then every week helps ensure that he is moving in the right direction. Definition Weekly practices are a system of regular analysis, restoration, and personal development that allows a person to maintain harmony between the body, psyche, consciousness, will, values, relationships, and lifestyle. In New Psychology DREVO, weekly practice is viewed as a natural cycle of reflecting on experience, strengthening social connections, and preparing for the next stage of development. Each week is a growth ring on the tree of life. Over time, they reveal how strong and mature the tree itself has become. Monthly practices Monthly Development Practice in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, a month is seen as a cycle of consolidation of changes. If a day forms habits, a week helps to adjust actions, then a month allows you to see the first results of development. Monthly practices help a person evaluate their progress, strengthen healthy habits, and change those that no longer contribute to development. A month is a time to take your time and grow consciously. 1. Summing up the month At the end of each month, set aside time for reflection. Ask yourself: What was the main event of the month? What has changed in me? What worked out best? What was the most difficult thing? What has this month taught me? Experience becomes wisdom only when a person comprehends it. 2. Checking your life balance Rate the main areas of your life on a scale of one to ten. health; mental state; knowledge; work; family; Friends; creativity; nature; rest; the meaning of life. See which areas need more attention. The goal is not perfect grades, but harmonious development. 3. Testing ten levels of a person Every month, evaluate the state of your personality. Body.
Has it become stronger and healthier? Subconscious.
What new habits have emerged? Psyche.
What emotions were predominant? Consciousness.
What new things did I understand? Will.
What promises did you keep to yourself? Soul.
Have I lived in alignment with my values? Spirit.
Have you lost your way? Meaning.
What was really important this month? Social connections.
What relationships have been strengthened? Interaction with nature.
Have I managed to maintain contact with the living world? 4. Purification practice Free up space. Clear out your work area. Delete unnecessary files. Finish old business. Get rid of things you no longer use. Order around helps create order within. 5. Teaching practice Master one new topic every month. It doesn't have to be deep. The main thing is to constantly expand your horizons. New knowledge helps maintain flexibility of thinking. 6. Practice of creation Create at least one completed result per month. This could be: article; study; painting; product; new skill; community project; now; educational course. Creation shows a person the fruits of his labor. 7. Communication practice Meet people you haven't seen for a long time. Thank your mentor. Make peace if possible. Meet someone new. Strengthen human connections every month. 8. Practice of nature Take a day to connect more deeply with nature. Hike. Forest. Mountains. Sea. Working in the garden. Planting a tree. Plant care. A person understands his own life better when he observes natural cycles. 9. Practice of service Every month, do something useful not only for yourself. This could be: volunteering; family assistance; teaching others; participation in an environmental project; local community support. Creation becomes mature when it benefits others. 10. Next month's plan Before the start of a new month, answer three questions. What do I want to save? What do I want to change? What will be the main direction of my development? The plan doesn't have to be long. The main thing is that it is conscious. DREVO's Monthly Development Formula Every month you need to: analyzeyour way; strengthen health; update knowledge; clearspace; deepen relationship; createsomething new; helpto others; spend timein nature; adjust direction; take the next step forward. The main principle Every month is a new chapter of life. Don't let the months go by unnoticed. If each month becomes a little more conscious than the previous one, then in a few years a person will be surprised to see how much his life has changed. Definition Monthly practices are a system of regular analysis, renewal, and reinforcement of personal development, allowing a person to maintain harmony between the body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, relationships, and the surrounding world. In New Psychology DREVO, a month is viewed as a natural growth cycle in which a person transforms daily actions into sustainable habits, and habits into a new way of life. A day changes your mood. A week changes your habits. A month changes your lifestyle. Years change you. Annual practices Annual Development Practice in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, the year is seen as a natural cycle of completion, renewal, and the beginning of a new stage in life. If every day forms habits, and every week helps us reflect on experiences, then every year allows us to see the direction of our entire life. Annual practice helps a person not live by inertia, but consciously choose the path of their further development. 1. Summing up the year At least once a year, stop and honestly answer yourself: What has changed in me? What have I learned? What was my greatest achievement? What mistakes became important lessons? What do I want to leave in the past? The past year becomes a teacher only when a person learns from it. 2. Testing ten levels of a person Assess the development of each level of your personality. Body. Have I become healthier and stronger? Subconscious. What habits have become part of my life? Psyche. How stable has my emotional state become? Consciousness. What knowledge changed my understanding of the world? Will. What promises have I kept to myself? Soul. Have I lived in alignment with my values? Spirit. Am I getting closer to my destiny? Meaning. What really became the main thing this year? Social connections. What relationships have been strengthened? Which ones require attention? Nature and the world. What useful thing have I done for the world around me? 3. Practice gratitude Give thanks for the passing year. Not only for joy. But also for the trials. For the people. For knowledge. For mistakes. For new opportunities. Gratitude helps us see progress where previously we only saw difficulties. 4. Practice forgiveness Make room for the new. Try to let go: old grievances; guilt; unnecessary conflicts; destructive habits; something that no longer helps your development. Forgiveness does not mean justifying the harm caused. It means refusing to allow the past to endlessly control the present. 5. Determining the direction Formulate the main goal for the next year. Not only material. Ask yourself: What kind of person do I want to become? What quality do I want to develop? What benefit do I want to bring to people? What do I want to learn? What will be my main contribution? Direction is more important than the number of goals. 6. Practice of renewal It's good to start something new every year. Master a profession. Learn the language. Read books. Start a project. Create a tradition. Plant a garden. Learn something you couldn't do before. Renewal helps the personality to continue to grow. 7. Practice of service Ask yourself: What will this year leave behind me? This could be: helping a person; raising a child; scientific work; tree; book; community project; restored nature; created community. A person grows when he begins to think not only about his own achievements, but also about his legacy. 8. Practice of unity with nature Spend a few days in nature every year. Forest. Mountains. Sea. Desert. River. Nature helps us see the long cycles of life. She reminds us that development takes time, patience and consistency. 9. Celebration of Life Note not only age. Celebrate development. Remember what kind of person you were a year ago. And notice what kind of person you have become today. A true holiday is a holiday of inner growth. DREVO's annual development formula Every year a person must: strengthen the body; refresh knowledge; develop character; strengthen the will; deepen love; open your soul; strengthen the spirit; create something useful; strengthen relationships; leave behind a good mark. The main principle You can't live a year over again. But every new year gives an opportunity to become a new person. Not richer. No more famous. And wiser. More free. More responsible. More loving. More creative. This is how a life is gradually built that a person can be truly proud of. Definition Annual practices are a system of consciously summing up results, renewing life direction, and setting new goals, aimed at the harmonious development of all levels of personality. In the New Psychology of DREVO, annual practice is viewed as a natural cycle of growth, allowing a person to transform the years lived not simply into age, but into wisdom, experience, and a creative legacy. Age is measured by the years one has lived. Maturity is measured by how much goodness, knowledge, love, and creativity one has brought to the world in each of those years.

title: Psychological ecology
excerpt: Psychological Ecology in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, a person is viewed as part of several interconnected systems. Of one's own organism. Families. Societies. Nature. Digital environment. Cultures.
text: Psychological Ecology in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, a person is viewed as part of several interconnected systems. Of one's own organism. Families. Societies. Nature. Digital environment. Cultures. Civilizations. Psychological health depends not only on a person’s internal state, but also on the quality of the environment in which he lives. Therefore, psychological ecology studies the conditions under which a person is able to maintain inner harmony, develop freely, and build healthy relationships with the outside world. What is psychological ecology? Psychological ecology is a system of principles and practices aimed at creating and maintaining an internal and external environment that promotes psychological health, free personal development, and harmonious relationships between people, society, and nature. Just as natural ecology studies the living conditions of organisms, psychological ecology studies the conditions of development of the human personality. Internal ecology Internal psychological ecology begins with caring for the person himself. It includes: health of the body; emotional balance; clarity of consciousness; development of will; loyalty to one's values; inner honesty; the ability to love; the presence of meaning in life. When a person's internal levels are aligned, it is easier for him to remain stable even in difficult circumstances. Ecology of Relationships A person develops through interaction with other people. Therefore, psychological ecology includes the culture of communication. It is based on: respect; trust; honesty; mutual support; listening abilities; peaceful resolution of conflicts; responsibility for one's words and actions. Every interaction either strengthens the psychological environment or destroys it. Information ecology Consciousness feeds on information. Therefore, a person is responsible for what he allows into his thinking every day. It is useful to choose: reliable knowledge; informative books; developmental communication; quality education; conscious use of digital technologies. Information chaos is gradually becoming psychological chaos. Ecology of space The environment influences a person’s internal state. Clean house. Cozy workplace. Wildlife. Beauty. Order. World. Silence. All these factors help the psyche to recover. By creating a harmonious space around oneself, a person simultaneously takes care of his inner world. Ecology of nature Man is a part of living nature. Therefore, caring for the environment becomes part of psychological health. Walks. Forest. Water. Mountains. Now. Working with the land. Observing nature helps people restore inner balance and a sense of connection with the world. Ecology of Culture Culture shapes human thinking. Music. Literature. Art. Language. Traditions. Education. All this influences the development of personality. A psychologically healthy culture supports respect for life, cooperation, creativity, and the search for truth. Ecology of the Future Every decision a person makes affects not only the present. It becomes part of the future environment for the next generations. Therefore, psychological ecology includes responsibility for the kind of world we create. For children. For society. For nature. For the future civilization. The practice of psychological ecology Every day a person can strengthen psychological ecology if: takes care of his health; consciously selects information; builds respectful relationships; limits the destructive impact of the digital environment; regularly interacts with nature; creates order and beauty around itself; helps other people; is engaged in creative activities. Psychological ecology begins with small daily decisions. The main principle A person becomes similar to the environment in which he lives. Therefore, caring for the inner world is impossible without caring for the outer world. By changing oneself, a person changes the environment. By changing the environment, he simultaneously changes himself. Definition Psychological ecology is the science and practice of creating conditions in which individuals, society, and the environment mutually contribute to psychological health, personal development, and a creative future. In DREVO's New Psychology, psychological ecology is the unifying principle of the entire system. It connects physical health, purity of consciousness, mental maturity, willpower, the development of the soul and spirit, the quality of relationships, culture, nature, technology, and responsibility to future generations. Just as a tree cannot thrive in poisoned soil, a person cannot maintain inner harmony in a destructive environment. By caring for ourselves, we care for the world. By caring for the world, we preserve ourselves. Development of will Development of Willpower in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, willpower is viewed as a person's ability to consciously control themselves, their thoughts, emotions, desires, and actions for the sake of a chosen goal and their own values. Will is not given to a person once and for all. She is developing. Like muscles, willpower is strengthened through regular practice. Every conscious decision makes her stronger. What strengthens the will? Willpower develops when a person regularly does what he believes is right, even if it requires effort. It is strengthened not by great feats, but by thousands of small daily decisions. Every time a person: keeps the promise he made to himself; completes the work started; overcomes the short-term desire to refuse; chooses long-term benefit over instant gratification, he strengthens his will. Basic principles of willpower development Mindfulness You can't manage yourself without understanding yourself. The first step is to notice your thoughts, emotions and desires. Awareness creates space for choice. Small steps Big changes start with small actions. It's better to keep a small promise to yourself every day than to make a big effort rarely. Consistency is stronger than jerks. Discipline Discipline is the habit of doing what is necessary regardless of your mood. It frees a person from dependence on random emotions. Discipline becomes an external form of manifestation of the inner will. Responsibility Willpower develops when a person stops looking for someone to blame and begins to take responsibility for his own decisions. Responsibility turns desire into action. Target The will needs direction. It is easier for a person to overcome difficulties when he understands why he is acting. The clearer the goal, the more stable the will. Meaning The strongest source of will becomes meaning. When a person understands why their actions are important, it is easier for them to remain persistent even in difficult circumstances. Practices for developing willpower It is useful to do small exercises every day. To restrain an unnecessary desire. Finish what you started. Get up on time. Fulfil the promise. Bring a difficult conversation to an end. Don't put off important matters. Tell the truth when it's hard. Do something useful, even if no one sees it. Each such action strengthens the ability to manage oneself. What weakens the will? The will is gradually weakened: constant procrastination; life without goals; lack of routine; chronic fatigue; dependencies; the habit of looking for excuses; disclaimer. Therefore, the development of willpower is impossible without caring for health and psychological well-being. Will and freedom Many people consider freedom to be the ability to do whatever they want. In the New Psychology of DREVO, freedom is understood differently. Truly free is the one who is able to choose not only what he wants, but also what is right. It is not a random desire that should control a person. A person must control his desires. It is the will that makes such freedom possible. The highest form of will The highest form of willpower is manifested when a person is able to remain true to his values ​​regardless of the circumstances. When it's difficult. When you're scared. When no one supports. When the result is not yet visible. It is at such moments that a person becomes the master of his own life. The main principle Willpower is not developed through struggle with oneself. It develops through conscious cooperation of body, psyche, consciousness, soul and spirit. When a person knows,Whatto do, understands,For whatto do this, and every day he takes at least one step forward, his will becomes stronger. Definition Developing willpower is the process of developing a person's ability to consciously manage their thoughts, emotions, desires, and actions while remaining true to their values ​​and long-term goals. In the New Psychology of DREVO, willpower is viewed as the central mechanism of personal self-governance, connecting consciousness with action. It is willpower that transforms knowledge into action, intentions into habits, and dreams into real change. Willpower is the art of choosing every day not the easiest thing, but what brings a person closer to the best version of himself. Revealing the Soul Revealing the Soul in New Psychology by DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, the soul is viewed as the inner core of the personality, the source of its uniqueness, conscience, love, beauty, and the ability to experience the deep meaning of life. Opening up your soul is not about acquiring something new. This is a gradual manifestation of the best that is already inherent in a person. Just as a seed gradually becomes a tree, the soul unfolds through life, experience, love, creativity and conscious choice.

title: What does it mean to open your soul?
excerpt: Soul revelation is a process of gradual manifestation of the inner qualities of a person, their true nature, talents, love, wisdom and the ability to live in harmony with their conscience and values. Every person is born
text: Soul revelation is a process of gradual manifestation of the inner qualities of a person, their true nature, talents, love, wisdom and the ability to live in harmony with their conscience and values. Every person is born with a certain potential. But only the person himself can turn this potential into real life. What helps to open the soul? Love Love helps a person to go beyond his own egoism. She teaches caring. Trust. Compassion. Creation. Through love the soul becomes open to the world. Truth The soul opens up when a person strives to live honestly. First of all, be honest with yourself. Self-deception gradually closes off the inner world. Honesty makes him freer. Creation A person reveals himself through creativity. It doesn't matter what exactly he creates. Picture. Book. Now. Music. Scientific discovery. Family. Community. By creating the world, a person simultaneously reveals his own soul. Service When a person begins to think not only about himself, his inner world becomes deeper. Helping people. Transfer of knowledge. Protection of nature. Raising children. Any activity that brings benefit to others contributes to the opening of the soul. Beauty The soul develops through contact with beauty. The beauty of nature. Music. Arts. Good deeds. Harmonious architecture. Human relationships. Beauty reminds a person of the possibility of living more harmoniously. Mindfulness Opening the soul is impossible without inner attention. It is helpful to ask yourself questions regularly. Who am I becoming? Are my actions consistent with my values? What makes me truly alive? What brings good to the world because of me? These questions help a person to better understand himself. What closes the soul? The soul does not disappear. But its manifestation may become less noticeable. This is facilitated by: lie; cruelty; constant hatred; indifference; destructive addictions; loss of meaning; renunciation of one's own conscience; life only for profit. The further a person moves away from his deepest values, the more difficult it is for him to feel inner integrity. Signs of an Opening Soul A person becomes: calmer; kinder; more honest; freer; more responsible; wiser; more capable of loving; more able to forgive; more capable of creating new things; more able to see the value of life. The revelation of the soul is manifested primarily in actions, not in words. Soul and Purpose The opening of the soul gradually helps a person understand his purpose. Not like a pre-written life script. But as a process of discovering one’s abilities, values, and the contribution that a person is capable of making to the world. The purpose is not found. It gradually unfolds along with the person. The main principle The soul is not revealed when a person talks a lot about spirituality. It is revealed when his life becomes a source of goodness, beauty, love, wisdom and creation. The more light a person brings into the lives of other people, the more brightly his own soul is revealed. Definition The revelation of the soul is the process of gradual manifestation of a person’s inner nature through love, conscience, creativity, service, striving for truth and a creative life. In the New Psychology of DREVO, soul-opening is seen as one of the main paths to personal development. It manifests itself not in unusual experiences, but in the kind of person one becomes and the mark they leave on the lives of others. Just as a tree reveals its nature through growth, flowering, and fruit, the soul reveals itself through actions. The true beauty of the soul becomes visible when, thanks to a person, the world becomes more alive, loving, and kind. Strengthening the spirit Strengthening the Spirit in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, the spirit is viewed as an internal vector of a person, connecting his life with higher values, purpose and future. If the body answers the question"How to live?", psyche —"What do I feel?", consciousness - "What to choose?", then the spirit answers the question: "What do I live for?" Strengthening your spirit is the process of developing inner resilience, loyalty to your values, and the ability to maintain direction in life no matter the circumstances. What does strong spirit mean? A strong spirit is a person’s ability to remain faithful to truth, conscience, love and one’s purpose even during difficult periods of life. The spirit does not manifest itself when everything is easy. It manifests itself when a person has to choose between what is convenient and what is right. What strengthens the spirit? Loyalty to your values Every time a person acts in accordance with his conscience, his spirit becomes stronger. Even if it requires sacrifice. Even if no one notices. Inner honesty strengthens the spirit. Responsibility A person with a strong spirit does not shift responsibility to circumstances. He asks himself: What depends on me? What can I change? What would be the right next step? Responsibility makes the spirit mature. Overcoming difficulties The spirit develops through trials. It is not the difficulties themselves that make a person stronger. What makes him stronger is how he goes through them. Every challenge overcome becomes part of the inner support. Service The spirit is strengthened when a person begins to live not only for himself. Helping people. Protection of nature. Knowledge creation. Raising children. Development of society. Service connects personal life with a broader meaning. Long-term thinking A strong spirit can look beyond today. He thinks about the future. About the next generations. About heritage. About the consequences of your actions. This perspective helps you make more mature decisions. Continuous development The spirit weakens in a state of internal stagnation. It is strengthened through: training; reflection; creativity; new challenges; overcoming one's own limitations. Development becomes a natural need of a strong spirit. What weakens the spirit? The spirit gradually loses its power if a person: constantly acts against his conscience; disclaims responsibility; loses direction in life; lives only for immediate gain; stops developing; allows fear to completely control his life. This does not mean that the spirit disappears. This means that it becomes more difficult for a person to follow his or her deepest values. Spiritual strengthening practices Useful regularly: keep the promises you make to yourself; do what is right even if it is difficult; read books that develop your worldview; reflect on life's purpose; help other people; spend time in nature; create long-term projects; Do at least one thing every day that you can be proud of. The spirit is strengthened through consistent living, not through occasional emotional experiences. Spirit and Freedom True freedom is impossible without a strong spirit. A person becomes free when he is able to preserve his values ​​regardless of external pressure. Freedom without an inner core easily turns into a chaotic pursuit of random desires. The spirit helps a person maintain direction. The main principle The spirit cannot be strengthened by words. Life strengthens him. Every honest choice. Every fear overcome. Every duty fulfilled. Every creative act. This is how the inner core of the personality is gradually formed. Definition Strengthening your spirit is the process of developing inner resilience, responsibility, loyalty to your values, and the ability to maintain direction in life regardless of external circumstances. In the New Psychology of DREVO, spirit is viewed as an internal compass that connects a person to their highest values, purpose, and long-term goals. A strong spirit helps a person remain human even when circumstances become difficult. A tree doesn't become strong when there's no wind. It becomes strong because it continues to grow despite the wind. Likewise, a person's spirit is strengthened not by an easy life, but by remaining true to one's path amidst trials. Search for purpose Finding Purpose in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, purpose is not seen as a pre-written fate or as the only profession a person is obliged to find. Purpose is a direction in life in which a person’s abilities, values, and the needs of the world begin to coincide. It is not given to a person in a ready-made form. It is gradually revealed through experience, learning, mistakes, work and creation. Finding your purpose is finding your place in life. What is purpose? Purpose is the most complete form of realization of human abilities, bringing benefit to himself, other people and the future. Purpose connects three questions: What can I do? What is really important to me? How can I be useful to the world? Where these three directions intersect, purpose begins to emerge. Purpose is not found instantly Many people expect to one day receive a clear answer to the question: "What is my purpose?" But in life things often happen differently. The purpose is revealed gradually. Through work. Through mistakes. Through meetings with people. Through new knowledge. Through overcoming difficulties. It's more like growing a tree than finding hidden treasure.

title: Signs of your path
excerpt: A person gradually approaches his destiny when: feels a deep meaning in his activities; wants to constantly develop in the chosen direction; feels satisfaction not only from the result, but also from the process itself;
text: A person gradually approaches his destiny when: feels a deep meaning in his activities; wants to constantly develop in the chosen direction; feels satisfaction not only from the result, but also from the process itself; sees that his work benefits other people; maintains the desire to continue even after failures. The difficulties do not disappear. But an understanding emerges as to why it is worth overcoming them. What prevents you from finding your purpose? Finding your way can be complicated: fear of mistakes; the desire to meet other people's expectations; lack of experience; constant comparison of oneself with others; living only for material gain; refusal to try new things; lack of faith in one's own abilities. Sometimes a person needs to stop looking for a purpose and stop being afraid to take the first step. How to find purpose? In the New Psychology of DREVO, the search for purpose begins with self-examination. It is useful to ask questions. What am I interested in studying even without external coercion? Which abilities do I exhibit most easily? What do people thank me for? What problems in the world do I want to solve? What activities bring a feeling of inner fulfillment? If success were guaranteed, what would I dedicate my life to? Answers to these questions rarely appear immediately. They become clearer as experience accumulates. Purpose and ministry Purpose does not exist separately from other people. Even the most personal talents acquire true meaning when they begin to bring benefit. True purpose always connects the development of the individual with the development of society. A person reveals himself by helping life around him to reveal itself. Purpose changes with a person At different periods of life, a person can perform different tasks. Study. Start a family. Develop the profession. To pass on knowledge. Create projects. Help society. The form of purpose may change. But his inner direction—the desire to realize his best qualities for the benefit of life—remains. Practice asked for purposes Each month it is helpful to answer five questions: What brought me the greatest joy from creation? In what activities did I feel most alive? Where were my abilities particularly useful? What do I want to develop in myself further? What's the next step that will bring me closer to a life I'm proud of? Purpose is revealed through action, not through waiting. The main principle Purpose is not something a person finds one day. This is what he gradually creates with his life. Every honest act. Every new skill. Every help to another person. Every creative project. They all become part of the journey. Definition Finding one's purpose is the process of recognizing and realizing one's abilities, values, and life direction through creative activity that benefits the individual, society, and future generations. In the New Psychology of DREVO, purpose is viewed as a natural result of harmonious personal development. It is revealed not through waiting for a special sign, but through continuous learning, work, service, creativity, and responsibility for one's contribution to the world. A tree doesn't ask what it will become. It grows, revealing all that was contained in its seed. So too, a person finds their purpose when, day after day, they uncover their best qualities and transform them into a benefit to life. Family development Family Development in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, the family is considered the first and most important environment for human development. It is in the family that a child first learns love, trust, cooperation, responsibility and mutual care. But a family exists not only for the sake of raising children. It is a space for joint development of all its members. A strong family helps every person become stronger. And strong personalities make a family stronger. What is family? A family is a voluntary union of people united by love, trust, mutual responsibility, and the desire to jointly create conditions for the development, support, and continuation of life. The main value of a family lies not only in living together. It consists of joint development. The foundation of the family In the New Psychology of DREVO, a strong family is built on five pillars. Love. The desire to care and help each other develop. Trust. Confidence in the honesty and support of loved ones. Respect. Recognition of the dignity of each family member. Responsibility. Willingness to fulfill one's responsibilities and take care of the well-being of the family. Cooperation. The ability to solve problems together and create a common future. If one of these pillars weakens, it becomes more difficult for the family to remain stable. Family as a space for development Each family member is both a student and a teacher. Children learn from their parents. Parents learn responsibility. The elderly pass on their experience. Young people bring new ideas. The family becomes a place where knowledge, traditions and love are passed down between generations. Family traditions Traditions strengthen the sense of unity. These could be: shared dinners; family holidays; trips; reading books; gardening; joint creativity; helping other people. Regular shared activities create a common family history. Conflict resolution Conflicts are inevitable in any family. Their presence does not mean the absence of love. The main thing is how the family overcomes them. In the New Psychology of DREVO, conflict becomes an opportunity to better understand each other. Important: speak honestly; listen carefully; look for a solution, not someone to blame; respect the dignity of every person. The victory of one over another rarely strengthens the family. The real victory is maintaining the relationship and finding a way out together. Family and children The main task of parents is not to make the child comfortable. The main task is to help him become an independent, responsible and kind person. The best education does not come through words. It happens through personal example. Children often imitate their parents' lifestyle rather than their advice. Family and Personal Development A good family helps a person: feel safe; to reveal abilities; learn responsibility; to experience difficulties; maintain internal stability; find support. The family becomes a place where a person can regain strength and re-enter the world. Family and Society Every family influences society. Strong families build strong communities. Strong communities make stable states. Therefore, the development of society begins with the development of family culture. Family development practice Useful regularly: spend time together without phones; discuss family plans; thank each other; learn new things together; help other people together; create family traditions; talk openly about feelings; spend time together in nature. A family develops through common activities, not just through living together. The main principle Family is not a place where people just live next to each other. This is a place where people help each other become better. A true family is measured not by the number of years lived together, but by the amount of love, trust, support and shared creation. Definition Family development is a process of strengthening love, trust, responsibility, cooperation, and mutual growth among all its members, creating conditions for the harmonious development of the individual and the transmission of values ​​to future generations. In the New Psychology of DREVO, the family is viewed as the first school of humanity, where people learn to love, respect, cooperate, and accept responsibility for others. The development of the family is the foundation for the development of society and future civilization. Just as a tree becomes strong thanks to strong roots, a person becomes strong thanks to a family in which love is transformed into daily actions and life together becomes a shared development. Community development Community Development in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, community is viewed as a space for the voluntary association of people bound by common values, goals, and a desire to co-create the future. If the family is the first environment for personality development, then the community becomes the first school of cooperation. It is in communities that a person learns to combine his abilities with the abilities of other people. Community development is the development of a culture of trust, mutual responsibility and collective creativity. What is a community? A community is a voluntary association of people based on common values, mutual respect, cooperation and shared responsibility for a common cause. A community is different from a random group of people. It is not only the place or the interest that unites him. It is united by a common goal. Community Foundation In New Psychology DREVO, a healthy community is built on several principles. Common values. People understand why they are uniting. Trust. Each participant knows that he is respected and supported. Responsibility. Everyone makes their contribution to the common cause. Freedom of participation. A person remains a free individual. Cooperation is not built on coercion. Creation. The main goal of the community is to create, not to destroy. Why does a person need a community? One person can do a lot. But together people are able to create what is impossible alone. The community helps: share knowledge; support each other; solve complex problems; implement large projects; to pass on experience; to reveal talents. Through community, a person becomes part of something greater than himself.

title: Community culture
excerpt: A strong community is created not by rules, but by culture. This culture is manifested in: respect; open dialogue; honesty; mutual assistance; conflict resolution skills; gratitude; willingness to learn from each other.
text: A strong community is created not by rules, but by culture. This culture is manifested in: respect; open dialogue; honesty; mutual assistance; conflict resolution skills; gratitude; willingness to learn from each other. Culture defines the atmosphere in which each participant develops. Community and Individuality A good community does not suppress individuality. It helps a person to reveal his abilities. Each participant has unique knowledge, experience and talents. Diversity becomes a source of strength rather than a cause of division. The richer the differences, the higher the potential for joint development. Community and collective intelligence In the New Psychology of DREVO, the community is the environment for the formation of collective intelligence. People unite: knowledge; experience; ideas; skills; resources. Collaborative thinking allows us to find solutions that rarely arise in isolation. Collective intelligence becomes a natural extension of a collaborative culture. Community and Leadership A true leader does not control people for his own power. He helps people to discover their abilities. Its task is to unite. Support. Create conditions for development. Transfer responsibility. A strong leader makes the entire community stronger. Community and Society From small communities, a society gradually forms. When communities are built on trust, cooperation and responsibility, society becomes more resilient. When communities collapse, social institutions weaken. Therefore, the development of civilization begins with the development of human communities. Community Development Practice Every community is strengthened when its members: meet regularly; make decisions together; help new members; share knowledge; implement common projects; support a culture of respect; openly discuss emerging difficulties; celebrate shared achievements. Community grows through shared experiences. The main principle Community is a place where a person stops asking: "What can I get?" And he begins to ask: "What can we create together?" It is at this moment that cooperation becomes a source of development. Definition Community development is the process of strengthening a culture of trust, cooperation, collective responsibility, and co-creation, enabling people to pool their abilities for the common good. In DREVO's New Psychology, community is seen as a natural environment for personal development, the formation of collective intelligence, and the creation of a sustainable society. Just as a forest is stronger than any single tree because of the relationships between them, a human community becomes stronger when each person reveals their talents and voluntarily combines them with the talents of others for the sake of a common future. Diary of desires Self-knowledge practice in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, desires are seen as one of the ways in which a person gets to know himself. Every desire communicates some need. Sometimes - the needs of the body. Sometimes - psyche. Sometimes - the desire of the soul. Sometimes - the direction of the spirit. However, not every wish should be fulfilled immediately. First, it needs to be understood. This is exactly what the Wish Diary is for. What is a Wish Diary? A desire journal is a practice of regularly recording and analyzing your desires, which helps a person better understand their needs, values, motives, and life direction. His goal is not to compile a dream list. Its goal is to learn to distinguish random desires from those that truly help personal development. Why keep a Wish Diary? Regular entries help you see: what is really important to me; what desires are repeated; what desires are imposed by others; what desires are born from fear; some - out of love and a desire for development. Gradually, a person begins to understand himself better. How to keep a Wish Diary? Every day or several times a week, write down the desires that arise during the day. Don't judge them right away. Don't judge yourself. Just write it down. Even the most unusual desires can tell a lot about a person’s inner world. Questions for analysis After some time, it is useful to ask yourself questions. Why did this particular desire arise? What need does it express? Is this a desire of the body? Psychics? Consciousness? Souls? Spirit? Will its implementation help my development? Will I be happy with this in a year? In ten years? If a desire is only for short-term pleasure, it's worth considering whether it satisfies deeper needs. Desire and values Not every desire corresponds to a person’s values. Sometimes a desire brings short-term pleasure but conflicts with its long-term goals. Therefore, it is important to ask yourself: Does this align with my values? Does this bring me closer to the person I want to become? Does this benefit not only me, but also those around me? Desires become creative when they are combined with values. Desire and goal Desire answers the question: "What do I want?" The target responds: "What am I willing to do to achieve this?" Will transforms desire into action. Therefore, a diary helps to gradually turn desires into real plans. Desire and Purpose If a person notices over many months or years that certain desires constantly return and are associated with development, creativity or helping people, this may indicate the direction of his destiny. Purpose is revealed not through random desires, but through stable aspirations, tested by time and actions. Practice of the month Reread your notes once a month. Please note: what wishes have already come true; which have ceased to be important; which ones are repeated most often; what desires became goals; which brought you closer to development. This analysis allows us to see how the personality changes. The main principle Desires do not make a person weak. They help to understand where his internal energy is directed. Wisdom does not consist in giving up all desires. Wisdom lies in choosing those desires that make life deeper, freer and more creative. Definition A desire journal is a practice of self-observation and self-analysis that allows a person to consciously explore their desires, understand the needs behind them, and transform true aspirations into life goals and creative actions. In the New Psychology of DREVO, the Desire Diary is viewed as a tool for developing consciousness, willpower, and self-knowledge. It helps one distinguish random impulses from the true aspirations of the soul and gradually find one's direction in life. Desires are like seeds. Not every seed is destined to sprout. But it's precisely by paying close attention to them that a person can cultivate the tree of their life into the one they truly desire. Daily newspaper Life Management Practice in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, the diary is seen as a tool for consciously managing one's life. Most people only plan things to do. But a mature person plans not only tasks. She plans her development. Every day becomes a step towards the person a person strives to become. A diary helps connect thoughts with actions, goals with habits, and purpose with everyday life. What is a diary? A diary is a planning and self-organization tool that allows a person to consciously manage their time, resources, development, and life direction. The main goal of a diary is not to fill the day with things to do. The main task is to live the day meaningfully. Morning planning It is helpful to answer a few questions every morning. What is the main goal of today? What three things are really important? What will help me become better today? Who can I help today? What am I grateful for? This is how a conscious day begins. Balance of the day In the New Psychology of DREVO, it is advisable to devote attention to the main areas of life every day. Body Movement. Nutrition. Dream. Rest. Intelligence Training. Reading. Reflection. Learning new things. Creation Work. Creativity. Projects. Practice. Relationship Family. Friends. Community. Support from other people. Soul and spirit Silence. Reflection. Nature. Gratitude. Loyalty to your values. The main rule Don't overload your day. It's better to do three really important things than to write down twenty and not complete any of them. A completed task strengthens the will. Unfinished business gradually drains attention. Evening analysis Before going to bed, it is helpful to answer a few questions. What happened today? What was the most valuable? What have I learned? What good deed have I done? What can be done better tomorrow? Thus the day turns into experience, and experience into wisdom. Development diary In addition to the to-do list, it is useful to note: mood; energy level; physical activity; new knowledge; good deeds; ideas; gratitude; steps towards long-term goals. After a few months, such a diary allows you to see real changes in your personality. DREVO's One-Day Formula It is advisable to take at least one step every day: for health; for knowledge; for family; for society; for nature; for its intended purpose. Even a small step is better than no action at all. The main principle Man does not control time. He controls his attention, his decisions and his actions. It is they who gradually create his life. Every day lived becomes part of one's character. Every choice made becomes part of destiny. Definition A diary is a tool for conscious life management, allowing you to plan not only your daily activities, but also your personal development, health, relationships, knowledge, willpower, and life purpose. In DREVO's New Psychology, a daily planner is seen as a practical bridge between values ​​and actions. It helps people transform their daily intentions into real actions and gradually build the life they desire. Life doesn't change on the day of a great decision. It changes every ordinary day when a person consciously chooses the next right step.

title: Dream Diary
excerpt: Self-knowledge practice in the New Psychology of DREVO In New Psychology DREVO, sleep is viewed as a natural part of human life, during which the body recovers and the brain continues to process experiences. Dreams can r
text: Self-knowledge practice in the New Psychology of DREVO In New Psychology DREVO, sleep is viewed as a natural part of human life, during which the body recovers and the brain continues to process experiences. Dreams can reflect experiences, memories, emotions, creative ideas and images that arise from the work of the brain. For some people, they also become a source of personal symbols and reflections. A dream diary helps you not only predict the future, but also better understand yourself. What is a Dream Diary? A dream journal is the practice of regularly recording and analyzing dreams, allowing one to observe recurring images, emotional states, and changes in one's inner world. The main goal of the diary is to develop self-observation. Not a search for mystical predictions. Why is it important to write down your dreams? Dreams are quickly forgotten. By writing down your dream immediately after waking up, you can preserve details that will disappear from your memory within minutes. Over time, the recordings begin to reveal patterns. Some themes are repeated. Some images change. Some experiences are reflected in dreams even before a person becomes aware of them in everyday life. How to keep a Dream Diary? After waking up, try to immediately write down: date; wake-up time; dream content; participants in the dream; place of action; main events; your feelings in a dream; feelings after waking up. Don't try to immediately explain what you saw. First, save it as accurately as possible. Sleep analysis After some time, ask yourself questions. What feelings did this dream evoke? What in my life resembles events in a dream? Does this image repeat itself? Is there a connection with recent events? Did a new perspective on the problem emerge in the dream?
