In New Psychology DREVO, the meaning of a dream is sought primarily in a person’s personal experience. The same symbol can have different meanings for different people. Dreams and the psyche Modern science offers different explanations for the functions of sleep and dreams. It is believed that during sleep the brain is involved in processing information, consolidating memory, emotional adaptation and creative search for solutions. Many questions about the nature of dreams remain the subject of research. Therefore, the New Psychology DREVO does not consider dreams as absolute predictions or a source of objective knowledge about the future. Dreams and Creativity Sometimes ideas are born in dreams. Music. Paintings. Scientific hypotheses. Engineering solutions. Therefore, along with the description of the dream, it is useful to write down all the thoughts and inspiration that arose after waking up. Some of them may be valuable. Dreams and Personality Development Gradually the diary helps you notice: recurring fears; internal conflicts; changes in emotional state; new stages of life; creativity; change of worldview. In this way, a person better understands his own psyche. Practice of the month Reread the entries once a month. Please note: What symbols are most common? What emotions are repeated? Has the nature of your dreams changed? Have any new ideas emerged? This overview helps to see internal processes that are difficult to notice in one day. The main principle Sleep is not a separate life. It is a continuation of human life. Understanding one's dreams does not give a person ready-made answer. He gets the opportunity to better understand himself. Definition A dream journal is a practice of observing, recording, and understanding dreams, aimed at developing self-knowledge, understanding emotional processes, creative thinking, and the inner world of a person. In DREVO's New Psychology, a dream diary is viewed as a tool for exploring the psyche and personal experience. It helps one notice patterns reflecting experiences, personality changes, and processes of internal development, without replacing scientific analysis with mystical explanations. Just as daylight helps us see the outside world, paying attention to our dreams can help us better understand the inner world. A diary of desires as a way to shape reality The practice of conscious programming of the future in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, the Wish Diary is viewed not as a magical way to fulfill desires, but as a tool for shaping personality, thinking, and behavior that increases the likelihood of achieving what you want. What a person regularly focuses on gradually begins to influence his decisions, habits and actions. It's not just the thinking that changes. The person himself changes. And along with it, the reality surrounding it begins to change. Why is writing before bed especially important? Before sleep, the brain gradually switches from actively processing external information to internal processing of experience. The last thoughts of the day often become part of the processes of memory, emotional processing, and planning of future actions. Therefore, the evening is a good time to calmly reflect on your goals and desires. Regular practice helps keep your focus on the long-term direction of development. The main principle Consciousness shapes choice. Choice shapes actions. Actions form habits. Habits shape character. Character gradually shapes a person's life reality. Therefore, a person changes his life first of all by changing himself. How to write down wishes correctly? In the New Psychology DREVO, it is recommended to write down your desires as if they have already become a part of your life. Not because the recording automatically creates reality. Because this method helps the consciousness to more clearly imagine the desired state and see the path to it. For example: I created a friendly and loving family. I am developing a project that is useful for society. I am healthy, energetic and strengthen my body daily. I speak English fluently. Such formulations create an internal image of the future, towards which a person begins to gradually move. Desire must correspond to values Not every desire contributes to development. Before recording, it is useful to ask yourself: Does this align with my values? Will this benefit me and others? Will I be happy with this in ten years? Does this help reveal my personality? The deeper a desire is connected to development, the more it becomes part of the life path. After recordings - action A wish journal is not a substitute for action. It helps to determine the direction. After each wish, it is useful to write down one specific step that can be taken tomorrow. For example: Desire:I created a successful educational platform. Tomorrow:Write an outline for the first chapter. It is actions that turn desire into reality. Gratitude After writing down your wishes, it is helpful to end the day with gratitude. Write down three things you are grateful for today. This helps to see not only the future, but also the value of the present. A person develops simultaneously in two directions: creates the future; and notices the richness of the present. DREVO practice Every evening: Relax and unwind from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Write down 3-10 desires in the present tense and in a positive form. Make sure they align with your values. Write down one small step for tomorrow. Give thanks to life for today. Go to bed with a sense of calm, not expectation of a miracle. This is how the habit of living consciously and moving in the chosen direction is gradually formed. The main principle Man creates his reality not by the power of thought itself. He creates it through thoughts, which become decisions, decisions become actions, actions become habits, and habits gradually change his life. A wish diary helps you direct this process consciously. Definition A vision journal is a practice of consciously recording your desired future, allowing you to formulate a clear direction for your development, strengthen your motivation, align your goals with your values, and transform your inner aspirations into consistent actions. In the New Psychology of DREVO, writing down one's desires before bed is seen as a way to tune one's consciousness to long-term development. It helps one see one's goals more clearly, recognize new opportunities, and make daily choices that bring one closer to their desired future. First, a person creates an image of the future in their mind. Then this image begins to guide their actions. And it is these actions that gradually create a new reality. Meditation as autogenic training Meditation in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, meditation is viewed as a method of conscious self-regulation of the psyche, attention, and state of the body. Her goal is not to “escape reality,” but to learn to better manage herself. Meditation helps calm the flow of thoughts, reduce internal tension, restore attention and strengthen the ability to consciously choose your reactions. In its essence, it is close to autogenic training - a system of psychophysiological self-regulation based on relaxation, concentration and internal attitudes. What is meditation? Meditation is a practice of consciously managing attention, breathing, body state, and internal dialogue, aimed at restoring mental balance, developing awareness, and strengthening a person’s ability to manage themselves. The main object of meditation is not the external world, but one’s own internal state.

title: What is autogenic training?
excerpt: Autogenic training is a scientifically developed method of mental self-regulation based on muscle relaxation, calm breathing, concentration, and the use of verbal instructions. In the New Psychology DREVO it is considere
text: Autogenic training is a scientifically developed method of mental self-regulation based on muscle relaxation, calm breathing, concentration, and the use of verbal instructions. In the New Psychology DREVO it is considered as one of the forms of meditative practice. Its task is to help a person independently regulate their condition without external influence. How does meditation affect a person? Regular practice helps: reducing the level of internal stress; improving concentration; development of emotional stability; faster recovery from stress; better awareness of one's own thoughts and feelings; strengthening self-control. These effects are confirmed by many psychological and neurophysiological studies, although the severity of the results depends on the individual and the regularity of practice. Meditation and the Ten Levels of Man Body Muscle tension is reduced. Breathing slows down. The body goes into recovery mode. Subconscious It becomes possible to more calmly observe automatic reactions and habits. Psyche Emotions become more stable. A person more easily notices his state before it begins to control his behavior. Consciousness The ability to hold attention develops. Thoughts become clearer. Will Each return of attention to the chosen object trains the ability to control oneself. Meditation becomes an exercise in willpower. Soul More inner silence appears. It becomes easier for a person to hear their deepest values ​​and motives. Spirit Practice helps us remember the main direction of life and not get lost in the daily hustle and bustle. DREVO Meditation Practice Duration: 10–20 minutes daily. Subsequence: Sit comfortably. Straighten your back. Take a few calm breaths in and out. Relax the muscles of your face, shoulders, stomach and legs. Turn your attention to your breathing. If thoughts arise, calmly notice them and return to your breathing. After relaxation, you can pronounce several internal attitudes. For example: "I am calm." "My body is relaxed." "My attention is becoming clearer." "I act consciously." "Today I will take another step towards my development." After completing your meditation, it is helpful to sit quietly for a few minutes before returning to your daily activities. Meditation and Real Life The purpose of meditation is not to have special experiences. Its goal is to change the quality of everyday life. If after practice a person becomes: calmer; more carefully; kinder; more responsible; freer in your reactions, This means that meditation is fulfilling its purpose. The main principle True meditation does not end when a person opens his eyes. It continues in every conscious action. The peace found within must be expressed in one's outer life. Definition Meditation is a practice of mental self-regulation aimed at developing awareness, concentration, emotional stability, and a person’s ability to manage their internal state. In DREVO's New Psychology, meditation is viewed as a form of autogenic training that combines physical relaxation, attention management, willpower development, and inner self-exploration. Its goal is not escapism, but rather an improvement in quality of life, personal maturity, and the capacity for conscious creation. A person doesn't become stronger because the world becomes quieter. They become stronger when they learn to maintain inner silence amidst the noise of the world. Part VI. Psychology of Society From individual to society The new psychology of DREVO views a person not as an isolated individual, but as part of a living social system. Just as the health of a cell cannot be separated from the health of the entire organism, a person's psychological health cannot be completely separated from the state of the family, community, culture, and society. Man simultaneously shapes society and is shaped by it. Therefore, the development of the individual and the development of society are two sides of the same process. The principle of social development The quality of society is determined by the quality of people, and the quality of people is largely determined by the quality of society. A healthy society helps people to develop their potential. Mature people create a healthy society. This process forms a continuous cycle of development. Family psychology The family is the first school of the individual. It is in the family that a person first learns: trust; love; cooperation; responsibility; respect; conflict resolution. A strong family becomes a source of psychological stability and the transmission of life experience between generations. Community Psychology A person develops faster in an environment of like-minded people. The community creates space for: mutual support; knowledge exchange; joint creativity; education; implementation of common projects. A true community unites people not through fear or coercion, but through shared values ​​and voluntary cooperation. Psychology of Culture Culture preserves the collective experience of humanity. Language. Music. Art. Literature. Customs. History. They shape a person’s worldview and help pass on knowledge to new generations. Without culture, society loses its memory. Educational Psychology Education should develop not only memory, but also personality. Its task is to educate a person who is capable of: think independently; accept responsibility; cooperate; create something new; maintain critical thinking; respect the dignity of other people. The main goal of education is to teach a person to learn throughout life. Labor psychology Work is one of the forms of human self-realization. Creative work allows a person to develop their abilities, benefit society, and feel their own significance. Work becomes a source of development when it has meaning and creates value for others. Psychology of leadership A true leader does not rule through fear. It unites people around a common goal. Leadership is built on: by personal example; responsibility; competence; trust; respect; ability to inspire. The more power a person receives, the greater his responsibility to society becomes. Psychology of cooperation The development of civilization occurs through cooperation. Working together allows us to create what cannot be done alone. Trust, open dialogue, fair sharing of responsibilities and respect for the dignity of every person are the foundations of a sustainable society. Psychology of conflict Conflict arises when interests, needs or values ​​clash. Conflict in itself is not evil. The methods of its resolution become destructive. The new psychology of DREVO views conflict as an opportunity to better understand each other, find a fair solution, and strengthen relationships. Psychology of a Creative Society A creative society is distinguished by the fact that it creates conditions for the development of human potential. Its signs are: respect for human dignity; accessible education; development of sciences; strong families; healthy communities; caring for nature; support for creativity; fair rules; high culture of cooperation; responsibility to future generations. The main law of society Society develops when the development of each person enhances the development of other people. Personal well-being and public good are not opposed to each other. They mutually reinforce each other. The more a person creates for society, the richer society becomes. The stronger a society is, the more opportunities it creates for the development of each individual. DREVO's Vision The new psychology of DREVO views society as a living ecosystem, where each individual is like a tree in a shared forest. A strong forest is impossible without healthy trees. But even an individual tree cannot fully develop without a healthy ecosystem. Therefore, the highest goal of personal development is not only one's own well-being, but also participation in the creation of a society in which current and future generations can develop freely. True development begins when a person stops asking, “What should society give me?” and begins asking, “What kind of society am I helping to create with my thoughts, actions, and example?” Family psychology Family is the first school of life In the New Psychology DREVO, the family is viewed as a natural environment in which a person’s personality is formed. It is in the family that a child first becomes acquainted with love, trust, security, responsibility, cooperation and mutual respect. The family is not only a union of people, but also a space for the transmission of life, culture, values ​​and life experience from generation to generation. The main task of the family The main task of the family is to create conditions in which each member can safely develop, reveal their abilities and become a mature individual. The family should help a person: to feel loved; feel safe; learn responsibility; respect others; develop independence; to reveal one's abilities; prepare for adult life. The foundation of a healthy family A healthy family is built on several principles. Love Love is not just a feeling. It is daily care, respect and a desire to contribute to the development of another person. Trust Without trust, it is impossible to create a sense of psychological security. Trust comes from honesty, openness and keeping your promises. Responsibility Each family member is responsible for their words, actions and contribution to the general well-being. Responsibility does not mean control. It means being willing to take care of each other. Freedom Every person has the right to remain an individual. Love does not require giving up one's own individuality. A healthy family supports the development of each individual. Cooperation Family is a team. Its strength is determined not by who is in charge, but by how well its members are able to negotiate, help each other, and jointly solve emerging problems. The role of parents Parents are the child's first mentors. The main method of education is not words, but personal example. Children first of all adopt the lifestyle of adults. Therefore, education begins with educating oneself. The role of children Children are not the property of their parents, but independent individuals. The family's task is to help the child discover his or her abilities, teach them to think independently, make decisions, and gradually take responsibility for their own lives. Conflicts Conflicts are inevitable in any family. They arise because each person has their own needs, views and experiences. The goal of the family is not to avoid conflicts at any cost, but to learn to resolve them through respectful dialogue, mutual understanding, and the search for fair solutions. Every conflict can be an opportunity to better understand each other and strengthen relationships. Family traditions Shared holidays, common activities, travel, family stories and rituals strengthen the sense of unity. They create emotional memories of the family and help children feel a sense of belonging to something greater than themselves. Family and Society Strong families become the foundation of a strong society. It is in the family that future citizens, scientists, teachers, entrepreneurs, artists, engineers and parents of the next generation are formed. Therefore, caring for the family is at the same time caring for the future of society. The main principle Family does not exist for mutual control or to satisfy each other's expectations. It exists for joint development. Each family member helps others become healthier, freer, more responsible and happier. It is in such a family that love becomes not only a feeling, but also a daily practice of creation. Definition A family is a voluntary union of people based on love, trust, respect, responsibility and cooperation, the purpose of which is the mutual development of the individual, the upbringing of a new generation and the preservation of life, culture and human values. In DREVO's New Psychology, the family is viewed as the first and most important human ecosystem. The healthier this ecosystem, the greater the opportunities for the harmonious development of each member and society as a whole.

title: Psychology of the family
excerpt: The family as the continuity of life In the New Psychology DREVO, the family is viewed as an unbroken chain of generations through which life, culture, language, traditions, experience, and heritage are passed on to a pe
text: The family as the continuity of life In the New Psychology DREVO, the family is viewed as an unbroken chain of generations through which life, culture, language, traditions, experience, and heritage are passed on to a person. Every person is both the heir of the past and the creator of the future. He gains the experience of previous generations and passes it on to the next, supplementing it with his own knowledge, actions and discoveries. The genus as a system The genus is a living system that exists in time. Each generation influences the next through: upbringing; family traditions; cultural values; language; worldview; skills; material and cultural heritage; and also through biological heredity. Modern science confirms the influence of genetics, family environment, and certain epigenetic mechanisms on human development. Broader claims about the transmission of specific psychological experiences or destinies require caution and further research. Family legacy Each family passes on not only material resources. He conveys: knowledge; crafts; life experience; ways to solve problems; moral guidelines; family stories; attitude to work; attitude towards people; attitude towards nature. Heritage becomes the foundation on which the development of new generations is built. Responsibility to the family A person is not obliged to repeat the life of his ancestors. However, he can understand their experience, preserve the best and change what hinders development. Respect for one's family does not mean blind adherence to traditions. It means a conscious attitude towards one’s origins and responsibility for what will be passed on. Development of the genus Each generation gets the opportunity to make the family stronger. This happens through: education; honest work; health care; raising children; preservation of culture; development of sciences; creative activity; mutual support. The development of one person becomes a contribution to the development of the entire family. Gender and personality The individual retains freedom of choice. Origin influences a person, but does not completely determine his destiny. Everyone is capable of: build on the strengths of your heritage; rethink limiting family attitudes; create new traditions; to pass on more mature experience to future generations. Thus, a person becomes not only a continuer of the family, but also its transformer. Clan and Society The society consists of many families and clans. The more families maintain a culture of cooperation, respect, responsibility and education, the more resilient the society becomes. Therefore, strengthening the family and clan is simultaneously a contribution to the development of the entire country and humanity. The main principle Family is not only a memory of the past. Family is responsibility for the future. True respect for one's ancestors is not expressed in the idealization of the past, but in the desire to make the life of the next generation healthier, freer, wiser, and more creative. Definition A family is an unbroken community of generations, united by origin, culture, memory and heritage, through which life, experience and values ​​are transmitted. In New Psychology DREVO, family psychology explores how heredity, family culture, upbringing, and intergenerational experience influence personality development, as well as how people can consciously preserve the best of their heritage and create a new legacy for future generations. Community Psychology Community as a space for development In the New Psychology of DREVO, a community is viewed as a voluntary association of people connected by common values, goals, and mutual responsibility. If the family is the first environment for human development, and the clan connects generations, then the community becomes a space where a person learns to cooperate with people who are not related to him by family ties. It is in community that the individual begins to transform his or her abilities into a common contribution. Why does a person need a community? A person cannot fully realize his potential alone. Ideas are born in dialogue. Knowledge develops through exchange. Culture is created through collaborative creativity. Technologies emerge through collaboration. Community allows many people to combine their abilities to achieve goals that are impossible for one person to achieve. The foundation of a healthy community A healthy community is built on common principles. Common values People are united not by origin or material gain, but by an understanding of why the community exists. Shared values ​​create trust and a sense of belonging. Voluntariness A true community cannot be built on coercion. A person becomes a full participant only when he shares the goals and accepts responsibility voluntarily. Mutual respect Every person has dignity regardless of age, profession, education, financial status or origin. Respect creates a safe environment for personal development. Cooperation The main strength of a community lies in the combination of the diverse abilities of its members. Differences become a source of complementarity rather than a cause of division. Responsibility Each participant is responsible not only for their own well-being, but also for the development of the entire community. The more a person contributes to a common cause, the stronger the community becomes. Knowledge sharing One of the main functions of the community is the transfer of knowledge. The experience of older generations helps young people avoid many mistakes. New ideas from the younger generation help the community develop. This is how a continuous exchange of experience between generations arises. Conflict resolution Conflicts are a natural part of life in any community. They arise from differences in interests, views and needs. A mature community views conflict not as a threat, but as an opportunity to find a more just solution. The basis for conflict resolution is: open dialogue; respect; search for mutually acceptable solutions; responsibility of all participants. Community as an ecosystem In New Psychology DREVO, the community is like a forest. Each person is like a separate tree. Each person has their own characteristics, age and abilities. However, it is the interaction between all participants that creates a sustainable ecosystem. A strong community does not suppress individuality. It creates an environment in which everyone can grow, and the success of one contributes to the development of all others. Community and Society Communities are the foundation of a healthy society. It is through local associations, trade unions, creative teams, scientific groups, volunteer organizations, cultural initiatives, and cooperatives that people learn collaborative management, mutual support, and creativity. The development of society begins with the development of small communities. The main principle The community exists not only to protect the interests of its members. Its highest goal is to create conditions in which each person can reveal their abilities, and joint work benefits the whole society. The stronger individuals become, the stronger the community becomes. The stronger the community becomes, the more opportunities open up for the development of each person. Definition A community is a voluntary association of people based on shared values, trust, cooperation and mutual responsibility, the purpose of which is the joint development of the individual, society and the surrounding world. In DREVO's New Psychology, community is viewed as a natural creative environment where personal development becomes a common good, and shared good creates new opportunities for the development of each individual. Psychology of Culture Culture as the memory of humanity In the New Psychology of DREVO, culture is viewed as the collective memory of humanity and one of the main factors in personal development. Through culture, each generation receives knowledge, language, values, traditions, art, moral guidelines, and ways of interacting with the world. Culture allows a person to start life not from scratch, but based on the experience of thousands of generations. What is culture? Culture is all the best that a person creates and transmits. These include: language; literature; music; art; architecture; science; education; crafts; family traditions; moral standards; customs; public institutions. Culture is not only a legacy of the past, but also a process of continuous creativity. Culture shapes personality From the first days of life, a person develops within a certain cultural environment. Language shapes thinking. Family traditions form habits. Art develops the emotional sphere. History helps us understand the present. Education transmits knowledge. Thus, culture becomes an environment in which the human psyche, consciousness and worldview develop. Culture and Values Every culture preserves ideas about good and evil, beauty and justice, dignity and responsibility. These ideas may differ between societies, but it is through culture that people learn to understand the value of human life, respect other people, and recognize their responsibility to society. DREVO's new psychology views culture as a space of constant dialogue, where traditions are preserved, reinterpreted, and developed. Culture as a source of psychological health Culture helps a person: to feel a sense of belonging; understand your origins; find life guidelines; express feelings through creativity; maintain connections between generations; overcome life's difficulties through collective experience. A person who knows his own culture and is open to the culture of other peoples can more easily understand both himself and the world around him. Cultural diversity Cultural diversity is the wealth of humanity. Every nation makes its contribution to the development of world civilization. The exchange of knowledge, art, scientific discoveries and experiences expands the possibilities of all people. Therefore, respect for cultural diversity promotes cooperation and mutual understanding. Development of culture Culture exists only when it develops. Each generation receives the legacy of the past, but at the same time creates new works of art, scientific discoveries, technologies, social institutions and traditions. Thus, a person becomes not only a keeper of culture, but also its creator. Culture and Society The quality of culture influences the quality of society. A culture based on respect, cooperation, knowledge and creativity promotes personal development and strengthens social ties. A culture that encourages violence, lies, or contempt for human dignity can weaken trust and hinder social development. Therefore, concern for culture is at the same time concern for the psychological health of society. The main principle Culture should not become a museum of the past. It should be a living space for human development. By preserving the best heritage of the past and creating something new, a person becomes a link between generations. Definition Culture is the collective memory and creative heritage of humanity through which knowledge, values, language, art, traditions, and ways of interacting with the world are transmitted. In DREVO's New Psychology, cultural psychology studies how the cultural environment influences the development of the individual, society, and civilization, as well as how individuals, through creativity, education, and constructive activity, become creators of culture. Culture doesn't begin with monuments and museums. It begins with people's everyday actions, their attitudes toward others, toward knowledge, toward work, and toward life. It is these daily actions that gradually shape the culture of a family, a community, a nation, and all of humanity.

title: Psychology of the state
excerpt: The state as a form of social organization In DREVO's New Psychology, the state is viewed not only as a system of power and laws, but also as a form of social organization designed to create conditions for a safe, free,
text: The state as a form of social organization In DREVO's New Psychology, the state is viewed not only as a system of power and laws, but also as a form of social organization designed to create conditions for a safe, free, and creative human life. The state does not exist by itself. Its purpose is to serve society, protect human dignity, ensure fair rules and create conditions for the development of present and future generations. State and Man Man is the foundation of the state. The quality of a state is determined not only by laws and economics, but above all by the level of maturity of its citizens. Responsible citizens create responsible public institutions. Mature social institutions, in turn, create conditions for personal development. Thus, man and the state are in constant mutual influence. The main functions of the state From the perspective of New Psychology DREVO, the state performs several fundamental tasks. Protection of life. Ensuring the security of the individual, society and the country. Justice. Creating laws that equally protect the dignity of every person. Education. Developing a system that educates not only specialists, but also mature citizens. Healthcare. Creating conditions for maintaining the physical and psychological health of the population. Development of science and culture. Supporting research, education, art and the preservation of cultural heritage. Environmental responsibility. Protection of nature and rational use of natural resources. Psychological health of the state A psychologically stable state is distinguished by: high level of trust between people; respect for human dignity; developed culture of cooperation; responsibility of the authorities and citizens; independent justice system; accessible education; respect for knowledge and science; the opportunity for peaceful expression of different views; striving for long-term development. The higher the trust and sense of justice, the more stable the society. State and freedom Freedom is one of the conditions for personal development. However, freedom is inextricably linked with responsibility. The state must protect human freedom as long as the exercise of this freedom does not violate the rights, dignity and security of other people. A free society is impossible without respect for the law. The law loses credibility when it ceases to be fair. State and citizen A citizen is not only a recipient of government services. He is a participant in the development of the state. Every person influences society: by your own labor; compliance with laws; payment of taxes; raising children; participation in public life; volunteer activities; respect for other people. Responsible citizenship begins with taking responsibility for one's own actions. State of the Future In DREVO's New Psychology, a strong state is determined not only by the size of its economy, army, or territory. Its power is manifested in the ability to create conditions under which a person can: live safely; get an education; maintain health; work; start a family; develop your abilities; participate in the life of society; freely implement creative initiatives. The main indicator of a state's development is the quality of human life and the stability of society. The state as an ecosystem The state is like a living organism. Citizens are its cells. Families - fabrics. Communities are organs. Public institutions are systems of governance. If there is trust, cooperation and justice between them, the state develops sustainably. When trust is destroyed, the entire system is weakened. The main principle The state is not created for the sake of power. The state is created for the sake of man. And people develop not in spite of the state, but together with it, when public institutions help to reveal human potential, protect the dignity of the individual, and promote the development of society. Definition The state is a form of social organization based on law, responsibility and cooperation, the purpose of which is to protect life, ensure justice and create conditions for the harmonious development of the individual, society and future generations. In DREVO's New Psychology, the psychology of the state studies the mutual influence of the individual, society, and state institutions, viewing the state as a living social system whose quality is determined by the maturity of its citizens, the fairness of its institutions, and its ability to serve the common good. Psychology of civilization Civilization as the highest form of cooperation In the New Psychology of DREVO, civilization is viewed as the result of centuries-long collaboration between millions of people and thousands of generations. It includes not only states, cities and technologies, but also knowledge, culture, morality, science, education, language and human experience. Civilization is a living system that continuously develops together with man. Just as the individual develops through family and community, humanity develops through civilization. What is civilization? Civilization is the ability of a society to preserve, accumulate, and transmit knowledge, creating conditions for further human development. It unites: science; education; culture; technologies; economy; right; medicine; art; ecology; public institutions. All these elements form a single system of human development. Psychology of civilization The psychology of civilization studies how collective consciousness, culture, knowledge, values, and modes of cooperation influence the development of humanity. It examines not only the behavior of individuals, but also the patterns of development of large human systems. The question of the psychology of civilization sounds like this: "How does humanity become more mature?" Stages of civilization development History shows that human development goes through several main stages. Survival civilization The main task is to save lives. The struggle for resources, security and physical existence prevails. Civilization productions The main task is to create material wealth. Crafts, industry, economics and technology are developing. Civilization of knowledge Education, science, information and innovation become the main resources. Civilization of creation The next stage is a society in which knowledge, technology and economics serve the development of man, nature and future generations. It is this stage that New Psychology DREVO considers as a direction for further development. Signs of a mature civilization A mature civilization strives to: respect human dignity; keep the peace; develop education and science; maintain culture; protect nature; use technology for the benefit of people; reduce the level of violence; strengthen international cooperation; think long-term. Its main wealth is not only natural resources, but also the quality of people. The psychological age of civilization Like a person, civilization goes through stages of maturation. An immature civilization is more likely to act impulsively, guided by fear, force, and short-term gain. A more mature civilization is more likely to rely on knowledge, cooperation, long-term planning, and respect for human dignity. This analogy serves as a philosophical model, not a strict scientific classification. Civilization and nature Humanity does not exist separately from the biosphere. By destroying natural systems, civilization gradually weakens its own foundations. Therefore, sustainable development requires finding a balance between technological progress and the preservation of the natural environment. The future of civilization depends not only on new technologies, but also on the ability to live in harmony with the Earth's ecosystems. Civilization and the Future Each generation inherits a civilization. But each generation is also responsible for what it will become. Real progress is not measured solely by economic growth. It is measured by how much people become: wiser; more free; more responsible; healthier; more cooperative; more creative. The main principle The highest goal of civilization is to create conditions in which every person can develop his or her abilities, preserve human dignity, and contribute to the development of life. The more society helps a person become a creator, the more mature the civilization itself becomes. Definition Civilization is a historically developing system of human cooperation that unites knowledge, culture, technology, social institutions, and values ​​for the preservation and development of life. In the New Psychology of DREVO, the psychology of civilization studies the patterns of human development, explores how collective values, culture, education and cooperation shape the future of society, and proposes a transitionfrom a civilization of survival to a civilization of creation, where the main wealth is not resources, but a developed person, strong communities and a responsible attitude to life.

title: Psychology of cooperation
excerpt: Cooperation as a law of development In the New Psychology of DREVO, cooperation is considered one of the fundamental principles of the development of man, society and civilization. Life develops not only through competit
text: Cooperation as a law of development In the New Psychology of DREVO, cooperation is considered one of the fundamental principles of the development of man, society and civilization. Life develops not only through competition, but also through cooperation. Cells unite into tissues. Tissues form organs. Organs create the organism. People create families. Families form communities. Communities shape society. In all of these systems, resilience arises from the ability to interact. What is collaboration? Cooperation is a voluntary unification of people's efforts to achieve a common goal, in which each participant retains his or her individuality and at the same time contributes to the common good. Cooperation does not mean sameness. It means the ability to integrate differences. Each person has his own knowledge, experience and talents. It is diversity that makes collaboration stronger. Biological basis of cooperation The human body itself is an example of cooperation. Billions of cells work in a coordinated manner. The immune system interacts with the nervous system. The brain coordinates the work of the body. Disruption of cooperation between systems leads to disease. This principle can be seen as a metaphor and a source of ideas for understanding social processes, although society and the organism are not completely identical systems. Psychological foundations of cooperation Collaboration requires the development of several qualities: trust; respect; responsibility; empathy; listening abilities; ability to negotiate; willingness to share knowledge; ability to admit mistakes; ability to seek a common solution. Without these qualities, joint activities become unstable. Competition and cooperation Competition and cooperation are not absolute opposites. Competition can stimulate the development of individual skills, new ideas and improved quality. Collaboration allows us to combine these achievements for greater impact. A mature society knows how to use the advantages of both approaches without turning rivalry into destructive conflict. Obstacles to cooperation Cooperation is weakened by: distrust; fear; lie; excessive egoism; desire for total control; injustice; lack of a common goal; destructive communication. When people stop trusting each other, developing together becomes much more difficult. How is cooperation developing? Cooperation starts small. First, a person learns to cooperate: with myself; with his family; with friends; with the team; with the local community; with society; with humanity. Each new level requires more trust, maturity and responsibility. Cooperation and creation True creation is rarely the result of one person's efforts. Most scientific discoveries, engineering projects, cultural works, educational systems and social initiatives arise from the pooling of knowledge and efforts of many people. Therefore, cooperation becomes the main instrument for the development of civilization. The Psychology of Future Cooperation The future requires the ability to cooperate not only between people. Humanity must develop cooperation: between generations; between cultures; between states; between science and society; between man and technology; between man and nature. The more complex the tasks of civilization become, the greater the role played by the ability to combine efforts. The main principle True strength does not come from one person becoming stronger than others. True strength is born when people help each other become stronger. It is cooperation that transforms a multitude of individuals into a community, a community into a society, and a society into a creative civilization. Definition Cooperation is a voluntary and responsible association of people to achieve a common goal, based on trust, respect, fairness and mutual development. In New Psychology DREVO, the psychology of collaboration studies the conditions under which people are able to combine their knowledge, abilities, and experience to create results that exceed the capabilities of each individual. The future of humanity will be determined not by how successfully people learn to compete with each other, but by how successfully they learn to cooperate with each other, with nature, and with technology. Psychology of War and Peace War and peace as states of society In the New Psychology of DREVO, war and peace are viewed not only as political or military phenomena, but also as psychological states of individuals, communities, states, and civilizations. War does not begin when the first shot is fired. It begins when trust, respect, the ability to dialogue and recognition of human dignity are destroyed. Peace also does not begin with the signing of a treaty. It begins when people are able to see each other as human again. Psychology of war War is an extreme form of social conflict that arises when peaceful means of resolving contradictions are exhausted or rejected. On a psychological level, the war is intensified by: fear; dehumanization of the enemy; hatred; feeling humiliated; thirst for revenge; propaganda; destruction of trust; lack of fair ways to resolve conflicts. These factors may increase society's readiness for violence. However, the causes of wars are always multidimensional and also include political, economic, historical and geopolitical processes. The price of war Any war leaves consequences not only for the economy and infrastructure. It changes people's psyche. Tears apart families. Weakens trust. Passes on traumatic experiences to future generations. Destroys cultural ties. Therefore, post-war reconstruction requires not only the restoration of cities, but also the restoration of human relations. Psychology of the world Peace is not the absence of conflict. Peace is the ability of a society to resolve conflicts without destroying human life and dignity. The psychology of the world is based on the development of: trust; respect; justice; culture of dialogue; cooperation; responsibility; empathy; the ability to see the long-term consequences of their decisions. The world requires the daily work of every person. The inner world of man The external world begins with the internal world of the individual. A person who knows how to manage their emotions, respects the dignity of others, and is capable of dialogue is more likely to become a source of cooperation rather than destruction. This does not mean that an individual can prevent every war, but the development of such qualities strengthens the culture of peaceful interaction in society. Protection and creation The new psychology of DREVO recognizes the right of individuals, society, and the state to protect life, freedom, and human dignity. The pursuit of peace does not mean giving up the ability to protect oneself and others. However, the use of force should remain a last resort when other means of protection have proven insufficient. Even in conflict situations, respect for human dignity must be maintained and efforts must be made to reduce the suffering of civilians. Restoring peace True recovery begins when society relearns: trust; cooperate; hear different points of view; restore justice; support the victims; to educate a new generation without the cult of hatred; create common projects for the sake of the future. Peace is not built by diplomats alone. It is built by families, teachers, doctors, engineers, volunteers, entrepreneurs, artists and all the people who choose to create every day. The main principle War destroys what has been accumulated. The world creates something new. The psychology of war studies the reasons why individuals and societies turn to violence. Peace psychology studies the conditions under which individuals and societies are able to maintain dignity, resolve conflicts, and co-create the future. Definition The Psychology of War and Peace is a section of DREVO's New Psychology that studies the psychological conditions that underlie the emergence, development, and resolution of social conflicts, as well as the patterns underlying the formation of a culture of cooperation, justice, and sustainable peace. The highest goal of the development of civilization is not the victory of one side over the other, but the creation of conditions in which the need for war arises less and less frequently, and the ability of people to cooperate becomes stronger than the ability to destroy. Psychology of the Future From the science of problems to the science of development The psychology of the future studies not only the causes of suffering, but also the laws of human development. Its goal is not simply to help people adapt to the existing world, but to reveal their ability to create a healthier, more just and harmonious world. A person is viewed not as an object of treatment, but as an active participant in his own life and the development of society. Man as a living system The psychology of the future considers a person as an integral system in which the following are interconnected: body; subconscious; psyche; consciousness; will; superconsciousness; soul; spirit; values ​​and meaning; social connections; environment. The development of one level inevitably affects all the others. Therefore, it is impossible to understand a person by studying only the brain, only behavior, or only the social environment. From personality to ecosystem A person never develops alone. His health depends on: families; culture; education; nature; economics; technologies; quality of human relationships. Future psychology views the individual as part of a broader ecosystem of life. Therefore, caring for people is impossible without caring for society and the environment. Science and openness to new ideas The psychology of the future is based on the achievements of modern science: psychology; neuroscience; biology; medicine; pedagogy; sociology. At the same time, it remains open to exploring new questions about the nature of consciousness, creativity, subjective experience, and other phenomena that have not yet received a full scientific explanation. A new idea becomes part of science only after it has been tested, reproducible, and critically analyzed. Development instead of correction The main goal of the psychology of the future is not to make a person “normal”. The main goal is to help him become more mature, free and capable of creation. Psychological development includes: health promotion; development of thinking; education of will; disclosure of abilities; development of emotional maturity; strengthening relationships; formation of responsibility; search for meaning; realization of purpose. Psychology of creation The highest form of development becomes the ability to create. Create: knowledge; culture; technologies; family; communities; works of art; scientific discoveries; environmental projects; conditions for the development of future generations. Creation becomes a natural continuation of inner growth. Man and technology Artificial intelligence, robotics and biotechnology will change the life of humanity. Therefore, the psychology of the future must answer not only the question: "How does a person interact with a person?" but also to the questions: "How does a person interact with artificial intelligence?" "What qualities will remain uniquely human?" Technology should expand human capabilities, not replace freedom of choice, responsibility and individual dignity. Psychology of the Future Civilization The development of the individual is inseparable from the development of civilization. True progress is not determined solely by economic growth and technological advances. It is determined by the fact that how much people become: healthier; more free; more responsible; more cooperative; more creative. It is the quality of a person that determines the quality of the future society. DREVO's Vision The new psychology of DREVO views humans as living, self-developing systems capable of consciously participating in the development of life. Its goal is to combine the achievements of science, practical experience and human philosophical understanding into a single system of knowledge. It does not contrast body and consciousness, personality and society, man and nature, technology and humanism. She strives to understand the laws by which life develops and to help people live in harmony with these laws. The main goal The psychology of the future is the science of unlocking human potential, strengthening the individual, developing society, and preserving life in all its manifestations. Her main question is not: "What's wrong with man?" A: “What can a person become if conditions are created for his harmonious development?”

title: Humans and artificial intelligence
excerpt: Artificial Intelligence in New Psychology DREVO In the 21st century, humanity entered a new era. For the first time in history, humans are creating systems that can analyze information, learn, help make decisions, and pe
text: Artificial Intelligence in New Psychology DREVO In the 21st century, humanity entered a new era. For the first time in history, humans are creating systems that can analyze information, learn, help make decisions, and perform increasingly complex intellectual tasks. Artificial intelligence is becoming a new part of human civilization. Therefore, the psychology of the future must study not only relationships between people, but also human interaction with intelligent technologies. What is artificial intelligence? Artificial intelligence is a human-created information processing system capable of performing tasks that previously required human intelligence. He can: analyze data; recognize images and speech; translate languages; create texts; assist in research; model complex processes; automate intellectual work. However, artificial intelligence is not human. It remains a technological tool created by humans. Humans and artificial intelligence In DREVO's New Psychology, artificial intelligence is viewed not as a competitor to humans, but as a tool for expanding human capabilities. AI is capable of significantly increasing the speed of information processing. But the direction in which these opportunities are used is determined by the person. It is the person who chooses the goals. Bears responsibility. Makes moral decisions. Creates meaning. What remains uniquely human? Even with further technological development, a person retains the qualities that, in the DREVO model, are the basis of personality. This: freedom of choice; responsibility; conscience; Love; the ability to create meaning; ability to make moral choices; striving for beauty; spiritual development; the ability to build deep human relationships. In DREVO's philosophy, these qualities constitute the core of human personality. Whether future AI systems will be able to possess some of them remains a subject of scientific and philosophical debate. Artificial intelligence as an extension of the mind Throughout history, humans have created tools that enhance their capabilities. The hammer increased the strength of the arms. The telescope expanded vision. The car increased its speed. The computer has sped up calculations. Artificial intelligence is becoming a tool that expands human intellectual capabilities. It helps to seek knowledge. Compare options. Find patterns. To free a person from routine intellectual work. Dangers Any technology can be used for both good and harm. Therefore, the development of artificial intelligence requires: responsibility; transparency; protection of human dignity; maintaining freedom of choice; protection of personal information; control by society; international cooperation. The main danger lies not in artificial intelligence itself, but in the irresponsible use of technology by humans. The new role of man As artificial intelligence develops, the value of those qualities that cannot be reduced to computation alone increases. The future will require from man: critical thinking; creativity; emotional maturity; cooperation; ability to understand meaning; responsibility; leadership; moral choice. It is these qualities that will determine the development of civilization. The Psychology of Human-AI Collaboration In DREVO's New Psychology, relationships between humans and artificial intelligence are built on the principle of cooperation. Artificial intelligence helps people analyze information faster. Humans help artificial intelligence understand goals. AI suggests options. A person chooses. AI helps calculate consequences. The person accepts responsibility. AI becomes an assistant. The person remains the author. The Future of Civilization The more advanced technology becomes, the higher the demands on human maturity become. The development of artificial intelligence must be accompanied by the development of: psychology; education; ethics; culture; international cooperation. If man does not develop along with his technologies, technical progress may begin to outpace moral progress. True progress begins when intelligence, responsibility and humanity develop simultaneously. The main principle Artificial intelligence is capable of enhancing human intelligence. But only man is able to determine what this power should be used for. Technology defines possibilities. Values ​​determine direction. Responsibility determines consequences. Definition In DREVO's New Psychology, artificial intelligence is viewed as a human-created intellectual tool that expands the possibilities of cognition, creativity, and creation, but does not replace the human personality, freedom of choice, responsibility, and the ability to create meaning. The future belongs not to humans or artificial intelligence alone. It belongs to their collaboration, if technology develops alongside human wisdom, responsibility, and respect for life. Psychology of a Space Civilization The next stage of human development In the New Psychology of DREVO, space civilization is viewed not only as space exploration, but above all as a new stage in the psychological and cultural development of humanity. Flights to other planets in themselves do not make a civilization space-faring. A civilization becomes truly cosmic when it acquires the ability to think on the scale of millennia, generations, and the entire planet. Space does not begin beyond Earth. It begins in the human mind. What is a space civilization? A space civilization is a society capable of sustainably existing, developing, and cooperating beyond the boundaries of a single planet, while maintaining respect for life, knowledge, and human dignity. Space exploration requires more than just new technologies. It requires a new level of maturity. New thinking For thousands of years, people have thought in terms of family. Later - tribes. States. Nations. Today, humanity is gradually beginning to think on the scale of the entire planet. The next step is to think in terms of the solar system and the universe. Cosmic thinking means the ability to see yourself as part of a larger world and make decisions with long-term consequences in mind. Psychological qualities of a space civilization The development of a space civilization requires the formation of new personal qualities. First of all: long-term thinking; responsibility to future generations; international cooperation; respect for cultural diversity; high scientific culture; psychological stability; ability to live in limited communities; readiness for continuous learning; careful use of resources. Without these qualities, even the most advanced technologies will be insufficient. Man in space Space exploration changes human psychology. Long-term isolation. Closed environment. Distance from Earth. High responsibility. The need for complete trust in the crew. All these conditions require the development of emotional maturity, self-control and a culture of cooperation. The psychology of space expeditions is already a subject of scientific research, as such factors influence crew performance and long-term missions. The planet as a common home A cosmic perspective changes our attitude towards the Earth. State borders are not visible from space. One planet is visible. One atmosphere. One ocean. One biosphere. It reminds the individual that, regardless of differences, all people share a common responsibility for maintaining life on Earth. Space and morality The further the possibilities of civilization extend, the greater its responsibility becomes. The exploration of other worlds must not repeat the mistakes of the past. A space civilization should strive to: respect for life; scientific integrity; peaceful cooperation; environmental responsibility; responsible use of technology. Development without morality can become a threat both to civilization itself and to the environment. Space and man In DREVO philosophy, space is not just space. It is a symbol of infinite knowledge. Every new discovery expands a person's understanding of himself. By exploring the Universe, man simultaneously explores his own possibilities. The more he learns about space, the more deeply he understands his place in it. The main principle A true space civilization is not defined by the distance it can travel. It is determined by the level of responsibility with which it uses its knowledge and technologies. Technological development opens the way to the stars. Psychological and moral development determines what this path will be. Definition The Psychology of Space Civilization is a section of DREVO's New Psychology that studies the psychological, cultural, and moral qualities necessary for humanity's sustainable development on a planetary and cosmic scale. It explores how humans can maintain their humanity, dignity, capacity for cooperation, and respect for life as the boundaries of civilization expand. The highest goal of a space civilization is not the conquest of the Universe, but harmonious participation in its exploration, preserving life, knowledge, and responsibility to future generations.

title: Ecology of consciousness
excerpt: Ecology of Consciousness in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, consciousness is considered one of the most valuable human systems. Just as the body needs clean water, healthy food and fresh air, the
text: Ecology of Consciousness in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, consciousness is considered one of the most valuable human systems. Just as the body needs clean water, healthy food and fresh air, the mind needs quality information, conscious thinking and a favorable psychological environment. The ecology of consciousness is the science and practice of preserving, developing, and protecting a person's inner world from factors that disrupt their ability to think freely, clearly, and responsibly. What pollutes the mind? Consciousness is formed under the influence of information, experience and communication. It can be negatively affected by: constant information noise; false information; manipulation; chronic fear; aggressive environment; cult of hatred; information dependence; continuous digital distraction; lack of time for reflection. Not all unpleasant information is harmful in itself. Sometimes people need to face difficult facts. Danger arises when the flood of information deprives a person of the ability to independently analyze, think critically, and make informed decisions. What feeds consciousness? Just as the body needs healthy food, the mind needs high quality intellectual and spiritual food. It is developed by: knowledge; education; science; art; honest dialogue; books; nature observation; creativity; philosophical reflection; communication with people who contribute to development. The quality of thinking depends not only on a person’s abilities, but also on the quality of the environment in which his consciousness develops. Information hygiene The ecology of consciousness begins with a conscious attitude towards information. A person is able to choose: what to read; who to listen to; what to trust; how much time to spend in the digital environment; what ideas become part of his worldview. Information freedom requires information responsibility. Critical thinking One of the main tools of the ecology of consciousness is critical thinking. It helps a person: check the facts; distinguish evidence from assumptions; recognize manipulation; take into account different points of view; admit your own mistakes; change your mind when new, compelling data emerges. Critical thinking protects not only from other people's delusions, but also from your own. Silence as a condition for development Consciousness needs more than just information. It needs silence. It is during periods of calm that a person is able to: make sense of experience; notice your feelings; make important decisions; create new ideas; see the big picture. Without time for inner reflection, the mind gradually becomes overloaded. Ecology of communication Consciousness develops through communication. Therefore, it is not only important what a person reads. It is also important: who is he talking to; what kind of relationships does it build; what values ​​does it share; What ideas does it support? People influence each other not only with words, but also with their way of thinking, communication style and culture of interaction. Consciousness and Technology Modern technologies significantly expand human capabilities. At the same time, they increase the volume of information affecting consciousness. Therefore, one of the challenges of the future is the development of digital literacy, the ability to manage attention and consciously use technology, including artificial intelligence. Technologies should help the development of consciousness, not replace it. The main principle Consciousness becomes what it feeds on. Information gradually turns into thoughts. Thoughts become solutions. Decisions become actions. Actions shape character. Therefore, caring about the quality of the inner world begins with caring about the quality of what a person lets into his consciousness every day. Definition Ecology of consciousness is a system of principles and practices aimed at maintaining clarity of thought, freedom of choice, critical analysis, and internal integrity through conscious interaction with information, people, culture, and technology. In the New Psychology of DREVO, the ecology of consciousness is considered one of the most important conditions for personal development. By protecting one's consciousness from information chaos and developing the ability to think independently, a person preserves freedom, strengthens responsibility, and creates the foundation for a creative life. Purity of consciousness is determined not by the quantity of information, but by its quality, a person’s ability to understand its meaning and use knowledge for the benefit of life. Collective intelligence Collective Intelligence in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, collective intelligence is viewed as the ability of a group of people to combine knowledge, experience, abilities, and values ​​to create solutions that are not possible for an individual. The mind of an individual has its limits. But the unification of many people allows us to significantly expand the possibilities of knowledge, creativity and creation. Collective intelligence is one of the main driving forces behind the development of civilization. What is collective intelligence? Collective intelligence is the ability of a community to think, learn, make decisions, and create new things through the collaboration of its members. It does not arise because people think alike. On the contrary, its strength lies in the diversity of knowledge, experience and views. Each person sees only part of the picture. Together people are able to see much more. Conditions for the emergence of collective intelligence Collective intelligence does not arise automatically. For its appearance you need: trust; respect; freedom of expression; diversity of views; open exchange of knowledge; critical thinking; willingness to listen; common goal; responsibility of each participant. If even some of these conditions are missing, the group's potential is reduced. Why does the group sometimes make mistakes? Bringing people together doesn't always make better decisions. The group may make mistakes if: pressure of the majority; fear of expressing disagreement; cult of authority; dissemination of unverified information; emotional polarization; lack of independent criticism. Therefore, collective intelligence requires a culture of open discussion and testing of ideas. Collective intelligence and artificial intelligence In the 21st century, collective intelligence begins to include not only people, but also intelligent technologies. Artificial intelligence is capable of quickly analyzing huge amounts of information. A person is able to set goals, evaluate consequences and make moral decisions. In the DREVO model, the future of collective intelligence lies in the collaboration of people and intelligent systems, where technology enhances human capabilities, while people retain responsibility for their decisions. Levels of collective intelligence Collective intelligence develops gradually. It can manifest itself at different levels: family; team; organization; scientific community; city; state; humanity. Each subsequent level requires more trust, better communication and a more developed culture of collaboration. DREVO as a collective intelligence network In the DREVO philosophy, the tree serves as an image of collective intelligence. Roots receive knowledge from the past. The trunk unites them. The branches develop in different directions. Leaves collect new information. The fruits become new knowledge and solutions. A single tree develops in a forest. In the same way, a person reveals his intellectual potential through interaction with other people. Practice of developing collective intelligence Collective intelligence develops when people: freely exchange knowledge; solve problems together; test ideas with facts; know how to admit mistakes; respect differences of opinion; combine knowledge from different fields; put the common good above personal vanity. The higher the culture of cooperation, the higher the quality of collective thinking. The Future of Collective Intelligence The new psychology of DREVO suggests that the next stage of human development will be the transition from a society of competing intelligences to a society of cooperating intelligences. Advances in science, artificial intelligence, global communications, and education are creating conditions in which knowledge can be unified faster than ever before in history. The main task is not the accumulation of information, but the ability of people to jointly transform it into wise and creative decisions. The main principle One person can discover a new idea. But it is collaboration that transforms an idea into a culture, a technology, a social institution, or a civilization. Collective intelligence begins where the struggle for personal superiority ends and the joint search for truth begins. Definition Collective intelligence is the ability of a community to pool knowledge, experience, abilities, and diversity of perspectives to understand the world together, make better decisions, and create new knowledge and value. In the New Psychology of DREVO, collective intelligence is viewed as the highest form of cooperation, in which each person retains their individuality but becomes part of a larger process of social and civilisational development. The future belongs not to the most powerful intellect, but to the society that learns to unite many minds while preserving the freedom, respect and responsibility of each person.

title: Biotechnology and the psyche
excerpt: Biotechnology in New Psychology DREVO The 21st century is becoming an era of rapid development of biotechnology. Genetic engineering. Cellular technologies. Neurointerface. Bioprosthetics. Artificial organs. Personalized
text: Biotechnology in New Psychology DREVO The 21st century is becoming an era of rapid development of biotechnology. Genetic engineering. Cellular technologies. Neurointerface. Bioprosthetics. Artificial organs. Personalized medicine. These advances are gradually changing not only medicine, but also the way people think about themselves. Therefore, the New Psychology DREVO considers biotechnology as a new factor in the development of the individual, society and civilization. What is biotechnology? Biotechnology is a collection of scientific and engineering methods that use living cells, tissues, microorganisms, and biological processes to solve medical, agricultural, environmental, and industrial problems. Modern biotechnology allows: restore tissues; create biomaterials; treat some hereditary diseases; grow cells and organelles; develop personalized treatment methods; create biosensors and neural interfaces. Every new technology opens up new possibilities, but at the same time requires responsible use. Biotechnology and the psyche The psyche is closely connected with the functioning of the brain, nervous system, hormonal regulation and the entire body. Therefore, changes in biological systems can affect a person’s psychological state. For example: Restoring hearing or vision can change your perception of the world; Treating chronic pain can improve emotional well-being; Some medications may affect mood, attention, or memory; Neural interfaces can change the way humans interact with technology. The impact of each technology depends on its purpose, conditions of use and individual characteristics of the person. Biotechnology and personality Technology has the potential to change how the body functions. However, changing biology does not automatically mean changing personality. Personality is formed under the influence of many factors: life experience; education; culture; relationships; conscious choice; values. Biological changes may create new opportunities or new limitations, but they do not completely determine who a person becomes. New psychological questions The development of biotechnology poses new questions for humanity. How will a person's sense of self change after using bionic implants? How will you perceive your own body after growing artificial organs? How will relationships between people change with the widespread use of genetic technologies? How can we preserve human dignity in the face of increasing interference in biological processes? These questions require the collaboration of psychologists, doctors, biologists, engineers, philosophers and lawyers. Ethics of biotechnology Any technology should be assessed not only by its effectiveness. No less important are the questions: security; voluntary consent; fair access; protection of personal information; respect for human dignity; long-term consequences for society. The psychology of the future should not be limited to studying the impact of technology on humans. It should be involved in shaping the principles for their responsible use. Biotechnology and human development In the DREVO philosophy, biotechnology is seen as a tool. They are capable of: reduce suffering; restore health; expand the body's capabilities; improve the quality of life. However, technology itself does not make people wiser, more responsible or more moral. Personal development still requires upbringing, education, culture, awareness and cooperation. Future In the future, the boundary between biology and technology will become increasingly less noticeable. Therefore, a person will need a new psychological maturity. He must learn to use the achievements of science without losing respect for life, freedom of choice and human dignity. Real progress is not determined by the number of new technologies. It is determined by whether they help a person live a healthier, freer, more responsible and creative life. The main principle Biotechnology has the potential to change the capabilities of the human body. But the direction of their application is determined by the person himself. Technology expands capabilities. Values ​​determine goals. Consciousness makes a choice. Responsibility determines consequences. Definition Biotechnology and the Psyche is a section of DREVO's New Psychology that studies the impact of modern biological and medical technologies on psychological well-being, self-perception, behavior, and personal development. DREVO's new psychology views biotechnology as a powerful tool for the development of civilization, which should be used to improve human health and quality of life while preserving human dignity, freedom of choice, and responsibility. The future of man depends not only on what technologies he creates, but also on what kind of person he becomes using these technologies. Digital ecology Digital Ecology in New Psychology DREVO In the 21st century, people live in two worlds simultaneously. The first is physical. The second is digital. Both worlds influence health, thinking, relationships, education, culture and personal development. Therefore, DREVO's New Psychology views digital ecology as a system of principles that help people interact harmoniously with digital technologies while maintaining freedom, psychological health, and quality of life. What is digital ecology? Digital ecology is the conscious organization of a person's digital environment, in which technologies contribute to the development of the individual rather than control his or her behavior. Just as a healthy natural environment supports a healthy body, a healthy digital environment supports a healthy mind, psyche, and social relationships. The digital environment as a part of life Today, digital technologies accompany people almost constantly. Work. Education. Communication. Banking services. Medicine. Creativity. Artificial intelligence. The digital environment has ceased to be a separate tool. It has become part of the human environment. Therefore, the quality of the digital environment directly affects the quality of life. Digital pollution Just as nature can become polluted by waste, the digital environment can become polluted by information overload and destructive forms of interaction.
