Digital pollution includes: information noise; constant notifications; unverified information; manipulation; aggressive communication; digital addiction; excessive screen time; loss of ability to concentrate for long periods of time; uncontrolled use of artificial intelligence. The main problem is not the quantity of technologies, but the lack of conscious management of them. Digital health A healthy digital environment helps a person: study; work; create; cooperate; develop thinking; maintain relationships; gain access to knowledge. Technology should free people to be creative, social and develop, rather than absorbing all their attention. Digital freedom Freedom in the digital world means the ability to choose how to use technology. A person remains the master of his decisions. It defines: how much time to spend online; what sources of information to use; what technologies help development; when you need to disconnect and return to real communication. True freedom is impossible without self-control. Digital security The development of technology requires concern not only about physical security. No less important are: protection of personal data; cybersecurity; protection of intellectual property; responsible use of artificial intelligence; verification of the accuracy of information. Digital literacy is becoming a new form of culture. Man and technology In DREVO's philosophy, technology is seen as an extension of human capabilities. But no technology should replace: independent thinking; responsibility; live communication; Love; conscience; creativity; freedom of choice. Technology is a tool. Man remains their creator and responsible user. Principles of digital ecology A healthy digital life is built on several principles. Awareness. Use technology for a purpose, not out of habit. Quality is more important than quantity. It is better to have less information, but more reliable and useful. Balance. Digital life should complement real life, not replace it. Attention protection. Attention is one of the most valuable human resources. Technologies for creation. Use digital tools primarily for learning, creativity, collaboration, and development. The main principle The digital environment should serve people. A person should not become its appendage. The faster technology develops, the more important it is to maintain the ability to think, feel, choose, and build genuine human relationships independently. Definition Digital ecology is a system of principles and practices aimed at harmonious human interaction with the digital environment, ensuring the preservation of psychological health, freedom of choice, critical thinking, human relationships, and the creative use of technology. In DREVO's New Psychology, digital ecology is viewed as a necessary condition for personal development in the era of artificial intelligence and global communications. The goal of digital ecology is not to abandon technology, but to learn to use it in a way that strengthens people rather than weakens their attention, freedom, and creative capacity.

title: Psychology of future generations
excerpt: Responsibility to the future In the New Psychology of DREVO, man is seen not only as the heir of the past, but also as the creator of the future. Each generation inherits language, culture, knowledge, technology, nature
text: Responsibility to the future In the New Psychology of DREVO, man is seen not only as the heir of the past, but also as the creator of the future. Each generation inherits language, culture, knowledge, technology, nature and social institutions. But each generation also determines what will be passed on next. Therefore, the psychology of future generations studies not only the development of modern man, but also the psychological principles of creating a world in which people of the future can live harmoniously. Future generations begin today Future generations are not yet born. But the conditions for their life are already being created. Every decision a person makes affects the future. Raising children. Development of sciences. Conservation of nature. Creation of new technologies. Culture of communication. Education. All these actions shape the world that will one day become real for new generations. Intergenerational responsibility In DREVO's New Psychology, responsibility extends beyond contemporaries. It includes responsibility to people who have not yet been born. This means striving to: preserve nature; develop education; create knowledge; strengthen peace; develop a culture of cooperation; use technology responsibly; build sustainable social institutions. The future cannot be protected by itself. It is created by today's decisions. Psychological legacy A person passes on not only material values ​​to future generations. He conveys: language; culture; knowledge; scientific discoveries; works of art; moral guidelines; methods of communication; attitude towards nature; attitude to work; ability to cooperate. In many ways, it is this legacy that determines the quality of future society. Education of the future The main goal of education is not only to transmit knowledge. It should develop a person who is capable of thinking independently, learning, collaborating and making responsible decisions. Future generations will require qualities that cannot be completely replaced by technology: critical thinking; creativity; emotional maturity; ability to cooperate; ethical thinking; environmental responsibility; readiness for continuous learning. Technology and the Future Artificial intelligence, biotechnology, robotics and new forms of communication will increasingly influence the life of society. Therefore, future generations must not only master technology. They must understand: why are they used; what opportunities do they open up; what risks do they create; What responsibility do their creators and users bear? The development of technology must be accompanied by human development. Future generations and nature The future cannot be imagined without a healthy natural environment. Clean water. Fertile soil. Diversity of living organisms. Stable climate. All these conditions are not only ecological, but also psychological resources for the future of humanity. Caring for nature becomes caring for the people who will live after us. Cosmic thinking The new psychology of DREVO proposes to expand the time horizon of human thinking. A mature person is able to think not only about today. He considers the consequences of his decisions over years, decades and generations. It is this kind of long-term thinking that becomes the basis for a sustainable civilization. The main principle Each generation receives the world for temporary use. Its task is to pass it on to the next generation more developed, more secure, more just and richer in knowledge than it was received. True development is not measured by how much a person has consumed. It is measured by what he left behind. Definition The Psychology of Future Generations is a section of DREVO's New Psychology that studies the psychological principles of human responsibility to the people of the future, the patterns of transmission of cultural, moral, and intellectual heritage, and the conditions necessary for the sustainable development of civilization. In DREVO's New Psychology, the future generation is viewed as a full-fledged participant in humanity's moral space. Although these people haven't yet been born, today's decisions already influence their quality of life. A person's highest maturity is revealed when he begins to live not only for himself and his generation, but also for those who will one day continue the history of humanity. Examples of positive affirmations, desires and thoughts The practice of internal dialogue in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, words are viewed as a tool for shaping thinking, attention, and behavior. A person constantly conducts an internal dialogue. This dialogue can increase anxiety, fear and helplessness. And it can strengthen confidence, calmness, responsibility and the desire for development. Therefore, it is important to consciously choose thoughts that help you live and develop. Affirmations are not magic spells. They do not change reality by themselves. Their task is to help a person change their own thinking, attitude towards themselves and willingness to act. Health affirmations My body is getting stronger and healthier every day. I take care of my health with respect and love. Every choice I make strengthens my body. My breathing is calm and free. I am filled with energy and vitality. Affirmations of calm I remain calm under any circumstances. I can manage my emotions. My consciousness is clear and focused. I choose conscious reactions over impulsive ones. Every day brings me new experiences and new opportunities. Affirmations of will I keep the promises I make to myself. Every day I become more disciplined. I finish what I start. My actions are consistent with my values. I control my habits, they don't control me. Love affirmations My heart is open to love and goodness. I treat people with respect. I know how to receive and give care. I build relationships based on trust. My presence makes the world a little kinder. Affirmations for Development Every day I learn something new. I reveal my abilities. I calmly learn from my mistakes. My development continues throughout my life. I create the future with my actions today. Affirmations of Purpose I am gradually discovering my purpose. My abilities benefit people. I create projects that make the world a better place. Every day brings me closer to my path. I live in harmony with my values. Examples of desires In the Diary of Desires, it is recommended to write them down in the present tense and in a positive form. I live in a strong and loving family. I am healthy, energetic and full of strength. I speak several languages ​​fluently. I am successfully developing my business. I create projects that help people. I live in a beautiful, cozy house. I am surrounded by honest and reliable friends. I am financially free and manage my resources responsibly. I develop as a person every day. I live in harmony with nature. Thoughts that strengthen personality It is helpful to regularly remind yourself: Any great undertaking begins with the first step. Mistakes are a source of experience if I draw conclusions. Today I can become a little better than yesterday. My attention determines the direction of my life. I am responsible for my decisions. My development is more important than other people's assessments. True strength is found in the ability to control oneself. Everything great is created gradually. The good I do today changes the future. I choose creation over destruction. Morning Affirmations After waking up: Today will be a good day. I meet him calmly and consciously. My body is full of energy. My mind is clear. My heart is open to people. Today I will take at least one step towards my destiny. Evening affirmations Before bed: I am grateful for the day I lived. Today I became a little wiser. My body is recovering. My psyche calms down. Tomorrow I will continue my development. I fall asleep calmly and with trust in life. The main rule The affirmation must comply with the three principles of DREVO. Truthfulness. She must not deny the obvious reality. Instead of: "I don't have any problems." Better: "I am able to gradually solve problems that arise." Creativity. It should help in personal development. Action. A good affirmation inspires real action. After it you want to act. The main principle Thoughts gradually become words. Words become decisions. Decisions become actions. Actions become habits. Habits shape personality. Therefore, a person changes his life not by repeating beautiful phrases, but by allowing these thoughts to gradually change his daily actions. Definition Affirmations are consciously chosen positive statements designed to strengthen constructive thinking, develop inner resilience, and support actions that align with a person's values. In DREVO's New Psychology, affirmations are viewed as a tool for mental self-regulation and the development of internal dialogue. Their purpose is not to replace reality, but to help people see a direction for their development, strengthen motivation, and affirm their values ​​daily through concrete actions. Words become power when they are followed by thoughts. Thoughts become reality when they are followed by actions.

title: Example of a Wish Diary (for shaping reality)
excerpt: Date: ___________________ Time:Before bed (5-15 minutes) 1. Gratitude Today I am grateful for: 2. Today's success What went best today? What did I learn today? 3. My future reality Write down your desires as if they have
text: Date: ___________________ Time:Before bed (5-15 minutes) 1. Gratitude Today I am grateful for: 2. Today's success What went best today? What did I learn today? 3. My future reality Write down your desires as if they have already become a part of your life. Health I am healthy, full of strength and energy. I strengthen my body every day. I easily maintain a healthy lifestyle. Family I live in a friendly, loving and happy family. In my home there is respect, trust and mutual support. We grow together and enjoy life. Finance I am financially free. My work brings in a decent income. I manage money wisely and create new opportunities. Purpose I am doing what I love. My knowledge and abilities help people. Every day I get closer to my destiny. Work and projects I am successfully developing my projects. Reliable partners gather around me. We create useful solutions for society. Personal development I become wiser every day. My will becomes stronger. I learn new things easily. I overcome difficulties calmly. Love My heart is open to love. I know how to love, respect and support people. People around me feel calm and good. Community I am surrounded by honest, kind and talented people. Together we create projects that make the world a better place. Our cooperation is based on trust and respect. Nature I live in harmony with nature. I care about the world around me. Thanks to my actions, there is more life and beauty around. 4. My main image of the future In five years, I see myself as a person who: 5. One step towards tomorrow What one action will bring me closer to this future? 6. Evening Affirmation Today I took another step towards the life I want to live. My consciousness is becoming clearer. My will becomes stronger. My actions are consistent with my values. I fall asleep peacefully, knowing that tomorrow I will continue my development. Seven Rules of the DREVO Wish Diary Write down your wishes in the present tense. Formulate them positively, without the particle “not”. Write down only what is in line with your values. Visualize not only the outcome, but also the person you are becoming. After each wish, identify at least one next step. End your entry with gratitude. Reread your diary once a month and notice real changes in your life. The main principle A wish diary does not create reality on its own. It helps a person to direct attention, thoughts, decisions and actions towards the chosen future on a daily basis. First, an image is born. Then a plan emerges. Then action. It is actions that gradually transform the desired future into a lived reality. The future doesn't begin tomorrow. It begins with a thought written today and an action taken this morning. Definition of maturity Maturity in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, maturity is not viewed as age or as the number of years lived. A person may be mature in age but remain immature in his actions. And vice versa, a young person can exhibit a high degree of maturity. Maturity is not determined by time. It is determined by the level of personality development. This is the ability to consciously manage your life, maintain internal stability and create good for yourself and the world around you. What is maturity? Maturity is a state of harmoniously developed personality, capable of consciously managing oneself, taking responsibility for one's decisions, living in accordance with one's values, and making a creative contribution to the life of society. Maturity is a process. It develops throughout life. Signs of a mature personality Responsibility A mature person stops looking for someone to blame. He asks: What depends on me? And it works. Self-management He knows how to manage: emotions; desires; habits; attention; actions. It is not circumstances that control a person. A person learns to control himself. Mindfulness A mature person understands: your strengths; its limitations; your values; their motives. He is able to look at himself honestly. Developed will He knows how to do the right thing even when it is difficult. Willpower helps to maintain direction in life. Love Maturity is demonstrated by the ability to love without the desire to possess. To love means to respect the freedom, dignity and development of another person. Creation A mature person strives to leave behind something useful. He doesn't just consume. He creates. Transfers knowledge. Helps people. Develops society. Long-term thinking He thinks about more than just today. He takes into account the consequences of his decisions for the future. For the family. For society. For nature. For future generations. Maturity and the Ten Levels of Man In the New Psychology of DREVO, maturity is manifested in the coordinated development of all levels of personality. Body- takes care of health. Subconscious- forms useful habits. Psyche- maintains emotional stability. Consciousness- thinks independently and critically. Will— turns decisions into actions. Soul- lives in harmony with conscience and love. Spirit- remains faithful to its purpose and highest values. Meaning— understands what he lives for. Social connections— builds relationships based on trust and cooperation. Nature- realizes his responsibility to the world around him. Maturity is not perfection at every level, but their harmonious development. What hinders maturity? Personal growth is hindered by: disclaimer; constant blaming of others; life only for pleasure; lack of self-knowledge; fear of change; dependence on other people's opinions; unwillingness to learn; loss of meaning. All these conditions can be overcome through conscious development. Practice of maturity It is useful to ask yourself questions every day: What depended on me today? Which decision was the most mature? What have I learned? Who did you help? What did you create? What kind of person have I become today? Maturity develops through the daily practice of responsibility. The main principle Maturity is not shown when a person knows the answers to all questions. It manifests itself when he is able to honestly seek answers, take responsibility for his decisions and continue to develop. Definition Maturity is a harmonious state of personality in which a person is able to consciously manage themselves, take responsibility for their lives, remain true to their values, build creative relationships, and make a sustainable contribution to the development of society and future generations. In DREVO's New Psychology, maturity is viewed as one of the primary goals of personal development. It encompasses physical health, mental stability, clarity of consciousness, willpower, spiritual development, strengthening of the spirit, social responsibility, and caring for the world. A mature person measures success not only by what he has personally achieved, but also by how much life, freedom, knowledge, love, and opportunity has come from his existence. Personality Development Map Personality Development Map in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology DREVO, personality development is viewed as the gradual growth of a tree. It is impossible for a tree to develop only one branch. If the roots are weak, the whole organism suffers. If there is no light, growth stops. If the crown does not develop, the tree stops bearing fruit. A person develops in the same way. The personality is a single system where all levels are interconnected. The development of one level helps the development of the others. Weakening one level gradually affects the entire system. Ten levels of personal development I. Body The main question: How healthy and vital is my body? Develops through: dream; nutrition; movement; breath; rest; care for health. II. Subconscious The main question: What habits control my life? Develops through: healthy habits; repetition; work with beliefs; affirmations; diary of desires; conscious training of behavior. III. Psyche The main question: Do I know how to understand and regulate my emotions? Develops through: self-observation; meditation; diary of emotions; psychological literacy; communication; emotional maturity. IV. Consciousness The main question: How do I understand the world? Develops through: education; reading; research; critical thinking; reflection; training. V. Will The main question: Am I in control of myself? Develops through: discipline; keeping promises; regular practices; overcoming difficulties; responsibility. VI. Soul The main question: What makes me truly alive? Develops through: Love; creativity; beauty; good deeds; sincerity; revealing talents. VII. Spirit The main question: What do I live for? Develops through: search for purpose; service; loyalty to values; courage; long-term thinking. VIII. Values ​​and Meaning The main question: What really matters? Develops through: introspection; life experience; philosophy; culture; choosing life priorities. IX. Social Connections The main question: What kind of relationships am I creating? Develops through: family; friendship; cooperation; trust; community development; helping people. X. Interaction with nature The main question: How do I interact with the world around me? Develops through: life in harmony with nature; ecological thinking; walks; caring for animals and plants; participation in environmental restoration.

title: Four stages of development
excerpt: 1. Awareness A person begins to understand himself. Notices his strengths and weaknesses. The desire to change appears. 2. Self-management Habits develop. The will is strengthened. Discipline appears. A person becomes th
text: 1. Awareness A person begins to understand himself. Notices his strengths and weaknesses. The desire to change appears. 2. Self-management Habits develop. The will is strengthened. Discipline appears. A person becomes the master of his life. 3. Creation Man begins to create. Projects. Family. Community. Art. Science. Good works. He brings benefit to other people. 4. Legacy The highest stage of development. A person begins to think: What will remain after me? What knowledge will I impart? What world did I help create? The individual begins to work for the sake of future generations. Self-assessment of development Once a month, rate each level on a scale of1 to 10. Level Rating Body ___ Subconscious ___ Psyche ___ Consciousness ___ Will ___ Soul ___ Spirit ___ Values ​​and meaning ___ Social connections ___ Interaction with nature ___ After evaluating, answer: What are the three strongest levels right now? Which two require special attention? What one step will I take this month to develop them? Formula for harmonious development DREVO Develop your body. Train your subconscious. Strengthen your psyche. Expand your consciousness. Train your will. Open your soul. Strengthen your spirit. Live by your values. Build healthy relationships. Take care of nature. The main principle Personality does not develop in a straight line. Sometimes the body grows faster. Sometimes consciousness. Sometimes relationships. The main thing is not to stop. Harmony is achieved not by the equal development of all spheres, but by their constant mutual strengthening. Definition A personal development map is a holistic model of a person that describes the main levels of their development, their interrelationships, and practical paths to personal growth. In New Psychology, DREVO's Personal Development Map serves as a navigator that helps people see their current state, understand their development direction, and consciously strengthen all aspects of their lives. Just as a tree doesn't grow in a single season, a person doesn't mature in a short time. But if you strengthen your roots, trunk, and branches every day, one day the tree will begin to bear fruit that will last for generations. Psychological immunity Psychological Immunity in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, psychological immunity is viewed as the ability of an individual to maintain internal stability, clarity of thought, and fidelity to one's values ​​when faced with difficulties, stress, environmental pressure, and life crises. Just as the immune system protects the body from disease, psychological immunity protects a person from the destructive influence of fear, manipulation, chronic stress, information chaos, and internal crises. Its purpose is not to ensure that a person never experiences pain or anxiety. Its task is to help a person recover, maintain the ability to think, love and act. What is psychological immunity? Psychological immunity is a set of internal qualities, habits, and skills that enable a person to maintain emotional stability, the ability to make informed choices, and constructive behavior in the face of life's challenges. It does not make a person invulnerable. It makes a person more resilient. What does psychological immunity consist of? Healthy body Good sleep. Physical activity. Complete nutrition. Rest. A weakened body is less able to cope with psychological stress. Emotional stability A person knows how to notice his emotions. Doesn't suppress them. Doesn't allow them to fully control themselves. He is able to experience feelings while retaining the ability to think. Clear consciousness A person can: check the facts; think critically; distinguish knowledge from rumors; make decisions independently. Information literacy becomes part of psychological defense. Strong will Willpower helps a person not to succumb to random impulses, fear or pressure from others. It allows you to follow your values ​​even in difficult circumstances. Values ​​and meaning A person who understands why he lives can more easily endure difficulties. Meaning becomes an internal support. Social support Strong relationships with family, friends, and community greatly enhance a person's resilience. Asking for help is not a sign of weakness, but part of mature behavior. What weakens psychological immunity? It is gradually reduced: chronic stress; lack of sleep; constant loneliness; information overload; dependencies; lack of meaning; long-term internal conflicts; life in an atmosphere of fear and violence. Usually it is not just one factor that is at work, but a combination of them. How to strengthen psychological immunity? In New Psychology DREVO recommends: take care of physical health; maintain a sleep schedule; develop emotional literacy; engage in physical activity regularly; limit the destructive flow of information; strengthen the will; develop supportive relationships; spend time in nature; engage in creative activities; regularly analyze your values ​​and life goals. Psychological immunity develops gradually, just like physical endurance. Testing psychological immunity It is useful to ask yourself questions periodically. Do I stay calm in difficult situations? Am I able to make decisions independently? Do I have people I trust? Do I recover from failures? Am I living in accordance with my values? Am I running my life out of constant fear or pressure? The answers help you see areas that need strengthening. Psychological immunity and personality development A person with strong psychological immunity does not become insensitive. He continues to experience emotions. He is mistaken. Worried. But it retains the ability to recover, learn and move on. It is the ability to recover that is one of the main signs of a mature personality. The main principle Psychological strength is not determined by the number of difficulties experienced. It is defined by the ability to transform life experience into wisdom and trials into development. Definition Psychological immunity is the ability of an individual to maintain internal stability, clarity of thought, emotional balance, and fidelity to one's values ​​under the influence of stress, crises, and adverse environmental factors, and to recover from them. In DREVO's New Psychology, psychological immunity is considered one of the most important foundations of psychological health. It is developed through the harmonious development of the body, psyche, consciousness, will, soul, spirit, social connections, and a meaningful lifestyle. Just as a strong tree can withstand strong winds because of its deep roots, a person remains stable not because there are no storms in his life, but because there is a strong support within him. Ecology of information Ecology of Information in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, information is viewed as psychological food. Just as the quality of food affects the health of the body, the quality of information affects the health of the psyche, consciousness and personality. A man becomes not only what he eats. It gradually becomes something that he reads, listens to, watches and discusses on a daily basis. Therefore, conscious selection of information is one of the most important practices of psychological ecology. What is information ecology? Information ecology is a conscious approach to receiving, verifying, storing, distributing and using information with the aim of maintaining psychological health, clarity of thinking and harmonious development of the individual. Information can develop a person. Or it can drain his attention, increase anxiety and distort his perception of reality. Why does information affect the psyche? Every day a person receives thousands of messages. News. Social media. Video. Advertising. Conversations. Books. All of them gradually form: picture of the world; beliefs; habits of thinking; emotional state; decisions taken. Therefore, the quality of the information environment becomes part of psychological health. Sources of information pollution The psyche can be overloaded by: a constant flow of negative news; false information; manipulation; propaganda; information noise; endless social media feed; aggressive content; excessive number of notifications; digital device addiction. The problem often lies not in individual information, but in its constant excess. Principles of Information Ecology Check the information Don't take everything you hear as truth. Compare sources. Check your facts. Separate opinion from evidence. Critical thinking protects consciousness. Limit information noise Not all information is equally useful. It is important to be able to choose. Sometimes the best news is the one you don't need to read. Choose knowledge over sensations Give preference to information that: teaches; helps to understand the world; promotes development; allows you to make more informed decisions. Use technology consciously Technologies should help people. If they start to become a constant distraction, addictive, or interfere with your ability to focus, it's time to reconsider your usage habits. Create an information environment Don't limit yourself to passive consumption. Choose books. Seek mentors. Discuss ideas. Create your own projects. Think about it. Consciousness develops through active work with information.

title: Information and the Ten Levels of Man
excerpt: Information affects all levels of personality. Body- through knowledge about health and the formation of habits. Subconscious- through repeated messages and behavior patterns. Psyche- through the emotional impact of cont
text: Information affects all levels of personality. Body- through knowledge about health and the formation of habits. Subconscious- through repeated messages and behavior patterns. Psyche- through the emotional impact of content. Consciousness- through the formation of worldview and knowledge. Will- through the ability to manage your attention. Soul— through contact with beauty, culture and moral ideals. Spirit— through the choice of life guidelines and meanings. Social connections— through the nature of communication and the quality of public dialogue. Interaction with nature- through understanding one’s place in the surrounding world. Thus, the information environment influences almost the entire personality. Practice of information ecology Every day is useful: read quality books; check important information; limit the flow of random content; set aside time without your phone and social media; develop critical thinking; discuss ideas, not rumors; create your own knowledge and projects; ask a question: Does this information make me wiser or just occupy my attention? The main principle Information becomes part of the personality only when a person allows it to enter his consciousness. Therefore, responsibility for the quality of your inner world begins with responsibility for the quality of the information you consume. Definition Information ecology is a culture of conscious selection, verification, and use of information, aimed at maintaining psychological health, developing critical thinking, and forming a harmonious personality. In DREVO's New Psychology, information ecology is considered one of the key elements of psychological ecology. It helps people protect their consciousness from information pollution, maintain freedom of thought, and focus their attention on knowledge that promotes development, collaboration, and creativity. Just as pure water nourishes a tree, so does quality information nourish the mind. Conversely, if the roots are constantly poisoned, the tree gradually loses its strength. Therefore, a person must be not only a consumer of information but also its attentive gardener. Architecture of a happy life The Architecture of a Happy Life in New Psychology by DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, a happy life is seen not as a random coincidence, but as the result of consciously constructing one's own personality and the world around one. Just as a beautiful house cannot be built without a design, a solid foundation and constant maintenance, a happy life also requires interior architecture. It is created gradually. Every choice. Every habit. With every action. What is the architecture of a happy life? The architecture of a happy life is a holistic system of principles, values, and practices that enables people to harmoniously develop themselves, build healthy relationships, realize their purpose, and create a prosperous future for themselves and others. Happiness does not happen by chance. It is being built. Foundation Any sustainable building starts with a foundation. The foundation of a happy life is made up of: health; safety; honesty; responsibility; respect for oneself and others; internal values. Without a solid foundation, even the greatest achievements become unstable. Load-bearing walls, columns The foundation contains the main supports of life. Body The source of vital energy. Without health it is difficult to realize your potential. Psyche Source of emotional stability. It helps to overcome difficulties and maintain inner balance. Consciousness The source of understanding the world. Consciousness helps us distinguish truth from error and make informed decisions. Will Source of action. She transforms knowledge and desires into real actions. Soul The source of love, conscience, beauty and inner humanity. Spirit The source of life direction. It helps a person remember why he lives. Living spaces A happy life consists of several interconnected areas. Family Source of love, support and trust. Friends and Community A source of collaboration, exchange of experience and joint growth. Labor and creativity A source of self-realization and benefit to society. Nature A source of restoration, inspiration and a sense of oneness with life. Culture and knowledge The source of worldview, wisdom and development. Roof of the house The top part of the architecture of a happy life is purpose. When a person understands: what does he live for; what he wants to leave behind; what benefit can I bring to the world, all other elements of life begin to come together into a single system. Maintaining the home Even the most beautiful house requires constant maintenance. Likewise, a happy life is maintained through daily practices. Taking care of the body. Training. Love. Gratitude. Creative work. Rest. Communication. Development. Happiness cannot be built once and then forgotten. It is supported by every day we live. Signs of a harmonious life A person gradually feels: inner peace; physical energy; clarity of thinking; resilience in the face of difficulties; strong relationships; desire to develop; sense of meaning; the joy of creation; gratitude for life. This does not mean there are no problems. This means there is internal support. Architect of your life In the New Psychology DREVO, each person is seen as the architect of their own life. Circumstances influence the project. But the final appearance of a home depends on many daily decisions. No one can live life for another person. Therefore, the responsibility for its construction belongs to the person himself. The main principle Happiness does not come from outside. It is gradually born within a person and manifests itself in the way he lives, loves, works, builds relationships and cares for the world. The architecture of a happy life is not created by dreams. It is created by actions. Definition The architecture of a happy life is a system for the harmonious development of the individual, based on health, awareness, will, love, purpose, creativity, and responsibility to society and nature. In the New Psychology of DREVO, a happy life is viewed as the result of the coordinated work of all levels of a person and all spheres of their existence. The stronger the inner foundation of a person and the more harmonious their relationship with the outside world, the more stable their sense of happiness becomes. Like a tree that grows thanks to strong roots, a strong trunk and care for each new shoot, a person builds a happy life when he daily strengthens his body, develops his mind, opens his soul, strengthens his spirit and bears fruits that others can enjoy. Karma Karma in the New Psychology of DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, karma is viewed not as a mystical punishment or reward, but as a natural law of cause and effect in a person’s life. Every thought. Every decision. Every action. Every habit. Every word. They gradually change the person himself, his relationships with others and the reality in which he lives. Karma is the process by which a person creates the consequences of his actions. What is karma? Karma is the sum of the consequences of a person's thoughts, decisions, actions, and habits, which gradually shape their personality, relationships, life circumstances, and future. Karma operates primarily through natural psychological, social and biological mechanisms. It does not require a mystical explanation. How is karma formed? Every action leaves a trace. In memory. In habits. In character. In a relationship. In reputation. To health. In society. Gradually, these traces form a person’s life path. The law of cause and effect The New Psychology of DREVO operates on a simple principle: Thoughts shape decisions. Decisions shape actions. Actions form habits. Habits shape character. Character shapes destiny. It is this chain that is the psychological mechanism for the formation of karma. Personal karma Every person creates his own karma every day. When he: speaks the truth; helps people; takes care of health; studies; creates useful projects; keeps promises, he gradually strengthens his own personality. When a person constantly: deceives; destroys relationships; avoids responsibility; lives only for immediate gain; causes harm to oneself or others, the consequences gradually become part of his own life. Collective karma Karma is created not only by an individual person. Family. Community. Organization. State. Civilization. Every shared culture of behavior gradually creates consequences for all participants. When a society develops trust, education, cooperation, and respect for individuals, it creates the conditions for its own prosperity. When violence, corruption and lies prevail, society gradually faces the consequences of these processes. Karma and freedom Karma does not cancel freedom. On the contrary, it makes freedom meaningful. Every new choice has the potential to change the direction of your life. The past influences the present. But it does not completely determine the future. A person is capable of: realize your mistakes; change habits; repair the damage caused, if possible; start creating a new chain of causes and effects. Therefore, karma is not a sentence. It is a process of constant choice.

title: Karma and responsibility
excerpt: In the New Psychology of DREVO, responsibility becomes the main way to change karma. The person stops asking: "Why did this happen to me?" And he begins to ask: "What can I do now?" It is from this moment that life begin
text: In the New Psychology of DREVO, responsibility becomes the main way to change karma. The person stops asking: "Why did this happen to me?" And he begins to ask: "What can I do now?" It is from this moment that life begins to change. Practice of generating favorable karma It is useful to ask yourself questions every day: What consequences do my actions create today? What habits am I strengthening? What will remain after me? Do my actions bring me closer to the person I want to become? What did I do today that made the world a little better? Such questions gradually form responsibility for one’s own life. The main principle Karma is not created by one big action. It is created by thousands of daily decisions. Every choice becomes a new seed. From these seeds the tree of human destiny gradually grows. Definition Karma is the natural process of forming the consequences of a person's thoughts, decisions, actions, and habits, which gradually change their personality, relationships, life circumstances, and future. In DREVO's New Psychology, karma is viewed as a psychological and social law of cause and effect. It manifests itself through the development of character, habits, relationships, and the environment a person creates around themselves. Karma is not an inevitable punishment or reward—it is the result of what a person consistently does every day. The best way to change karma is to change today's actions. The present becomes the point at which a new future is born. The legacy of man The Legacy of Man in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, a person's life is valued not only by what they have received, but also by what they leave behind. True heritage is not just property. Not just money. Not just fame. The most valuable legacy is the change that continues to benefit long after the person is gone. A person becomes part of the future through his heritage. What is heritage? A person's legacy is everything that continues to positively influence people, society, nature and culture through their life, knowledge, actions and creative activity. Heritage is the continuation of personality over time. Forms of heritage Every person is capable of leaving behind different types of legacies. Family Love. Raising children. Transferred values. Family traditions. Good name of the family. Knowledge Books. Scientific discoveries. Experience. Inventions. Educational projects. Teaching. Creation Enterprises. At home. Gardens. Works of art. Technologies. Public organizations. Any work that continues to benefit people. Community Created groups. Traditions of cooperation. Trust between people. Culture of mutual assistance. Strong communities outlive their creators. Nature Planted trees. Restored forests. Clean rivers. Conserved species. Environmental projects. Man can leave behind a more living Earth. Culture Music. Language. Customs. Philosophy. Architecture. Paintings. Movies. Culture becomes a bridge between generations. The legacy begins today Many people believe that inheritance only comes in old age. In fact, it is created daily. Every good deed. Every honest act. Every knowledge transmitted. Every well-mannered child. Every completed project. Every day becomes part of a person's future legacy. Heritage and Purpose Purpose answers the question: "What do I live for?" Heritage responds: "What will remain after me?" When a person connects these two questions, his life takes on long-term meaning. Legacy and Immortality In the New Psychology of DREVO, immortality is understood primarily as the continuation of a person’s influence through his actions. The man continues to live: in your children; in students; in books; in discoveries; in created communities; in planted trees; in culture; in good deeds that inspire others. In this way, the life of an individual becomes part of the life of humanity. Heritage Creation Practices It is helpful to regularly ask yourself: What will remain after me? What knowledge am I passing on? What traditions am I creating? What world will be better because of my life? What have I done today that will be useful in ten, twenty, or a hundred years? These questions help us live not only in the present, but also in the future. Seven Types of DREVO Heritage Every person can leave behind: Biological heritage- children and healthy future generations. Moral heritage- values, life example, culture of relationships. Intellectual heritage— knowledge, books, discoveries, education. Creative legacy— projects, technologies, works of art, organizations. Social heritage— communities, traditions of cooperation, mutual assistance. Environmental heritage— restored nature, preserved ecosystems, care for the planet. Spiritual heritage— ideas, inspiration, life wisdom that help other people become better. The main principle A person's life is measured not only by the years he lives. It is measured by how much life is continued thanks to it. The more goodness, knowledge, love, beauty and opportunities a person leaves behind, the richer his legacy. Definition A person's legacy is the sum of the tangible and intangible results of his or her life that continue to benefit people, society, nature, and future generations after him or her. In the New Psychology of DREVO, creating a legacy is viewed as the highest stage of personal maturity. A person's development reaches its full potential when their knowledge, actions, love, and creative activity take on a life of their own, continuing to shape the world even after their passing. A tree neither eats its own fruit nor rests in its own shade. It grows for the continuation of life. Similarly, a person reaches maturity when they begin to live not only for themselves but also for those who come after them. How to become happy? The Path to Happiness in New Psychology DREVO In the New Psychology of DREVO, happiness is not seen as random luck, a gift of fate, or a constant feeling of joy. Happiness is a way of life. This is the result of harmonious development of the personality. A person becomes happier not when he gets everything he wants. He becomes happier when he realizes his abilities, lives in accordance with his values ​​and makes a difference in life. Happiness is a journey, not a destination. The first step is to know yourself It is impossible to build a happy life without understanding yourself. It is useful to ask questions: Who am I? What is really important to me? What are my strengths? What brings me a feeling of fulfillment? What kind of person do I want to become? Self-knowledge becomes the foundation of a happy life. Take care of your body The body is the basis of all other levels of personality. A good night's sleep. Movement. Healthy eating. Fresh air. Rest. Without taking care of your body, it is difficult to maintain psychological well-being. Develop your consciousness Learn throughout your life. Read. Explore. Ask questions. Develop critical thinking. The more a person understands the world, the freer his choice becomes. Strengthen your will Happiness requires not only desires, but also actions. Keep the promises you make to yourself. Develop discipline. Finish what you started. Every small success strengthens your inner confidence. Open your soul Love. Create. Notice the beauty. Be sincere. Help people. A person becomes happier when he reveals his best qualities. Strengthen your spirit Live for something more than your own comfort. Seek purpose. Follow your values. Think about the future. When life has meaning, even difficulties become part of the journey. Build relationships Happiness rarely exists alone. Love. Friendship. Family. Community. Trust. Support. It is relationships that become one of the main sources of inner well-being. Create Don't limit yourself to consumption. Create. Teach. Build. Write. Be inventive. Plant trees. Help people. Creation gives a sense of the true value of one's own life. Live in harmony with nature Man remains a part of the living world. Nature helps to restore strength. Teaches patience. Reminds us of the natural rhythms of life. Caring for nature simultaneously becomes caring for man himself. Thank you Every day, notice the good that is already present in your life. Gratitude does not cancel out the desire for development. It helps you see the value of the present moment. Accept difficulties A happy life does not mean a life without problems. Difficulties help develop: wisdom; patience; strength of spirit; compassion; experience. It is not the trials themselves that make a person stronger. What makes him stronger is how he goes through them. Live in the moment The future is being built today. Don't put off life until better times. Every day you can: do a good deed; learn something new; improve health; hug a loved one; plant a tree; take a step towards your dream. It is from days like these that a happy life is made. DREVO's Formula for Happiness Happiness is born when a person: takes care of your body; maintains psychological health; develops consciousness; strengthens the will; reveals the soul; strengthens the spirit; lives in accordance with his values; builds healthy relationships; cares about nature; creates a good legacy. When these elements are combined, a person feels inner integrity. The main principle It is impossible to become happy by constantly expecting happiness to come from outside. It is born inside a person and gradually manifests itself in his way of life. Happiness does not appear overnight. It is created by every day we live. Definition Becoming happy means gradually building a life in which the body is healthy, the psyche is stable, the consciousness is free, the will is strong, the soul is open, the spirit has direction, relationships are filled with love, and activities benefit people and the world. In the New Psychology of DREVO, happiness is viewed as a natural result of harmonious personal development. It arises when a person lives daily in accordance with their values, develops their abilities, and participates in creating the future. Happiness isn't a reward for a life well lived. Happiness is a way of living. Every day, a person builds it with their thoughts, their decisions, their actions, and the goodness they leave behind.

title: What will remain after me?
excerpt: The Main Question of a Mature Personality in New Psychology DREVO At a certain point in life, a person begins to ask himself a question that goes far beyond personal success: What will remain after me? This question beco
text: The Main Question of a Mature Personality in New Psychology DREVO At a certain point in life, a person begins to ask himself a question that goes far beyond personal success: What will remain after me? This question becomes one of the signs of maturity. The child thinks about what to get. An adult talks about what to save. A mature person begins to think about what to leave behind. It is with this question that the transition from living for oneself to living for the future begins. Why is this question so important? Every person's life is limited. But the consequences of his actions can last for decades and even centuries. Every person becomes a link between the past and the future. He receives the legacy of previous generations. And creates a legacy for those who follow. Therefore, the main question is not only how long a person lived. And that it will continue to live thanks to him. What's really left? Not everything a person accumulates becomes an inheritance. True legacy is created where life continues through our actions. Remaining: The love we gave. Knowledge shared. People who were inspired. Children who were raised. Students who were helped to open up. Communities that united. Trees that were planted. Projects that continue to work. Culture that has been preserved or created. Goodness that has become a habit for other people. Seven questions to ask yourself It is useful to regularly ask: What kind of person will I be remembered as? What has become better thanks to me? What knowledge have I passed on? Who did I make stronger? What have I created with my own hands or my own mind? What kind of world will remain after my life? Will people's lives be easier because I was here? The answers to these questions gradually determine the direction of your entire life. The legacy begins today Legacy is not created on the last day of life. It is created daily. Every conversation. Every decision. Every book. Every lesson. Every tree. Every idea. Every honest act becomes part of the future. Therefore, the question of legacy is a question of today. The highest form of success In the New Psychology of DREVO, success has several levels. The first is to learn to provide for yourself. The second is to learn to be happy. The third is to help others become happy. The highest form of success is to create a system that continues to benefit people even without the constant involvement of its creator. This is when personal life becomes a legacy. Heritage Practice Once a month, it is helpful to write down the answers to three questions. What new have I created? Who did you help grow? What have I done that will be useful in ten years? This practice gradually changes your outlook on life. A person begins to make decisions not only for today. But also for the sake of future generations. The main principle The greatest legacy is not what a man leaves to his children. His greatest legacy is the world that is made better by his life. Definition The question "What will be left after me?" is a question about personal legacy, the meaning of life, and responsibility to future generations. It helps a person transcend personal interests and begin to build a life whose results continue to be beneficial long after their passing. In the New Psychology of DREVO, this question is considered one of the signs of personal maturity. It guides a person toward creation, service, knowledge sharing, social development, and environmental conservation. When a person stops asking only, "What will I get?" and begins asking, "What will remain after me?", their life takes on a new dimension. At that moment, they cease to be simply a participant in history and begin to become its creator.
